28 August (Fri): 10:30 – 12:30
網上預約：
https://ilccuhk.as.me/schedule.php
更多中文輔導時段。
====================================
C. “The Power of Words” 「書寫力量」
This is a reading and writing event organized by the ILC, Hong Kong Literature Research Centre, the Office of Arts Administrator (OAA) and Tolopoem. Activities we have this semester include Blackboard / Glass Wall Poems, Talks of Dialogue in the Arts and Workshops.
自學中心、香港文學研究中心、藝術行政主任辦公室及吐露詩社合辦的大型閱讀及寫作活動。這個學期的活動，除黑板詩及玻璃詩外，還有藝文縱談及各式工作坊。各項活動的資料可以參看：https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/Event/thepowerofwords.aspx
====================================
【Independent Online Learning Resources】自學中心網上自學資源
A. Independent Online Learning Resources in English
- Academic Writing
Visit this link on academic writing skills and convention for different citation styles:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/Writing_Writing.aspx
- Vocabulary
Visit this link for both General Vocabulary and Specific Vocabulary (e.g. For Business and Medical Professionals) lists and practices:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/Writing_Vocab.aspx
- Job Search and Interviews
Visit this link to identify your capabilities and personality types, learn how to prepare job search documents and personal statements, and how to get ready for job interviews:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/JobSearching.aspx
B. Independent Online Learning Resources in Chinese中文網上自學材料
- Academic Writing論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on academic writing, with highlights on structure, expressions, common grammatical mistakes, etc.
針對大學生撰寫學術論文時所遇到的困難，提供實用的知識和練習。內容包括：學期論文的結構與寫作步驟、常見語法錯誤、表達與語言邏輯等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/AWOnline/general1.html
- ‘Pulewang’ Online Putonghua Platform「普樂網」網上普通話平台
An online Putonghua learning platform designed for CU students. Essential knowledge of Putonghua is introduced with interactive exercises and games. Extended conversational exchanges on selected topics of social affairs and student life are available for oral practice with texts and pinyin.
針對本校同學學習需要的網上普通話平台，內容圍繞大學生的學習與日常生活，設計深入淺出，每單元均有練習與遊戲，互動有趣，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Chinese/plw/index.html
- Argumentative Writing議論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on the structure, the content and the language of argumentative writing.
介紹議論文的結構及寫作要求，以解說、例子及練習，呈現寫作議論時要注意的內容及語言特點：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/arguWriting/001.html
- Cantonese Pronunciation粵語拼音速遞
This guide is designed for mainland students as an effective way to learn Cantonese pronunciation. Basic knowledge of Cantonese syllables is introduced with exercises. Comparison of Cantonese and Putonghua pronunciation is also highlighted
協助內地同學迅速掌握粵語發音。內容包括：語音基礎、粵普對比、難點練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/cantontones/_home/index.html
- Cantonese Express港式粵語速遞
An interactive introduction to Hong Kong style Cantonese. Daily expressions and situational conversations are introduced with interactive exercises.
以有趣互動的方式介紹港式粵語，包括日常生活用語、情景會話、互動練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/canton_express/others/frontpage.html
- Online Cantonese for Foreigners
A free online platform for international students to learn basic Cantonese. The texts are clear and simple, and interactive exercises easy to use: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/can_eng/layout.html
- Online Putonghua for Foreigners
Do you know how to make orders in a Chinese restaurant and learn how to bargain when you travel in China? Here are some situational conversations and basic knowledge of Putonghua to learn online: https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/CHResources/Lang_PTH_EnglishSpk.aspx
- Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) 中國語言及文化自學資源網
Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) is a biliterate (English and Chinese) online platform that contains reviews of learning materials suitable for autodidactic study in the 5 big areas of Mandarin, Cantonese, Chinese Characters, Chinese Culture, and Hong Kong Culture. Electronic learning materials that is good for self-learning would be review. Each review consists of a description and other useful information. Users can search for resources by various criteria, rate the resources, and write their own comments. A self-assessment system is also provided so as to recommend an entry point to the users according to their current level.
中國語言及文化自學資源網(OPSCL)為一推薦自學資源之網上平台。平台為有意學習普通話、粵語、漢字、中國文化或香港文化等五大範疇的人士提供中文及英文雙語之學習資源，以推動自主學習與終身學習。平台內推薦的資源均附有簡介及評語，使用者可按自身需要搜尋學習資源，並在使用後給予評分或評論，以備其他使用者參考。此外，平台設有「自評系統」，使用者可通過完成自評，確定自身的學習起步點，從而尋找適合自己程度的學習資源。

自學中心八月二十四日至八月二十八日舉辦 (1) 「射者正己而後發」——射藝與修身 (粵), (2) JRE 議論文寫作 (II), (3) 學術寫作：引用與文獻目錄 (普), (4) 「信而好古」——粵語與中國古代文化 (粵), 及 (5) 自學粵語 (三)等工作坊，歡迎報名。

自學中心、香港文學研究中心、藝術行政主任辦公室及吐露詩社合辦的大型閱讀及寫作活動。這個學期的活動，除黑板詩及玻璃詩外，還有藝文縱談及各式工作坊。各項活動的資料可以參看：https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/Event/thepowerofwords.aspx

A. Independent Online Learning Resources in English
- Academic Writing
Visit this link on academic writing skills and convention for different citation styles:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/Writing_Writing.aspx
- Vocabulary

https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/Writing_Vocab.aspx
- Job Search and Interviews
Visit this link to identify your capabilities and personality types, learn how to prepare job search documents and personal statements, and how to get ready for job interviews:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/JobSearching.aspx
B. Independent Online Learning Resources in Chinese中文網上自學材料
- Academic Writing論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on academic writing, with highlights on structure, expressions, common grammatical mistakes, etc.
針對大學生撰寫學術論文時所遇到的困難，提供實用的知識和練習。內容包括：學期論文的結構與寫作步驟、常見語法錯誤、表達與語言邏輯等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/AWOnline/general1.html
- ‘Pulewang’ Online Putonghua Platform「普樂網」網上普通話平台
An online Putonghua learning platform designed for CU students. Essential knowledge of Putonghua is introduced with interactive exercises and games. Extended conversational exchanges on selected topics of social affairs and student life are available for oral practice with texts and pinyin.
針對本校同學學習需要的網上普通話平台，內容圍繞大學生的學習與日常生活，設計深入淺出，每單元均有練習與遊戲，互動有趣，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Chinese/plw/index.html

介紹議論文的結構及寫作要求，以解說、例子及練習，呈現寫作議論時要注意的內容及語言特點：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/arguWriting/001.html

This guide is designed for mainland students as an effective way to learn Cantonese pronunciation. Basic knowledge of Cantonese syllables is introduced with exercises. Comparison of Cantonese and Putonghua pronunciation is also highlighted
協助內地同學迅速掌握粵語發音。內容包括：語音基礎、粵普對比、難點練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/cantontones/_home/index.html
- Cantonese Express港式粵語速遞
An interactive introduction to Hong Kong style Cantonese. Daily expressions and situational conversations are introduced with interactive exercises.
以有趣互動的方式介紹港式粵語，包括日常生活用語、情景會話、互動練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/canton_express/others/frontpage.html
- Online Cantonese for Foreigners
A free online platform for international students to learn basic Cantonese. The texts are clear and simple, and interactive exercises easy to use: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/can_eng/layout.html
- Online Putonghua for Foreigners
Do you know how to make orders in a Chinese restaurant and learn how to bargain when you travel in China? Here are some situational conversations and basic knowledge of Putonghua to learn online: https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/CHResources/Lang_PTH_EnglishSpk.aspx
- Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) 中國語言及文化自學資源網
Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) is a biliterate (English and Chinese) online platform that contains reviews of learning materials suitable for autodidactic study in the 5 big areas of Mandarin, Cantonese, Chinese Characters, Chinese Culture, and Hong Kong Culture. Electronic learning materials that is good for self-learning would be review. Each review consists of a description and other useful information. Users can search for resources by various criteria, rate the resources, and write their own comments. A self-assessment system is also provided so as to recommend an entry point to the users according to their current level.

title: [HK$300] Brain Health Study [HK$300] 中大醫學院邀您參與腦部健康研究
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/08/21
»
Announcements
[HK$300] Brain Health Study  [HK$300] 中大醫學院邀您參與腦部健康研究 - CUHK Psychiatry Sleep Assessment Unit
From: Wong Yuen Tung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
yuentungwong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
便秘？嗅覺變差？睡覺拳打腳踢？有腦退化家族史？
這些看似平常的小毛病，其實可能是柏金遜症等大腦退化的早期先兆！
提早了解大腦健康，預防神經退化！
中大醫學院睡眠研究小組推出全新手機篩查App，誠邀您參與醫學研究！
研究對象：
年齡介乎
50 至 65 歲
的華人
未確診
任何腦神經退化疾病（如柏金遜症、阿爾茲海默症/失智症等）
參加者需完成以下程序：
參與研究
費用全免
，成功完成相關研究程序者最多可獲
HK$300元超市禮券
作為津貼
階段一：
下載手機程式並完成問卷 （約需 15–20 分鐘）
完成後可獲得早期柏金遜病風險分數
符合資格並完成問卷者可獲 HK$100元超市禮券
階段二：
部分參加者將獲邀進一步參與臨床評估
包括身體檢查、臨床訪談、居家睡眠測試及神經認知測試
符合資格並完成階段二者，可額外獲 HK$200元超市禮券
立刻掃描海報右下方
二維碼 (QR Code)
或
點擊連結
下載程式「柏健通」參與研究
IOS用戶：
https://apps.apple.com/hk/app/%E6%9F%8F%E5%81%A5%E9%80%9A/id1626241589
Android用戶：
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=edu.cuhk.parkinapp.v2
查詢（致電或WhatsApp）：3919 7792 / 5282 5786（研究助理 黃小姐）
Constipated？Weakened sense of smell？Acting out dream during sleep (punching and kicking) ？Having a family history of neurodegenerative disease？
Common issues like these can actually be early warning signs of brain degeneration, including neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson’s disease.
Understand your brain health early to prevent neurodegeneration.
Sleep Assessment Unit - Psychiatry, CUHK has launched a brand-new screening App, and we sincerely invite you to join our medical research study.
Target participants：
Chinese aged between 50 to 65 years old
Have NOT been diagnosed
with any neurodegenerative disease (e.g. Parkinson’s disease, Alzheimer’s disease/ Dementia, etc.)
What you will need to do:
Participation is completely free. Those who successfully complete the study procedure can receive up to HK$300 in supermarket voucher as an allowance.
Phase 1:
Download the mobile app "柏健通" and complete the questionnaires (take approximately 15-20 minutes)
An early Parkinson’s disease risk score will be provided upon completion
Eligible participants who complete the questionnaires will receive HK$100 supermarket voucher
Phase 2:
Selected participants will be invited to undergo further clinical assessments
Assessments include physical examination, clinical interviews, sleep studies, and neurocognitive assessments
Eligible participants who complete Phase 2 will receive an additional HK$200 supermarket voucher
Interested parties are welcome to participate by
clicking the links below
or
scanning the QR Code
in the poster to download the "柏健通" mobile application:
IOS users:
https://apps.apple.com/hk/app/%E6%9F%8F%E5%81%A5%E9%80%9A/id1626241589
Android users:
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=edu.cuhk.parkinapp.v2
For details and registration enquiries, please contact our hotline: 39197792 or 5282 5786 (WhatsApp) (Research Assistant, Ms Wong)
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

title: Are you the next CUHK Outstanding Student? Apply now for 2026!! 香港中文大學傑出學生獎2026－現正接受報名!!
bodyText:

Are you the next CUHK Outstanding Student? Apply now for 2026!! 香港中文大學傑出學生獎2026－現正接受報名!! - Office of Student Affairs
From: Office of Student Affairs
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
osa@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
你是否曾在藝術、創新、體育或社會服務方面發揮所長，創造影響力？歡迎申請 2026 傑出學生獎，與大家分享你的成就和故事！
除了追求學術成就外，香港中文大學(中大)學生亦積極在非學術範疇發揮所長。為表揚在不同領域有傑出表現，並持續為大學社群及社會作出積極貢獻的學生，中大設立「傑出學生獎」，以肯定其成就與貢獻，並鼓勵同學追求卓越、勇於突破自我。
【獎項類別】
1. 藝術
2. 創新與發明
3. 社會服務
4. 體育
5. 特別表現
【申請資格】
在2025–26學年就讀於香港中文大學的全日制本科生或研究生，如於有關學年在上述其中一個範疇取得卓越成就或作出重大貢獻，均符合申請資格。
【截止日期】
2026年9月18日（星期五）中午12時正。
歡迎以個人或團隊形式申請。
【詳情及報名】
https://www.osa.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/osa-application-guideline/
【查詢】
潘小姐(電話：3943 7210；電郵： gladys@cuhk.edu.hk )或
陳小姐(電話：3943 1843；電郵： kimichan@cuhk.edu.hk )。
誠邀你把握機會展示卓越成就，分享成長歷程，並以自身經驗啟發同儕。
我們期待收到你的報名！
Are you the next CUHK Outstanding Student? Apply now for 2026!
Have you made a mark in the arts, innovation, sports, or social service this year? It’s time to be recognized for your passion and achievements!
The CUHK Outstanding Students Awards 2026 aim to celebrate students who have demonstrated outstanding achievements and made a positive impact on the University community and society through their dedication, talent, and perseverance.
【Award Categories】
• Arts
• Innovation and Invention
• Social Service
• Sports
• Special Achievement
【Eligibility】
Full-time undergraduate and postgraduate students enrolled at CUHK during the 2025–26 academic year who have demonstrated outstanding achievements or made significant contributions in one of the above categories within the same academic year are eligible to apply.
【Application Deadline】
18 September 2026 (Friday), 12:00 noon.
(Applications are welcome from both individuals and teams.)
【Details & Application】
https://www.osa.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/osa-application-guideline/
【Enquiries】
Ms. Gladys Poon (Tel: 3943 7210 | Email: gladys@cuhk.edu.hk)
Ms. Kimi Chan (Tel: 3943 1843 | Email: kimichan@cuhk.edu.hk)
We cordially invite you to seize this opportunity to present your remarkable achievements, share your journey, and inspire your peers with your experience.
We look forward to receiving your application!
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

中大月餅．愛心傳承
中秋佳節將至，您計劃如何度過這個團圓時刻？不妨與摯愛一同共賞月色、共享溫馨時光，同時也為社會盡一份心意。今年，香港中文大學（中大）特別呈獻一份貼心選擇——「
中大愛心月餅
」。
中大今年再次推出「
中大愛心月餅
」，由社會企業明愛天糧*製作。月餅禮盒以中大重要地標——科學館為主題，在皎潔明月的映襯下，展現中大校園恬靜閒適的醉人景致。
「中大愛心月餅」為一盒四個低糖雙黃白蓮蓉月餅，每盒糖份只有10.8克，
售價HK$300
。每售出一盒，中大．關懷義工隊就會為沙田、大埔及馬鞍山的獨居長者送上一個「中大愛心月餅」，而收益亦撥捐至「香港中文大學教育基金」，支持大學推動創新教育與體驗式學習項目，旨在優化學生學習體驗，並進一步豐富校園生活，推動全人發展。
當閣下與親友品嚐「
中大愛心月餅
」共賀佳節之時，不但是支持香港社會企業及中大學生，也是分享助人為樂之精神。今年同樣提供速遞送貨服務，數量有限，請即訂購！
*
明愛天糧為社會企業，透過經營烘焙業務，為精神復元人士及其他殘疾人士提供就業及職前訓練機會，協助融入社區生活。

CUHK Mooncake - Sharing Happiness and Reaching Everyone
Mid-Autumn Festival is just around the corner. How do you plan to spend this joyful time with your loved ones? You can enjoy the beautiful moonlight with the people closest to you, share wonderful moments together, and at the same time extend a helping hand to society. This year, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) is bringing you a special choice that can fulfill all these wishes – the
CUHK Mooncakes
.
CUHK has joined hands again with the social enterprise Caritas La Vie* to launch “
CUHK Mooncake
“. The mooncake gift box features the Science Centre, an iconic CUHK landmark, showcasing the tranquil scenery of the CUHK campus under the glow of a bright full moon.
The CUHK Mooncakes come in a box of 4 low-sugar dual-yolk white lotus paste mooncakes, with only 10.8g of sugar per box,
priced at HK$300
. For each box sold, the CUHK • Care Service Team will deliver a free mooncake to the elderly living alone in Shatin, Tai Po and Ma On Shan. Proceeds from the sales will be donated to the “CUHK Education Fund” which provides support to develop education and experiential learning initiatives that aim at enhancing study experience and enriching campus life.
By enjoying “
CUHK Mooncakes
” with your family and friends, you not only support local enterprises and CUHK students but also share the spirit of giving to the community. The CUHK Mooncakes are limited in stock, so please order now!
* Caritas La Vie is a social enterprise that provides job opportunities for the recovering mentally-disabled and self-reliance of people with disabilities through its baking workshop.

title: 【$200 Coupon】Recruiting Children (aged 4 or under) for the Gut Microbiome and At-risk Children's Brain Development Study 誠意邀請5歲以下兒童參加腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/08/21
»
Announcements
【$200 Coupon】Recruiting Children (aged 4 or under) for the Gut Microbiome and At-risk Children's Brain Development Study 誠意邀請5歲以下兒童參加腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Dr. WONG Wing Ho, Oscar
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
hatch@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
家長您好，我們是香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系的研究團隊。本研究由香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系、內科及藥物治療學系統籌。
本研究團隊誠邀5歲以下兒童參與一項有關腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究。此研究希望透過收集小朋友之大便及口腔樣本，幫助了解腸道微生態與大腦發展的關係。
研究對象:
1) 確診/懷疑小朋友有自閉症傾向或其他發展問題
2) 4歲或以下的小朋友 (交齊問卷和樣本的日子未滿5歲即可)
3) 父母皆為華裔或亞裔人士
4) 小朋友18歲以下的兄弟姊妹
以下為是次研究需要完成的事項：
1) 簽署參加同意書
2) 網上問卷調查：網上問卷主要詢問小朋友的行為及腸道情況，填寫時間約45分鐘
3) 收集大便和口腔樣本：我們會給家長一個樣本收集包，請家長使用收集包內的物在家中資協助收集樣本
4) 飲食習慣的問卷：記錄小朋友的飲食習慣
完成研究後，參加者可以獲得$200的超市現金券、 G-NiiB益生菌試用裝和腸道健康報告作為答謝 另外，家長有機會被邀請進行面談並隨訪2年,如有需要我們會提供轉介信。是次研究是自願參與性質參與，這個研究期間所取得的資料都會被嚴格保密。
如家長有意願參與此項研究，請填寫以下網上篩選問卷(https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o)。收到問卷回覆後，我們會再與合適參加是次研究的小朋友之家長連絡。
如果家長對研究細節有任何疑問，歡迎透過WhatsApp 6099-3064或致電 2607-6057與我們聯絡。
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Parents,
We are a team of researchers from the Department of Psychiatry at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. We are conducting a research project jointly organised by the Department of Psychiatry, the Department of Medicine and Therapeutics of the Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Our team sincerely invites your children to participate in research on gut microbiome and children's brain development. Through collecting stool and buccal samples, we aim to investigate the relationship between gut microbiome and brain development.
A gut health report will be provided, A G-Niib probiotics trial pack and a $200 supermarket voucher will be awarded to participants.
Target participants:
1) The child is diagnosed/suspected to have autism or other developmental problems
2) The child is 4 years old or under (all questionnaires and samples are submitted before 5 years old)
3) Both parents are Chinese or Asian
4) Children’s brothers and sisters under 18 years old are also welcome to join
Procedures and details of this Study:
1) Research Consent
2) Online Questionnaire : A 45-minute questionnaire on children’s behaviors and their physical health condition
3) Stool and Buccal Sample Collection: Samples collection kit will be provided for sample collection at home
4) Dietary Questionnaire: Recording children's eating habits
You will receive a $200 supermarket voucher after completing all the research procedures. Participation is voluntary, and your responses will be kept confidential. The information you provide will be used solely for research purposes.
If you are interested in participating in our research study, please fill out the following online questionnaire (https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o). We will contact you afterwards if your children are suitable to join this study.
For inquiries, please contact 2607-6057 or WhatsApp 6099-3064.

From: MSSc in Global Political Economy, on behalf of Prof. Karim Bettache and LIN, Yu Hong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mgpeinfo@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
From: Research Team, School of Governance and Policy Science, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to WeChat: 13809899482 / WhatsApp: 69409544 / 1155220689@link.cuhk.edu.hk
**This study is supervised by Prof. Karim Bettache (email: karimbettache@cuhk.edu.hk)**
Dear Potential Participants,
We are a research team from the School of Governance and Policy Science at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. This study is funded by the Research Grants Council (RGC) and led by a leading scholar in political psychology. The findings are expected to be published in top-tier international journals.
We sincerely invite South Asian permanent residents of Hong Kong (e.g., Indian, Pakistani, Nepalese, Bangladeshi, Sri Lankan, etc.) to participate in a focus group interview on the long-term psychological impact of colonialism on post-colonial societies.
Target participants:
South Asian ethnicity (e.g., Indian, Pakistani, Nepalese, Bangladeshi, Sri Lankan, etc.)
Holders of Hong Kong Permanent Resident status
Able to communicate in Mandarin, Cantonese, or English
Procedures and details of this study:
Research Consent
Focus Group Interview: A group discussion led by professional researchers, lasting approximately 1.5 hours
Flexible Location: In-person at CUHK campus or online participation available
A $100 HKD token of appreciation will be provided upon completion. All personal information and discussion content will be kept strictly confidential and used for academic research purposes only.
Participation is voluntary, and your responses will be kept confidential.
If you are interested in participating, please contact us via:
WeChat: 13809899482
WhatsApp: 69409544
Email: 1155220689@link.cuhk.edu.hk
We will contact you afterwards to arrange further details.
For inquiries, please feel free to reach out through the above channels.
**本研究由Prof. Karim Bettache監督（電郵：karimbettache@cuhk.edu.hk)**
您好，我們是香港中文大學政務與政策科學學院的研究團隊。本研究由香港研究資助局（RGC）資助，PI為政治心理學領域泰斗級學者，最終成果擬發表於國際頂級期刊。
本研究團隊誠邀南亞裔香港永久居民參與一項焦點小組訪談，旨在探討殖民主義對前殖民地社會心理的長期影響。
研究對象：
南亞裔人士（如印度、巴基斯坦、尼泊爾、孟加拉、斯里蘭卡等裔）
持有香港永久居民身份
能以普通話 / 廣東話 / 英文進行溝通
以下為是次研究需要完成的事項：
簽署參加同意書
參與焦點小組訪談：在專業研究人員帶領下進行小組討論，時長約1.5小時
地點靈活：可選擇香港中文大學校內面談，或透過線上平台參與
完成研究後，參加者可獲得$100港幣酬謝。訪談內容將全程嚴格保密，所有個人信息及對話內容僅用於學術研究用途。
本研究屬自願參與性質，期間所取得的資料都會被嚴格保密。
如有意參與此項研究，歡迎透過以下方式聯絡我們：
微信：13809899482
WhatsApp：69409544
Email: 1155220689@link.cuhk.edu.hk
收到聯絡後，我們會再與合適參加者溝通後續安排。
如果對研究細節有任何疑問，歡迎透過上述方式與我們聯絡。

From: Mary Ip
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【研究招募｜工作坊參加者：青少年（18–24歲）及兒童／青少年照顧者】
「由出生到就業（Birth to Work）」是一項以香港為背景的研究及行動項目，旨在了解兒童、青少年及年輕人由成長到初入職場期間的精神健康歷程，並推動香港青年精神健康生態系統的長遠改善。
我們現正招募：
18–24歲青年（有精神健康挑戰或心理困擾經歷）
兒童及青少年照顧者（照顧有精神健康挑戰或心理困擾經歷的兒童／青少年）
而兒童及青少年有以下身份或經歷:
多元族裔及文化背景
難民/尋求庇護
性/別小眾(LGBTQ+)
受障者/殘障者/殘疾人士
聾人
參加者將獲邀出席一節約 2 小時的線下工作坊，與其他參加者一同分享經歷、討論支援需要，並共同建立「旅程地圖（Journey Mapping）」，整理影響精神健康的重要經歷、支援及改善方向。
完成工作坊可獲港幣 600 元答謝金
報名截止：2026年8月31日（香港時間晚上11:59）
報名表：
https://esurvey.psy.cuhk.edu.hk/jfe/form/SV_5jccwg74G5mKlXU
查詢：birth2work@cuhk.edu.hk

【Research Recruitment｜Workshop Participants: Youth (Aged 18–24) and Caregivers of Children and Youth】
Birth to Work is a Hong Kong-based research and action project exploring the mental health journeys of children, adolescents, and young adults, with the goal of informing long-term improvements to youth mental health systems in Hong Kong.
We are recruiting:
Youth aged 18–24 with lived experience of mental health challenges or psychological distress
Caregivers of children or young people who have experienced mental health challenges or psychological distress
Of which, children or young people have the following identities or lived experiences:
ethnically and culturally diverse; or
refugee/asylum seekers; or
sexual and gender minority; or
with disabilities; or
Deaf
Participants will be invited to join a 2-hour in-person workshop to share experiences, discuss support needs, and co-create a journey map that identifies key experiences, support systems, barriers, and opportunities for improvement.
HKD 600 incentive upon completion
Application deadline: 31 August 2026 (11:59 PM HKT)

Announcements
[$200 travel allowance] Recruiting aged 65 or above, and their caregivers to participate in a research interview assessing perceptions of health-related quality of life among older adults.  [$200交通津貼] 誠邀65歲或以上及其照顧者參與研究訪談，以了解長者對健康相關生活質素的看法和感受 - JC School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: Amy Wong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
amy.wong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
***
中文版本
***
研究背景
香港中文大學現正進行一項有關長者身心健康的研究訪談，從而制定一個可以測量長者健康生活品質的工具。
招募對象
長者：65歲或以上，照顧者：18歲或以上；
香港居民；
能閱讀中文及以廣東話溝通； 及
曾使用長者服務設施或入住護理之家
參與方式
如果符合上述條件，請在下方連結登記及留下相關資料以作跟進，需時約1-3分鐘。完成登記後，研究人員將於兩星期內與你聯絡，並安排你與被照顧的長者以面對面形式完成訪問。
答謝安排
個人訪問約需時 30-45 分鐘。完成訪問後，長者與照顧者合共可獲港幣 200 元現金以作答謝。每位參加者只限參加一次。
報名登記連結
:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_00u21fpHbgdjKuO
查詢
本研究已獲香港中文大學 —
調查及行為研究操守委員會
的審批。 (參考編號: SBRE-25-0737) 。如有任何查詢，歡迎聯絡主研究員 黃麗儀教授 (電郵:
lywong@cuhk.edu.hk
) 或研究員黃小姐 (Amy) / 張小姐 (Annie) (電話: 2252-8408 / 2252-8404) 。
名額有限！先到先得！
歡迎轉發此訊息給您的家人及朋友！
***
English version
***
S
tudy Background
The JC School of Public Health and Primary Care at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently conducting an interview on the physical and mental health of older adults in Hong Kong to develop a tool in measuring their health-related quality of life in Hong Kong.
Target Group
Elderly: Aged 65 or above; Caregiver: 18 years old or above;
Hong Kong residents;
Able to read Chinese and communicate in Cantonese; and
Has ever used elderly service facilities or nursing homes.
How to Participate
If you meet the above criteria, please complete the registration form in around 1-3 minutes. After registration, our staff will contact you within two weeks and arrange an in-person interview for you and the elderly participant to complete.
Appreciation
The individual interview takes about 30-45 minutes. Upon completion, you and the elderly participant will receive a total of HK$200 cash as a token of appreciation. Each participant may only participate once.
Registration L
ink:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_00u21fpHbgdjKuO
Contact Us
This study has been approved by the Survey and Behavioural Research Ethics Committee (Ref: SBRE-25-0737). Should you have any enquiries, please contact the Principal Investigator Prof. Eliza Wong (E-mail: lywong@cuhk.edu.hk), or researchers Ms. Amy Wong or Ms. Annie Cheung (Tel: 2252-8408 / 2252-8404).
Limited quotas only! First come, first served!
Feel free to share this invitation with your family and friends!

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

From: Andy Cheng

andycheng@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Are you ready to explore the future of mental health care?
【 Nursing and Healthcare Innovation & Insights Dialogue Series | Webinar #1 】
Theme: Rethinking Psychological Interventions and Care: Innovative and Emerging Pathways in Mental Health
Date: 10 Sep (Thu)
Time: 10:00 AM – 12:00 PM (Hong Kong / Mainland China / Singapore, GMT+8)
Equivalent times: 9:00 AM – 11:00 AM (Thailand, Vietnam, and Jakarta); 7:30 AM – 9:30 AM (India); 3:00 AM – 5:00 AM (London (UK)); 4:00 AM – 6:00 AM (Paris/Berlin); 12:00 PM – 2:00 PM (Sydney); and 10:00 PM – 12:00 AM (previous day) (New York (USA)).
Format: Zoom Webinar
Language: English (English live captions will be available for all participants during the webinar)
Registration: https://cuhk.zoom.us/webinar/register/WN_xFAJtPa0QCCmU1zBOGXirA
Registration Deadline: 3 Sep (Thu)
Access: A Zoom access link will be provided upon registration.
Join us for the upcoming edition of the Healthcare and Nursing Innovation & Insights Dialogue Series Webinar, featuring an engaging intellectual exchange among distinguished global scholars on the future of mental health care.
From evolving diagnostic frameworks and personalized approaches to care, to the growing role of artificial intelligence in mental health interventions, this webinar will explore emerging directions that are reshaping psychological care and practice worldwide.
Meet our four esteemed speakers:
Prof. Kenneth Fung (Professor & Director of Global Mental Health, Department of Psychiatry, University of Toronto)
Topic: The Future of the DSM and Global Mental Health
Prof. Baljinder K. Sahdra (Professor, Institute for Positive Psychology and Education, Australian Catholic University & Editor-in-Chief, Journal of Contextual Behavioral Science)
Topic: Personalized and Idiographic Approaches: Moving Beyond the Average and Tracking Individual Processes of Change
Prof.
Wai Tong Chien
(Professor & Director, The Nethersole School of Nursing, The Chinese University of Hong Kong); and
Prof.
Connie Chong
(Associate Professor, The Nethersole School of Nursing, The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
Co-presenting: AI Mental Health Interventions: Current Approaches and Challenges
This webinar is ideal for healthcare professionals, researchers, educators, students, and anyone interested in the future of mental health care.

實驗內容
：
① 正式實驗開始前需先完成1 次記憶認知能力實驗，時長為 1 小時；
正式實驗：
② 第1天：1 次磁力共振(MRI)掃描實驗，需在掃描過程中完成行為任務，時長為 3 小時；③ 第2到7天：每天1次語言訓練或測試實驗，每次時長為 2.5-3 小時。
實驗地點：
①磁力共振掃描實驗在威爾斯親王醫院（新界沙田銀城街30-32號）進行；②認知及其他行為實驗在香港中文大學梁銶琚樓G/F進行
八次實驗結束後，會支付
1800
港元被試費用。
以下情況
不應進行磁力共振成像（
MRI
）掃描
：
體內有任何金屬植入物，例如：
1) 無法取下的穿孔飾品; 2) 固定式牙套（永久性保持器）; 3) 人工耳蝸植入物; 4) 心臟起搏器; 5) 動脈瘤夾或其他經手術植入的金屬; 6) 人工關節; 7) 骨折後遺留的金屬螺釘或鋼板.
此外，若符合以下任一情況，亦不適合接受
MRI 掃描：
1) 已懷孕，或正在嘗試懷孕; 2) 曾從事金屬相關工作（如焊接），或眼睛中可能存在金屬碎屑; 3) 有幽閉恐懼症，或害怕長時間待在狹小空間內（例如 MRI 掃描儀中）.
另外，掃描過程中會產生較大的噪音，可能引起耳部不適或疼痛。
參與者還應符合以下要求：
1. 年齡18-30歲，非心理學/語言學專業。
2. 母語為廣東話；
3. 聽力、視力或矯正視力正常；
4. 無腦損傷、癲癇等神經類疾病，無頭皮外傷或感染；
5. 右利手；
6. 實驗時間身體健康，無感冒發燒咳嗽等狀況；
7. 實驗前要保證充足的睡眠，精力充沛認真負責完成實驗；
8. 實驗前24小時未服用大量茶、咖啡等飲料；實驗前不要有劇烈的體育活動；
9. 實驗前兩週不能染髮；
10. 實驗當天需要洗頭，不能化妝，額頭不要塗防曬霜、隔離霜等。
如有任何問題，請聯繫：zhenjiangcui@link.cuhk.edu.hk
報名連結：
http://137.189.158.12/limesurvey/index.php?r=survey/index&sid=116925&lang=en
Experiment Duration
:
September to November 2026 (until all places are filled). The main experiment requires participation on 7 consecutive days, with approximately 2.5–3 hours per day, totaling around 18–19 hours.
Experiment Details
:
One memory and cognitive ability assessment (1 hour) before formal experiment;
Day 1: One magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) session, during which participants will complete behavioral tasks (3 hours);
Days 2–7: One language training or testing session per day, each lasting approximately 2.5 hours.
Experiment Locations
: 1. The MRI experiment will be conducted at the Prince of Wales Hospital (30-32 Ngan Shing Street, Sha Tin, New Territories); 2. the cognitive and other behavioral experiments will be conducted on the ground floor (G/F) of the LKK Building, CUHK.
After completing all eight sessions, participants will receive a reimbursement of HKD$1800.
MRI scanning should not be performed under the following conditions:
Presence of any metal implants in the body, such as:
Non-removable piercings;
Fixed orthodontic appliances (permanent retainers);
Cochlear implants;
Cardiac pacemakers;
Aneurysm clips or other surgically implanted metal;
Artificial joints;
Metal screws or plates remaining from previous bone fractures.
In addition, individuals who meet any of the following criteria are also not suitable for MRI scanning:
Currently pregnant or attempting to become pregnant;
Have worked in metal-related occupations (e.g., welding) or may have metal fragments in the eyes;
Have claustrophobia or are afraid of staying in confined spaces for extended periods (e.g., inside an MRI scanner).
Furthermore, the scanning process generates loud noise, which may cause ear discomfort or pain.
Other Eligibility Requirements
:
Aged 18–30; not majoring in psychology or linguistics.
Cantonese native speaker.
Normal hearing and vision, or corrected-to-normal vision.
No history of brain injury, epilepsy, or other neurological conditions; no scalp injuries or infections.
Right-handed (i.e., habitually writes or uses chopsticks with the right hand).
In good health on the day of the experiment (no cold, fever, cough, etc.).
Well-rested before the experiment, and able to complete the task attentively and responsibly.
No consumption of large amounts of tea, coffee, or similar drinks within 24 hours prior; no intense physical activity before the experiment.
No hair dyeing within two weeks before the experiment.
Please wash your hair and do not wear makeup or apply sunscreen/ primer/foundation on the forehead on the day of the experiment.
For inquiries, please contact:
zhenjiangcui@link.cuhk.edu.hk
Registration link:
http://137.189.158.12/limesurvey/index.php?r=survey/index&sid=116925&lang=en
View Count

title: Free HPV Screening for Men in Specific Groups [Free!!!] !!!注意: 男性特定群組 HPV 病毒篩查 [費用全免] [$400交通津貼]
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/08/21
»
Announcements
Free HPV Screening for Men in Specific Groups [Free!!!] !!!注意: 男性特定群組 HPV 病毒篩查   [費用全免] [$400交通津貼] - Department of Surgery
From: Tim Lau
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學泌尿外科研究招募
:
香港中文大學泌尿外科現正進行一項男性特定群體的尿液及生物樣本HPV和病例對照研究。人類乳頭瘤病毒（HPV） 是全球最常見的性傳染病毒之一，能影響男性並導致多種疾病，包括生殖器疣（椰菜花）、陰莖癌、肛門癌 及 口咽癌。然而，男性 HPV 的感染情況一直缺乏研究，而你的參與將有助填補這個重要的知識空白。
本研究旨在了解HPV感染率、患者人口統計特徵、臨床特徵以及被診斷患有HPV相關惡性腫瘤的男性患者的疾病負擔。以評估男性尿液 HPV 測試的準確性，並更深入了解男性感染 HPV的風險因素，以及幫助未來預防及治療策略。
-如初步檢測確診為HPV陽性的患者，或將安排進一步行檢查 (例如:軟式膀胱鏡檢查等等)及跟進複檢。
參加者條件（男性，18歲或以上）：
1) 陰莖癌，肛⾨癌，或咽喉癌患者
2) 曾患性傳染病
3) 曾有同性性⾏為
4) 慢性前列腺炎患者
地點：沙⽥威爾斯親王醫院
樣本收集： 尿液及尿道拭子、口咽拭子、肛門拭子、冠狀溝拭子
-填寫簡單問卷
-根據情況也可能採集 20 毫升血液
[費用全免]
-完成整個研究計劃後可獲得港幣
$400
津貼
參加者的資料將會以專業方式絕對保密!!
所收集的資料僅用於學術研究用途
名額有限，先到先得!
閣下如對本研究有興趣請透過以下連結報名：
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf__iQ0Ike8hpG6qIm1mjtF0nCTdcPFKT2v9jFARsuZbqjMJw/viewform?usp=header
-如果評估合適參與研究，將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如有查詢，歡迎電郵: timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk，與研究人員劉先生聯絡。
________________________________________________________________________
Free HPV Screening for Men in Specific Groups [Free!!]
The Chinese University of Hong Kong Division of Urology Research Recruitment
The Department of Surgery (Urology), The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently recruiting participants for a hybrid cohort and case-control study on male urinary HPV.
Human Papillomavirus (HPV) is one of the most common sexually transmitted viruses worldwide. It can affect men and lead to serious conditions including genital warts, penile cancer, anal cancer, and oropharyngeal cancer. However, HPV infection in men remains under-studied. Your cooperation is highly solicited.
This research aims to determine HPV prevalence, patient demographics, clinical characteristics, and disease burden in men. It will also evaluate the accuracy of a new urine-based HPV DNA test and explore risk factors to support future prevention and treatment strategies.
Participants who test positive for HPV in the initial urine test may be invited for further investigations (e.g. flexible cystoscopy) and regular follow-up re-testing.
Eligibility (Males aged 18 or above)
Patients diagnosed with penile cancer, anal cancer, or oropharyngeal cancer
Men with a history of sexually transmitted diseases (STD)
Men who have sex with men (MSM)
Patients with chronic prostatitis / chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CPPS)
Study Location: Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin
Narrative description
Urine sample + swabs (urethral, oropharyngeal, anal, coronal sulcus)
Complete a simple questionnaire
Optional: 20 ml blood sample (if required)
Free of Charge in HPV test !!
Upon successful completion of the study, participants will receive a
HKD 400
travel subsidy
Your Privacy is Fully Protected.

Announcements
Free HPV Screening for Men in Specific Groups [Free!!!] !!!注意: 男性特定群組 HPV 病毒篩查   [費用全免] [$400交通津貼] - Department of Surgery
From: Tim Lau
timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學泌尿外科研究招募
:
香港中文大學泌尿外科現正進行一項男性特定群體的尿液及生物樣本HPV和病例對照研究。人類乳頭瘤病毒（HPV） 是全球最常見的性傳染病毒之一，能影響男性並導致多種疾病，包括生殖器疣（椰菜花）、陰莖癌、肛門癌 及 口咽癌。然而，男性 HPV 的感染情況一直缺乏研究，而你的參與將有助填補這個重要的知識空白。
本研究旨在了解HPV感染率、患者人口統計特徵、臨床特徵以及被診斷患有HPV相關惡性腫瘤的男性患者的疾病負擔。以評估男性尿液 HPV 測試的準確性，並更深入了解男性感染 HPV的風險因素，以及幫助未來預防及治療策略。
-如初步檢測確診為HPV陽性的患者，或將安排進一步行檢查 (例如:軟式膀胱鏡檢查等等)及跟進複檢。
參加者條件（男性，18歲或以上）：
1) 陰莖癌，肛⾨癌，或咽喉癌患者
2) 曾患性傳染病
3) 曾有同性性⾏為
4) 慢性前列腺炎患者
地點：沙⽥威爾斯親王醫院
樣本收集： 尿液及尿道拭子、口咽拭子、肛門拭子、冠狀溝拭子
-填寫簡單問卷
-根據情況也可能採集 20 毫升血液
[費用全免]
-完成整個研究計劃後可獲得港幣
$400
津貼
參加者的資料將會以專業方式絕對保密!!
所收集的資料僅用於學術研究用途
名額有限，先到先得!
閣下如對本研究有興趣請透過以下連結報名：
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf__iQ0Ike8hpG6qIm1mjtF0nCTdcPFKT2v9jFARsuZbqjMJw/viewform?usp=header
-如果評估合適參與研究，將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如有查詢，歡迎電郵: timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk，與研究人員劉先生聯絡。
________________________________________________________________________
Free HPV Screening for Men in Specific Groups [Free!!]
The Chinese University of Hong Kong Division of Urology Research Recruitment
The Department of Surgery (Urology), The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently recruiting participants for a hybrid cohort and case-control study on male urinary HPV.
Human Papillomavirus (HPV) is one of the most common sexually transmitted viruses worldwide. It can affect men and lead to serious conditions including genital warts, penile cancer, anal cancer, and oropharyngeal cancer. However, HPV infection in men remains under-studied. Your cooperation is highly solicited.
This research aims to determine HPV prevalence, patient demographics, clinical characteristics, and disease burden in men. It will also evaluate the accuracy of a new urine-based HPV DNA test and explore risk factors to support future prevention and treatment strategies.
Participants who test positive for HPV in the initial urine test may be invited for further investigations (e.g. flexible cystoscopy) and regular follow-up re-testing.
Eligibility (Males aged 18 or above)
Patients diagnosed with penile cancer, anal cancer, or oropharyngeal cancer
Men with a history of sexually transmitted diseases (STD)
Men who have sex with men (MSM)
Patients with chronic prostatitis / chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CPPS)
Study Location: Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin
Narrative description
Urine sample + swabs (urethral, oropharyngeal, anal, coronal sulcus)
Complete a simple questionnaire
Optional: 20 ml blood sample (if required)
Free of Charge in HPV test !!
Upon successful completion of the study, participants will receive a
HKD 400
travel subsidy
Your Privacy is Fully Protected.
Data will only be used for academic research purposes.

Research Project:
Organ Donation Intentions in Hong Kong University Students

Hello! We cordially invite
CUHK undergraduate students (must be Hong Kong permanent residents)
to participate in an online research study regarding organ donation intentions.

為了確保研究數據的質量與您的填寫體驗，請務必閱讀以下細則：

強烈建議使用電腦
完成本研究。

本研究包含
兩個部分
。參與者必須完成全部兩個部分才能獲得現金補償。

完成第一部分後，需
間隔
24
小時

30-40
分鐘

實驗系統設有篩選機制。如果在實驗過程中彈出「您無法參與本實驗」的提示，則證明您未通過篩選或喪失資格，屆時將無法獲得補償。

Device Recommendation:
To ensure ease of completion and data quality, it is
strongly recommended to use a computer
to complete this study.
Study Structure:
This study consists of
two parts
. Participants must complete both parts to be eligible for cash compensation.

24-hour interval
between the first and second parts. Please set aside sufficient time.

The total time to complete the study is approximately
30-40 minutes
.

The system includes a screening mechanism. If a message stating
"You are not able to participant this study"
pops up during the process, it indicates that you have not passed the screening or have lost eligibility, and no compensation will be provided.

Before starting the questionnaire, you will be required to sign an
informed consent form
.

100
港幣

Upon completing both stages of the experiment, you will receive
HKD 100 in cash
as monetary compensation.
Note: If you have already participated in this experiment, please do not sign up again. Duplicate registrations will be considered invalid.

持有香港永久居民身份的香港中文大學在讀本科生 。
未報名成為一名器官捐贈者
無抑鬱症確診史

Hong Kong permanent residents
.

not
registered as an organ donor.

梁菀洺女士 (Mia Liang)
1155106133@link.cuhk.edu.hk
導師：

cstse@cuhk.edu.hk

Announcements
[2026-2027] Multicultural Psychological Support Service: Counselling Service for Non-Local Students [2026-2027]多元文化心理支援服務: 為非本地學生提供母語輔導服務 - Wellness and Counselling Centre, Office of Student Affairs
From: Chu Choi Ying
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mpss@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
The Chinese version follows the English version of this email.
Multicultural Psychological Support Service: Counselling Service for Non-Local Students
No matter where we come from, we all desire to express our emotional needs with no barrier. Speaking in our mother tongue with someone who shares our cultural background not only allows us to better articulate ourselves but also fosters a deeper sense of understanding.
In order to support CUHK non-local students, the Wellness and Counselling Centre (WACC) of the Office of Student Affairs (OSA) offers Multicultural Psychological Support Service. This service allows students to receive counselling services in a comfortable environment.
The service is provided by St John’s Cathedral Counselling Service, and it is available to all CUHK full-time non-local students. The counsellors from St John’s Cathedral Counselling Service are capable of providing counselling services in English or Putonghua, as well as other languages including English, Putonghua, French, German, Dutch, Spanish, Hindi, Indonesian, Japanese, Portuguese, Korean, Urdu, Russian, Sindhi and Tagalog (subject to counsellor’s availability). Below are the specific details of the services provided:
Location:
St John’s Cathedral Counselling Service
Address:
10th Floor, Two Chinachem Plaza, 68 Connaught Road, Central
Website:
https://www.sjccs.hk/
Service Period:
July 2026 to June 2027
Opening hours:
9AM to 9PM Monday to Saturday, except on Public Holiday
Service Target:
All CUHK full-time non-local students, including exchange students.
Local students with extensive exposure to cultural experiences outside Hong Kong are also eligible (e.g. with international school backgrounds, or ethnic minorities born in Hong Kong).
Session:
6 counselling sessions
For more information about the Multicultural Psychological Support Service, please visit
OSA WACC website
or contact WACC staff at 3943 9951 or 3943 7208.
How can I make an appointment?
Enroll online by webform:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13733096
If you have an urgent need to see a counsellor, you may visit WACC during office hours. The Duty Counsellor will assess your needs and make appropriate arrangements with you. If you need emotional support during non-office hours, please call the CUHK 24-hour Emotional Support Hotline at 5400 2055 (exclusively for CUHK Full-time Students and Part-time PGDE Students).
Enquiries:
Contact number: 3943 9951/ 3943 7208
Email:
mpss@cuhk.edu.hk
/
wacc@cuhk.edu.hk
Best regards,
Multicultural Psychological Support Service (MPSS)
Wellness and Counselling Centre
Office of Student Affairs
3/F Pommerenke Student Centre, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shatin, N.T.
T: +852 3943 9951   E:
mpss@cuhk.edu.hk
多元文化心理支援服務
為非本地學生提供母語輔導服務
無論來自哪裡，我們都渴望輕鬆地表達感受。用母語與有相似文化背景的人交談，不僅讓我們能清楚表達自己，還可增強更深層次的理解。為支援非本地同學，學生事務處心理健康及輔導中心推出「多元文化心理支援服務」，讓同學可在舒服自在的情況下打開心扉。
輔導服務由中環聖約翰座堂輔導服務提供，服務對象為所有香港中文大學全日制非本地學生。輔導員除了能提供以英語或普通話為母語的輔導服務外，亦能以法語、德語、荷蘭語、西班牙語、印地語、印尼語、日語、葡萄牙語、韓語、烏爾都語、俄語、信德語和他加祿語等其他語言進行輔導。服務詳情如下：
服務提供者：
聖約翰座堂輔導服務中心
服務地址：
中環幹諾道中
68
號華懋廣場Ⅱ期
10
樓
網址：
https://www.sjccs.hk/
服務時段：
2026年7月至2027年六月
營業時間：
週一至週六上午 9 時至晚上 9 時，公眾假期除外
服務對象：
香港中文大學全日制非本地學生，包括交換生
本地學生如有豐富的非本地文化背景（如曾就讀國際學校，或在香港出生的少數族裔人士）亦可申請
輔導次數：
提供6次輔導服務
有關「多元文化心理支援服務」的詳情，請瀏覽
學生事務處心理健康及輔導中心網頁
或致電3943 9951或3943 7208向心理健康及輔導中心職員查詢。
如何預約輔導服務？
於網上預約:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13733096
如急需與輔導員見面，可於辦公時間內到訪位於龐萬倫學生中心2樓的心理健康及輔導中心。當值的輔導員會評估同學的需要，並作出適當的安排。如欲在非辦公時間尋求情緒支援，歡迎致電中大24小時情緒支援熱線5400 2055（僅供中文大學全日制學生及兼讀制學位教師教育文憑學生使用）。
查詢：
致電：3943 9951/3943 7208
電郵：
mpss@cuhk.edu.hk
/
wacc@cuhk.edu.hk

English Language Teaching Unit
Do you want to improve your English with your peers in an informal setting? Need help with your essays or job seeking?
Sign up for Peer Tutoring sessions now!
Peer Tutoring Scheme provides:
What:
Peer Tutoring services
One-on-one consultations in forms of
face-to-face
,
Zoom
and
online feedback sessions
For whom:
Undergraduates & Postgraduates of CUHK
When:
Summer:
1 June to 31 August 2026
Monday to Friday
(excluding university holidays and public holidays)
11:30 a.m. – 7:30 p.m.
Where:
Face-to-face sessions
will be conducted in the designated area in Learning Commons, 6/F Wu Ho Man Yuen Building
Zoom sessions
and
online feedback sessions
will be conducted online
How:
Register online – advance booking at
https://eltu.cuhk.edu.hk/pts/pages/instruction.html
(no walk-in sessions are available)

Academic Writing
Oral Presentation/ Public Speaking
Interview Skills
Job / Graduate School Application
Public Exams (e.g. IELTS/TOEFL)
Social English

countries/regions and
8
faculties to:

help you build up skills for effective and independent language learning.

title: Recruiting Participants: [Brief Training Programme for Eating Disorders] 「进食问题短期训练计划」诚邀普通话参与者
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/08/21
»
Announcements
Recruiting Participants: [Brief Training Programme for Eating Disorders] 「进食问题短期训练计划」诚邀普通话参与者 - Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory, Department of Psychology
From: Yanbin, XIE
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ybxie@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
招募参与者：进食问题短期训练计划
香港中文大学临床心理科学实验室团队现正推行一项针对进食问题的短期训练计划，诚邀符合资格的人士参与。
六周指导式自助练习，处理社会评价与自我批评
打破自我批评的恶性循环
找回自我肯定的正向情绪
香港中文大学校园内，全程免费
进食问题很多时候并非只是一个关于食物、身材偏好或者意志力的问题，而关乎我们如何看待自己，以及如何处理和他人的关系。目前，针对进食问题的治疗多采用认知行为取向，研究证实能有效控制非适应性进食行为的出现。本计划是团队基于实证研究开发的新训练方案，采用社会情绪取向，聚焦于处理自己与他人的关系。本项目遵循阶梯式照护模式，定位为指导式自助短期介入方案，旨在以较少的时间投入及心理负担为参加者提供支援。
训练为期6周，包括「每周1次实体会面 + 自助练习 + 线上心理评估访谈及问卷」；训练完成后1个月及6个月进行跟进评估。
「招募要求」
年满18岁或以上；普通话流利；
受进食问题困扰，例如，对进食、体重或体型有过度的关注，进食后感到强烈自责或羞愧，反复出现无法控制的暴食行为，或伴有反复出现的代偿行为（催吐、使用泻药或利尿剂、过度运动等）并因此影响日常生活或情绪；
目前并未接受其他形式的心理治疗或精神科药物治疗；
能够亲身前往香港中文大学校园参与训练。
「报名链接」
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0pJvKNUXXEGYx4G
报名后，我们将联络您安排筛选问卷及访谈，以确认是否适合参加本计划，并邀请符合条件者参与训练。
如有疑问请联络研究团队：epplab.ed@cuhk.edu.hk。
所有个人资料仅用作研究用途，并会严格保密。
临床心理科学实验室团队
Recruiting Participants: Brief Training Programme for Eating Disorders
The Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory at CUHK is currently running a brief training programme for individuals struggling with eating disorders. We are now inviting eligible participants to join.
We all care about how we look. But eating disorders are often about much more than food, body shape, or willpower—they are deeply tied to how we see ourselves and how we relate to others. While cognitive-behavioural therapy (CBT) is the most widely used and evidence-based treatment for eating disorders, our team has developed a new training protocol grounded in recent research, drawing on a socioemotional framework that focuses specifically on self-perception and interpersonal relationships. Following a stepped-care model, this programme is designed as a brief guided self-help intervention, offering meaningful support with a relatively low time commitment and psychological load.
  The programme runs for 6 weeks:
Weekly in-person sessions on campus
Guided self-help practice tasks to complete between sessions
Online assessment interviews and questionnaires
Follow-up evaluations will be conducted at 1 month and 6 months post-training.

Who We're Looking For
Are aged 18 or above;
Are fluent in Mandarin;
Are currently struggling with eating disorder symptoms, for example, excessive evaluation or concerns on food, weight, or body shape, intense guilt or shame after eating, recurrent episodes of binge eating that feel out of control, with compensatory behaviours such as self-induced vomiting, laxative or diuretic misuse, or excessive exercise;
Are not currently receiving any other form of psychological therapy or psychiatric medication;
Are able to attend in-person sessions on the CUHK campus

Sign Up Here
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0pJvKNUXXEGYx4G
After you sign up, we will contact you to complete a screening questionnaire and a brief interview to see if this programme is a good fit for you. If eligible, you will be invited to join the 6-week training.
 For any questions, feel free to reach out to us at:
epplab.ed@cuhk.edu.hk
All information you provide will be kept strictly confidential and used solely for research screening and intervention purposes.
Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory

[Brief Psychological Training Programme for Social Anxiety] Welcome Cantonese speakers  [社交焦慮短期訓練計劃] 誠邀符合條件的廣東話使用者參與 - Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory, Department of Psychology
From: Yanbin, XIE
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ybxie@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
招募參與者：社交焦慮短期介入訓練計劃
六週指導式自助練習，處理社會評價與自我批評
打破自我批評的惡性循環
找回自我肯定的正向情緒

香港中文大學校園內，全程免費
香港中文大學臨床心理科學實驗室團隊現正推行一項針對社交焦慮問題的短期介入訓練計劃，誠邀符合資格的人士參與。
社交焦慮不止影響我們如何應對社交場合，亦關乎我們如何看待自己，以及如何與他人建立聯繫。目前，社交焦慮問題的治療多採用認知行為取向，研究證實能有效改善個人在社交情境中的功能表現。本計劃則是團隊基於實證研究開發的新訓練方案，採用社會情緒取向，聚焦於處理個人與自我及他人的關係。本項目遵循階梯式照護模式 (stepped-care model)，定位為指導式自助 (guided self-help) 短期介入方案，旨在以較少的時間投入及心理負擔，為參加者提供有效支援。
訓練為期6週，包括「每週1次實體會面 + 自助練習 + 線上心理評估訪談及問卷」 ； 訓練完成後1個月和六個月進行隨訪評估
 「招募要求」
年滿18歲或以上；廣東話流利；
在社交焦慮方面感到困擾，例如在社交或公開場合強烈緊張焦慮、擔心自己被負面評價、迴避社交場合，並明顯影響工作或學習；
現時並未接受其他形式的心理治療或精神科藥物治療；
能夠親身前往香港中文大學校園參與訓練。

「參與流程」
報名後，我們將聯絡您安排篩選問卷及訪談，以確認是否適合參加本計劃，並邀請符合條件者參與訓練。

「報名連結」
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eDNm9u2HOUkR302
如有疑問，歡迎聯絡研究團隊：cdclabcuhk@gmail.com
本計劃已獲香港中文大學–新界東醫院聯網臨床研究倫理聯席委員會審批（CUHK-NTEC CREC 2025.796）。
所有個人資料僅用作研究篩選及介入用途，並會嚴格保密。
香港中文大學臨床心理科學實驗室團隊
Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory
Recruiting Participants: Brief Psychological Training Programme for Social Anxiety
The Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently conducting a brief intervention programme for individuals experiencing social anxiety difficulties. We invite eligible individuals to participate.
Social anxiety not only affects how we cope in social situations but also involves how we view ourselves and relate to others. While cognitive-behavioural approaches are widely used and evidence-based for treating social anxiety, our team has developed a novel training protocol grounded in empirical research that adopts a social-emotional approach, focusing on improving individuals’ relationships with themselves and with others. Following the stepped-care model, this programme is designed as a brief guided self-help intervention, aiming to provide effective support with minimal time commitment and psychological burden.
The training programme spans 6 weeks and includes:
Weekly in-person sessions (once per week)
Self-help practice exercises
Questionnaire assessments
Follow-up evaluations will be conducted one month and six months after the training.
「Eligibility Criteria」
Aged 18 or above
Fluent in Cantonese
Experiencing significant social anxiety-related distress (e.g., intense anxiety in social or public settings, fear of negative evaluation, avoidance of social situations, with noticeable impact on work or study)
Not currently receiving other forms of psychological therapy or psychiatric medication
Able to attend in-person sessions on the CUHK campus
「Procedures」
After registration, we will contact you to arrange a screening questionnaire and an interview to determine your suitability for the programme. Eligible participants will then be invited to join the training.
「Registration Link」
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eDNm9u2HOUkR302
For enquiries, please contact our research team at: cdclabcuhk@gmail.com
This study has been approved by the Joint CUHK-NTEC Clinical Research Ethics Committee (CUHK-NTEC CREC 2025.796).
All personal data collected will be used solely for research screening and intervention purposes and will be kept strictly confidential.

Better Gut, Better Sleep? Gut-Brain Study | Earn up to HKD 500 「腸」通無阻，瞓得更好？「腸·腦」研究 | 最高可獲 HKD 500 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Michael Ng
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
tsztsunng@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
近年醫學界發現，我們的腸道健康與大腦息息相關！原來「便秘」和「睡眠質素」的改變，可能是腦部退化的早期信號。為了深入了解這條神奇的「腸腦連線」，香港中文大學精神科學系睡眠研究組現正招募研究參加者。
研究對象:
年齡介乎 50 至 80 歲
關注腸道健康或者受便秘問題困擾（如排便困難、次數較少等）
沒有腦退化、精神疾病史
參加者需完成以下簡單程序：
填寫問卷 及 進行簡單面談
進行一次非入侵性睡眠檢測
記錄連續兩星期「大便日記」
進行一次結腸運輸試驗
收集一次大便樣本
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者最多可獲 HKD 500 超市禮券的津貼
如對本研究有興趣，請透過以下連結報名參加：
[網址連結:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eeTcY6hrKILNwhg
]
如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電 3919 7792 / 9568 9006 或 WhatsApp 9568 9006與負責研究人員聯絡、查詢詳情。謝謝
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Recent research suggests that gut health is closely linked to brain function. Changes in bowel habits (e.g. constipation) and sleep quality may even be early signs of neurodegeneration.
To better understand this “gut–brain axis, we sincerely invite you to take part in our research study.
Who can join:
Aged 50–80
Concerned about gut health or bothered by constipation
No history of dementia or psychiatric disorders
What you will do:
Complete questionnaires and a brief interview
Undergo a sleep assessment
Record a 2-week bowel diary
Complete a colonic transit time test
Collect one stool sample
Incentive:
All assessments are free of charge.
Eligible participants may receive up to HKD 500 in supermarket vouchers upon completion.
Interested? Please sign up here:

]

children reading test and brain imaging 【200蚊報酬】粵語母語兒童及家庭閲讀能力診斷與神經發展測試 - Department of Psychology
From: SUE GAO
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155229912@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【Introduction】: This research study, titled “Compensation of White Matter Pathways and Networks in Chinese Children with Developmental Dyslexia in Hong Kong,” is led by Prof. Jingjing Zhao from the Department of Psychology at The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
【Description of the study】: The purpose of this study is to explore how white matter pathways in the brain may compensate for reading difficulties in Chinese-speaking children with developmental dyslexia in Hong Kong.
【Study Procedures】 ● Reading and Cognitive Assessments: Your child will participate in reading and cognitive assessments lasting approximately 30–40 minutes. You are not required to complete any of these tasks. ● Brain Imaging (MRI Scan): Your child will also undergo a magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scan lasting about 20 minutes. The MRI procedure is non-invasive, painless, radiation-free, and no sedation. Please inform the research team in advance if your child has claustrophobia, metal implants, or a pacemaker.
Target participants: Children aged 8–16 years, whose parents are native Mandarin or Cantonese speakers, are eligible to participate.
【Data Confidentiality and Usage】:All data will be handled in accordance with data protection and privacy regulations. All collected data will be anonymized and will not include identifiable information (e.g., name, ID number, contact details). Data will be used solely for academic research purposes.
針對多種神經發育學習障礙的閱讀困難跨診斷研究
現正招募：
8-16歲、廣東話為母語的兒童
（1） 正常發展或
（2）被診斷或懷疑有任何一項：
（i）自閉症
（ii）注意力缺陷
（iii）讀寫障礙
測試内容：
語言、記憶及認知能力測試

Announcements
#Recruiting vocally healthy participants aged 18 and above to participate in an acoustic analysis study to explore the quality and characteristics of the voice (HK$150 coupon) 誠意邀請18歲或以上沒有聲線障礙的人士參與探索聲線質量和特徵的聲學分析研究 (HK$150 coupon) - Department of Otorhinolarynogology, Head and Neck Surgery
From: Rina To
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
rinato@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學耳鼻咽喉 頭頸外科學系現正招募十八歲或以上沒有聲線障礙的人士參與一項聲學分析的研究，旨在探究平滑化倒頻譜突出峰值 (CPPS) 的臨界值和其診斷準確性。
CPPS是一種可應用於日常對話的聲線聲學分析參數。CPPS相對於其他常用的聲學參數具有更高的診斷準確性。但是，根據文獻的報告顯示，使用不同的語言，聲線樣本類型，和軟件，都會影響到CPPS的結果。我們希望這項研究的結果能夠為臨床醫生和研究人員對聲線障礙患者進行客觀測量並為聲線評估的量化結果提供明確的參考。
招募對象：
年滿十八歲或以上
沒有聲線問題的人士
以廣東話為母語
費用：全免
評估與檢查地點：威爾斯親王醫院
研究程序及内容：
1）參加者將填寫聲線問卷， 並親臨威爾斯親王醫院接受喉纖維內視鏡檢查和聲線錄製。
2）喉纖維內視鏡檢查時能清楚看見咽喉，每次檢查需時約三十分鐘，是屬於低風險的檢查，一般只會感到輕微不適。
報名連結﹕
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=4267989
參與研究，獲得獎勵：
完成聲線評估後，您可獲得港幣150元的超市現金券。
名額有限，先到先得。收到報名後，我們會再與合資格的參加者聯絡。
歡迎將此招募信息推薦給身邊有需要的家人以及朋友。
如有查詢，請與研究人員王先生（Mr. Wang）聯絡。
電郵：
zikaiwang@link.cuhk.edu.hk
The Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, is currently recruiting vocally healthy participants aged 18 and above for a study investigating the cut-off score and diagnostic accuracy of the smoothed cepstral peak prominence (CPPS) for Cantonese speakers with dysphonia.
CPPS is a parameter for acoustic analysis of voice that can be used in everyday conversation to provide a more comprehensive and realistic picture of an individual's vocal characteristics in natural communication situations. CPPS has a higher diagnostic accuracy than other commonly used acoustic parameters. However, reports in the literature indicate that the use of different languages, different types of voice samples, and different software can affect the results of the CPPS. We hope that the results of this study will provide clinicians and researchers with a clear reference for the quantitative results of objective measurement and voice assessment in patients with voice disorders.
Recruitment target:
Age 18 or above
People who do not have voice problems
Fluent in Cantonese as a native language or proficient in Cantonese
Cost: Free of charge
Location: Prince of Wales Hospital
Procedures and details of this Study:
Participants will undergo a laryngeal videostroboscopy examination and a comprehensive voice assessment at Prince of Wales Hospital.
A videostroboscopy examination can clearly observe the throat to detect whether it has structural or functional problem for speaking. Each examination takes approximately thirty minutes. It is a low-risk procedure, and participants typically only experience mild discomfort.
Registration link:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=4267989
Participate in the study and receive a reward:
After completing the voice assessment, you will receive a HK$ 150 supermarket gift card.
Limited seats available on a first-come first-served basis. We will contact you afterwards if you are suitable to join this study.
Welcome to recommend this recruitment information to your family and friends in need.
If you have any inquiries, please contact Mr. Wang.
Email:
zikaiwang@link.cuhk.edu.hk

完成聲線評估後，您可獲得港幣150元的超市現金券。
名額有限，先到先得。收到報名後，我們會再與合資格的參加者聯絡。
歡迎將此招募信息推薦給身邊有需要的家人以及朋友。
如有查詢，請與研究人員王先生（Mr. Wang）聯絡。
電郵：
zikaiwang@link.cuhk.edu.hk
The Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, is currently recruiting vocally healthy participants aged 18 and above for a study investigating the cut-off score and diagnostic accuracy of the smoothed cepstral peak prominence (CPPS) for Cantonese speakers with dysphonia.
CPPS is a parameter for acoustic analysis of voice that can be used in everyday conversation to provide a more comprehensive and realistic picture of an individual's vocal characteristics in natural communication situations. CPPS has a higher diagnostic accuracy than other commonly used acoustic parameters. However, reports in the literature indicate that the use of different languages, different types of voice samples, and different software can affect the results of the CPPS. We hope that the results of this study will provide clinicians and researchers with a clear reference for the quantitative results of objective measurement and voice assessment in patients with voice disorders.
Recruitment target:
Age 18 or above
People who do not have voice problems
Fluent in Cantonese as a native language or proficient in Cantonese
Cost: Free of charge
Location: Prince of Wales Hospital
Procedures and details of this Study:
Participants will undergo a laryngeal videostroboscopy examination and a comprehensive voice assessment at Prince of Wales Hospital.
A videostroboscopy examination can clearly observe the throat to detect whether it has structural or functional problem for speaking. Each examination takes approximately thirty minutes. It is a low-risk procedure, and participants typically only experience mild discomfort.
Registration link:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=4267989
Participate in the study and receive a reward:
After completing the voice assessment, you will receive a HK$ 150 supermarket gift card.
Limited seats available on a first-come first-served basis. We will contact you afterwards if you are suitable to join this study.
Welcome to recommend this recruitment information to your family and friends in need.
If you have any inquiries, please contact Mr. Wang.

From: Maggie Lee
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
[
新中藥方劑治療
2
型糖尿病的臨床安全性、有效性和多組評價：對
β
細胞功能和胰島素抵抗的影響】
香港中文大學內科及藥物治療學系與香港中文大學香港中西醫結合醫學研究所現正聯合進行一項為期36週，以內服中藥(沖劑)治療 2 型糖尿病人
 研究對象：18至70歲華人
沒有重大疾病，沒有服用中藥， 身體質量指數 (BMI) ≥18 kg/m²  (公斤 ÷ 米 ÷ 米)
不吸煙或已戒煙至少 12 個月，如女性目前未懷孕
患糖尿病未滿 6 年，且在過去 3 個月內未使用任何降血糖藥物（包括胰島素）治療
至少具備以下其中一項風險因素:
糖尿病家族史 (尤其父母或兄弟姐妹在40歲前診斷 )
代謝綜合症 (3高：高血糖，高血壓，高膽固醇)
超重或肥胖
脂肪肝
多囊卵巢綜合症
妊娠糖尿病病史
如不確定自己是否患有糖尿病，會安排你服用葡萄糖飲料（75 克口服葡萄糖耐量試驗）
研究內容：中西醫評估、心電圖、肝纖維化掃描、抽血檢查、填寫問卷、服用研究中藥或安慰劑等
地點：新界沙田威爾斯醫院，舊座，3 樓，3M 病房 - 糖尿及內分泌研究中心
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者可獲得高達港幣 $1,000 的津貼，名額有限，先到先得！
閣下如對本研究有興趣請透過以下連結報名參加：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=3542692
如果初步合適參與研究，負責同事將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電  3505 3897 / 6937 3365 或 WhatsApp 6937 3365與負責研究人員聯絡、查詢詳情。
[Clinical safety, efficacy and multiomic evaluation of a novel Chinese Medicine formula in Type 2 diabetes: Effects on beta-cell function and insulin resistance
.]
Department of Medicine and Therapeutics and Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine, CUHK are jointly conducting a 36-week clinical study on the use of oral traditional Chinese medicine (granule form) for treating type 2 diabetes.
Eligibility Criteria: Ethnic Chinese individuals aged 18 to 70 years
No major illnesses, not currently taking any traditional Chinese medicine, and with a Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥ 18 kg/m² (kg ÷ metre ÷ metre)
Non-smokers or those who have quit smoking for at least 12 months; females must not be currently pregnant
Diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for less than 6 years and have not used any glucose-lowering medications (including insulin) in the past 3 months
Must have at least one of the following risk factors:
Family history of diabetes (especially if parents or siblings were diagnosed before age of 40)
Metabolic syndrome (three highs: high blood sugar, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol)
Overweight or obesity
Fatty liver
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
History of gestational diabetes
If you are unsure whether you have diabetes, a 75g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) will be arranged for you.

Study Procedures Include:
Chinese and Western medical assessments, Electrocardiogram (ECG), Liver fibrosis scan, Blood tests, Questionnaire completion, Taking either the study Chinese medicine or a placebo
Location: Ward 3M, 3/F, Old Block, Diabetes and Endocrinology Research Centre, Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin, New Territories
Free of charge to participate.
Successful participants may receive an allowance of up to HKD $1,000.
Limited quota – first come, first served!
Register via the following link:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=3542692
If you are eligible based on initial assessment, our research team will contact you shortly. Thank you!
For inquiries, please contact:
3505 3897 / 6937 3365
WhatsApp: 6937 3365

Deepen Your Practice: Free Online Info Session for "The Feeling Tone" Teacher Training!
Interested in exploring the subtle layers of Vedana (Feeling Tone) to transform reactivity into wise, compassionate action?
Join our lead trainer, Antonia Dorothea Sumbundu, alongside local trainers Prof. Stanley Chan and Mr. Ting Ka Tsun, for an exclusive interactive Zoom Information Session!
Whether you are looking to deepen your own practice or teach the new "Deeper Mindfulness" 8-week curriculum, this session will cover everything you need to know about programme structure, eligibility, and key learning outcomes.

bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/08/14
»
Announcements
[$320 travel allowance] Recruiting aged 65 or above elderly, along with their caregivers, to join a survey on elderly physical and mental health.  [$320交通津貼] 招募年滿65歲或以上的長者及其照顧者參加問卷調查，以了解香港長者的身心健康 - JC School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: Amy Wong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
amy.wong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
***
中文版本
***
研究背景
香港中文大學現正進行一項有關長者身心健康的調查，從而制定一個可以測量長者健康生活品質的工具。
招募對象
長者：65歲或以上，照顧者：18歲或以上；
香港居民；
能閱讀中文及以廣東話溝通； 及
曾使用長者服務設施或入住護理之家
參與方式
如果符合上述條件，請在下方連結登記及留下相關資料以作跟進，需時約1-3分鐘。完成登記後，研究人員將於兩星期內與你聯絡，並安排你與被照顧的長者以面對面或 Zoom形式完成問卷調查。
答謝安排
問卷調查約需 10–15 分鐘。首次完成問卷後，長者與照顧者合共可獲港幣 160 元現金以作答謝。約一星期後，我們將邀請二人再次完成相同問卷，完成後可再獲合共港幣 160 元現金以作答謝。每位長者只限參加一次。
報名登記連結
:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3qPvrQNVMFR0vz0
研究海報：
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1uT7ZS1Me6Nv_2qnVhXH6MozHA3GMc5mU/view?usp=sharing
查詢
本研究已獲香港中文大學 — 調查及行為研究操守委員會的審批。 (參考編號: SBRE-25-0737) 。如有任何查詢，歡迎聯絡主研究員 黃麗儀教授 (電郵:
lywong@cuhk.edu.hk
) 或研究員黃小姐 (Amy) / 張小姐 (Annie) (電話: 2252-8408 / 2252-8404) 。
名額有限！先到先得！
歡迎轉發此訊息給您的家人及朋友！
***
English version
***
S
tudy Background
The JC School of Public Health and Primary Care at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently conducting a survey on the physical and mental health of older adults in Hong Kong to develop a tool in measuring their health-related quality of life in Hong Kong.
Target Group
Elderly: Aged 65 or above; Caregiver: 18 years old or above;
Hong Kong residents;
Able to read Chinese and communicate in Cantonese; and
Has ever used elderly service facilities or nursing homes.
How to Participate
If you meet the above criteria, please complete the registration form in around 1-3 minutes. After registration, our staff will contact you within two weeks and arrange an in-person/ Zoom interview for you and the elderly participant to complete the questionnaire.
Appreciation
The survey takes about 10-15 minutes. Upon completion, you and the elderly participant will receive a total of HK$160 cash as a token of appreciation. You and the elderly participant will also be invited to take the same follow-up survey in around one week, and you will receive an additional HK$160 cash after finishing it. Each elderly participant may only participate once.
Registration L
ink:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_3qPvrQNVMFR0vz0
Study
Poster:
https://drive.google.com/file/d/1uT7ZS1Me6Nv_2qnVhXH6MozHA3GMc5mU/view?usp=sharing
Contact Us
This study has been approved by the Survey and Behavioural Research Ethics Committee (Ref: SBRE-25-0737). Should you have any enquiries, please contact the Principal Investigator Prof. Eliza Wong (E-mail: lywong@cuhk.edu.hk) or researchers Ms. Amy Wong or Ms. Annie Cheung (Tel: 2252-8408 / 2252-8404).
Limited quotas only! First come, first served!
Feel free to share this invitation with your family and friends!
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

AI ‘as’ and ‘for’ Education: Integrating AI Ethics in Curriculum Design and AI Tool Demonstration  - CUHK Centre for Bioethics
From: CUHK Centre for Bioethics
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
bioethics@med.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
[This email is sent on behalf of the CUHK Centre for Bioethics and the Centre for Learning Enhancement And Research, CUHK.]
Dear Colleagues,
As Artificial Intelligence (AI) rapidly drives the digital transformation of healthcare, shaping a university curriculum that balances advanced technical literacy with robust moral foundations is more essential than ever.
We are pleased to invite you to our upcoming event, “
AI ‘as’ and ‘for’ Education: Integrating AI Ethics in Curriculum Design and AI Tool Demonstration”
, co-organized by the
CUHK Centre for Bioethics (CBIOE)
and the
Centre for Learning Enhancement And Research (CLEAR)
. This event will explore approaches to integrating AI ethics into curriculum design and share practical insights and tips for colleagues interested in incorporating in their respective disciplines.
AI ‘as’ and ‘for’ Education: Integrating AI Ethics in Curriculum Design and AI Tool Demonstration
Date
21 August 2026 (Friday)
Time
3:00pm – 4:30pm
Venue
LT 9, Yasumoto International Academic Park (YIA), CUHK
Register Now
Click
HERE
Abstract
This talk discusses the development of a modern curriculum for Year 1 and 2 (pre-clinical) students in clinical medicine, modified from traditional frameworks to better align with the digital transformation of healthcare. The curriculum embeds AI literacy into both the technical and ethical foundations of early medical training. This includes a course that condenses traditional mathematics and physics, focusing on clinically relevant applications in statistics, AI, bioinformatics, and biomedical engineering. Additionally, AI-specific case studies are integrated into the existing Bioethics course to address challenges such as algorithmic bias and diagnostic accountability. By evolving these early-stage pre-clinical frameworks, the talk illustrates how education in clinical medicine can move beyond traditional models to ensure students are prepared for the technical and moral complexities of modern, technology-driven practice.
Speakers & Moderators
Speakers
AI Ethics as Education
Integrating AI into the Pre-Clinical Curriculum for Clinical Medicine
Professor Eunice CHAN
, Assistant Professor, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (Shenzhen)
AI Tools for Education (Demonstration*)
Professor Qi DOU
, Associate Professor, Department of Computer Science and Engineering, Faculty of Engineering, CUHK
*
Demonstration will be available.
Participants are welcome to prepare a single PPT slide to try out the AI platform.
Moderators
Dr. Ann LAU
, Co-Director, CUHK Centre for Bioethics; Principal Lecturer, School of Biomedical Sciences, Faculty of Medicine, CUHK
Professor Paul LAM
, Associate Professor, Centre for Learning Enhancement And Research, CUHK
please visit
HERE
for further details and updates.
Come join us for a critical conversation on shaping an AI‑enhanced, ethics‑grounded future for education—where technology serves both learning and human values!
Best regards,
CUHK Centre for Bioethics and Centre for Learning Enhancement And Research

Science in the Public Service 2026｜MoCC Programme Highlights 「科學為民」服務巡禮2026｜MoCC精彩活動 - Social Responsibility and Sustainable Development Office
From: Jockey Club Museum of Climate Change (MoCC)
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mocc@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
「科學為民」服務巡禮2026｜MoCC精彩活動
「科學為民」服務巡禮將於今年八月至十二月舉行，以「『科學為民』二十載，科創求變惠民生」為主題。聯合政府多個部門及其他機構舉辦活動，向市民介紹政府部門及相關機構的科學工作，以及如何應用科技提供公眾服務。
作為參與機構之一，中大賽馬會氣候變化博物館（MoCC）今年將繼續響應「科學為民」服務巡禮。除了舉辦廣受歡迎的博物館及校園生態導賞外，更將聯同香港中文大學物理系攜手推出科普講座及科學體驗活動，一同探索科學的奧妙，了解科學與創新科技如何應對氣候挑戰，共創更具韌性的未來。
MoCC精彩活動：
https://www.mocc.cuhk.edu.hk/zh-tw/news/2026/1437-sips2026-ch
Science in the Public Service 2026｜MoCC Programme Highlights
Science in the Public Service (SIPS) will be held from August to December this year under the theme ‘20 Years of “Science in the Public Service”: Improving Livelihood through Science and Innovation’. Jointly organized by the government bureaux/departments and other organizations, the campaign aims to promote their scientific work and how technological applications are being applied to the provision of public services.
As one of the participating organizations, the MoCC will continue supporting the SIPS this year. In addition to the popular museum and campus eco-guided tours, the MoCC will join hands with CUHK Department of Physics to present a series of public lectures and hands-on science activities. Since 2023, the establishment of National Ecology Day on 15 August has marked a new stage for ecological civilisation in China. It aims at raising public awareness of ecological civilization, environmental protection, and promoting nature conservation efforts.
In response to this annual National Ecology Day, CUHK’s Social Responsibility and Sustainable Development Office, Jockey Club Museum of Climate Change, School of Life Sciences, School of Architecture, Coral Academy, PI Centre, as well as SDSN Hong Kong, will organize a series of related activities from 15 to 31 August, including themed exhibition, talk and ecological tours to foster a collective focus on biodiversity conservation and protect the environment through action.

【中大生態月2026】「珊瑚寶寶的成長日記：珊瑚學院的修復技術與最新進展」專題講座
本次講座將探討在高度城市化及高混濁度海域中進行珊瑚修復所面臨的獨特機遇與挑戰。崔佩怡教授將詳細介紹珊瑚繁殖及培育策略。講座其中一個重點是成功於實驗室培育珊瑚幼體，並將幼體移植至海洋環境後成長至具繁殖能力的階段，以及總結香港珊瑚修復工作的主要成果與重要啟示，並探討未來如何擴大修復規模，於城市化沿岸環境中建立更具韌性的珊瑚生態系統。
日期：2026年8月21日（星期五）
時間：下午12時30分至1時30分
地點：賽馬會氣候變化博物館（香港中文大學康本國際學術園8樓）
語言：廣東話
報名及詳情：
https://www.mocc.cuhk.edu.hk/zh-tw/news/2026/1435-cuhk-ecology-month-2026-ch
【CUHK Ecology Month 2026】‘Coral Baby Growth Diary: Restoration Techniques and Latest Advances at the Coral Academy’ Talk
This talk will focus on the unique opportunities and challenges of coral restoration in highly urbanized, turbid settings. Professor Apple Chui will detail coral breeding and propagation strategies. A key highlight is the successful lab-based rearing of coral larvae, with outplanted juveniles reaching reproductive size and successful spawning events documented in recent years in Tolo Harbour and Channel. The talk will synthesize key lessons learned and discuss the path forward for scaling coral restoration and building resilient coral ecosystems in urban coastal environments.
Date: 21 August 2026 (Friday)
Time: 12:30 pm – 1:30 pm
Venue: Jockey Club Museum of Climate Change (Yasumoto International Academic Park 8/F, The Chinese University of Hong Kong)
Language: Cantonese
Registration and details:

Lecture Series in Honour of Professor Jao Tsung-i: Reflection and Truth in Jao’s Scholarship
Professor Jao Tsung-i (1917–2018), renowned for his profound erudition in both the artistic and humanistic spheres East and West, had pioneered numerous research innovations. To commemorate the 110th anniversary of his birth, the “Lecture Series in Honour of Professor Jao Tsung-i” is co-organized by the Institute of Chinese Studies at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK), Jao Tsung-I Petite Ecole at the University of Hong Kong (HKU), Jao Tsung-I Academy of Sinology at Hong Kong Baptist University, Fung Ping Shan Library at HKU, and Hok Hoi Library. The three upcoming lectures, themed “Reflection and Truth in Jao’s Scholarship” and hosted by the Institute of Chinese Studies, will be held at CUHK on 12 September, 19 September, and 3 October.
