Announcements
Native Mandarin speakers from Mainland China wanted for a Chinese reading research study 【An allowance of HKD $100 will be provided upon successful enrollment】 招募中國內地普通話母語者參與中文閱讀模式研究【成功參與者可獲得港幣 $100 的車馬費】 - Centre for Sign Linguistics and Deaf Studies, Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
From: Melody Cheung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
cslds-melodycheung@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學手語及聾人研究中心招募研究參與者
香港中文大學手語及聾人研究中心現正進行一項探討中文閱讀模式的研究，誠邀符合以下條件的人士參與：
年齡介乎18至50歲
香港中文大學本科生/碩士學生
正常聽力
正常視力或矯正至正常視力
沒有神經、語言或閱讀障礙病史
從未學習過任何手語
此外，參加者須符合以下條件：
中國內地普通話母語者
能熟練閱讀及書寫簡體中文
實驗內容及時間
：
參與1個電腦判斷實驗，共1次實驗，約2小時。
地點：
香港中文大學教研樓二座（近科學園）
車馬費：
參加者每完成一次實驗可獲港幣100元車馬費。
注意事項：
如需佩戴隱形眼鏡，請同時攜帶普通有框眼鏡前來參與實驗。
進行眼動追蹤實驗時請勿佩戴漸進鏡片或有色隱形眼鏡。
有關參與實驗所提供的所有可識別個人身份資料將被嚴格保密。整個實驗不會對身心帶來痛楚或影響。
如有興趣參與，請填寫報名表格：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_9ELDNEDkVedp7Fk
若獲選參與，我們將透過 WhatsApp 或電郵與您聯絡。
如有任何查詢，歡迎致電3943 1136或電郵至
cslds-melodycheung@cuhk.edu.hk
與張小姐聯絡。
Participants wanted for a Chinese reading research study
The Centre for Sign Linguistics and Deaf Studies at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is conducting a research study on Chinese reading and is recruiting participants.
Eligibility Criteria
Participants must:
Be between 18 and 50 years old
Be a full-time Undergraduate or Master's student at The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Have normal hearing
Have normal or corrected-to-normal vision
Have no history of neurological, language, or reading disorders
Have never learned any sign Language
In addition, participants must meet the requirements:
Native Mandarin speakers from Mainland China
Proficient in reading and writing Simplified Chinese
Research procedures and sessions:
Participants will complete 1 computer-based judgment task in a single session lasting approximately 2 hours.
Location
Academic Building No. 2, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (near Hong Kong Science Park).
Compensation
Participants will receive HK$100 upon completion of each session.
Notes
If you wear contact lenses, please also bring your glasses with you to the experiment.
Please do not wear progressive lenses or coloured contact lenses during the eye-tracking experiment sessions.
All identifiable personal information collected during the study will be kept strictly confidential. Participation in this study is not expected to cause any physical or psychological discomfort.
If you are interested, please complete the registration form:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_9ELDNEDkVedp7Fk
Selected participants will be contacted via WhatsApp or email.
For enquiries, please contact:
Miss Melody Cheung
Tel: 3943 1136
Email:
cslds-melodycheung@cuhk.edu.hk

For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

bodyText:

2026/08/14
»
Announcements
CUHK Research Recruitment | Cantonese-speaking undergraduate students wanted for a 20–30 min online interview (HKD 50 reward)  香港中文大學研究招募｜招募母語為廣東話的中大本科生參與20–30分鐘線上訪談，可獲HKD $50報酬 - educational psychology
From: Zhou Zhenyi
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
zhenyizhou@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

香港中文大學研究招募｜參與線上訪談可獲 HKD $50！
香港中文大學（CUHK）教育心理學系
LEaPP Lab
現正招募本科生參與一項有關
第二語言學習經驗
的研究。
我們希望透過簡短的背景問卷及線上訪談，進一步了解大學生在第二語言學習過程中的經驗與感受。
一、參與資格
您需要：
目前為
香港中文大學本科生
；
年滿18歲；
母語為廣東話（Cantonese）
；
有學習第二語言（如英語）的經驗。
二、參與內容
參與者需要：
填寫一份簡短的
背景問卷
；
其後參與一次約
20–30分鐘的線上訪談
。
訪談將以輕鬆的形式進行，主要了解您在第二語言學習中的個人經驗和感受。
三、參與報酬
完成背景問卷及線上訪談的參與者將獲得
HKD $50
，以感謝您的時間與支持。
四、名額及截止日期
本研究
只招募少量參與者
。符合研究條件的參與者將按報名先後次序聯絡，
名額有限，先到先得
。

報名截止日期：20 August 2026
五、參與方式
請點擊以下連結填寫背景問卷並登記參與：
https://esurvey.psy.cuhk.edu.hk/jfe/form/SV_bE4IovsqrgWaTfo
聯絡我們：
如有任何查詢，歡迎聯絡研究小組：
zhenyizhou@cuhk.edu.hk
感謝您的參與與支持！
香港中文大學教育心理學系
LEaPP Lab
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

CUHK Research Recruitment | Join an Online Interview and Receive HKD $50!
The
LEaPP Lab, Department of Educational Psychology, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK)
, is currently recruiting undergraduate students for a research study on
second language learning experiences
.
Through a brief background questionnaire followed by an online interview, we hope to better understand university students' experiences and feelings during second language learning.
1. Eligibility
You are eligible to participate if you:
Are currently an
undergraduate student at CUHK
;
Are aged 18 or above;
Are a
native Cantonese speaker
; and
Have experience learning a second language (e.g., English).
2. What Will You Do?
Participants will be asked to:
Complete a brief
background questionnaire
; and
Participate in a
20–30-minute online interview
.
The interview will be informal and will mainly focus on your experiences and feelings related to second language learning.
3. Participation Reward
Participants who complete both the background questionnaire and the online interview will receive
HKD $50
as a token of appreciation for their time and contribution.
4. Limited Places and Deadline
Only a
small number of participants
will be recruited. Eligible participants will be contacted on a
first-come, first-served basis
, subject to the recruitment criteria.

Registration deadline: 20 August 2026
5. How to Participate
Please complete the brief background questionnaire and register your interest through the link below:
https://esurvey.psy.cuhk.edu.hk/jfe/form/SV_bE4IovsqrgWaTfo
Contact Us:
If you have any questions, please feel free to contact the research team:
zhenyizhou@cuhk.edu.hk
Thank you for your participation and support.
LEaPP Lab
Department of Educational Psychology
The Chinese University of Hong Kong

For enquiries, please write to:

bodyText:

[Register Now]  Jockey Club Sleep Well Project Finale cum International Conference 2026  - Department of Psychiatry
From: Winifred Wong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
jcsleepwell@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Dear Colleagues and Friends,
We cordially invite you and your colleagues to the Jockey Club Sleep Well Project Finale cum International Conference 2026 organized by the Department of Psychiatry, Faculty of Medicine, CUHK.
The conference will bring together sleep medicine specialists, academics, and frontline healthcare professionals to share the latest research and clinical advances. Through this conference, you will be equipped with evidence-based knowledge and practical skills in sleep health, with a focus on CBT-I directly from both local and world leaders. This conference brings us altogether to create strong interdisciplinary collaborations and promote coordinated, person-centered care for sleep health service users.
Conference Details
Date: 14 September 2026
Time: 11:00-18:30
Venue: LT1, Cheng Yu Tung Building, CUHK, Shatin, NT, HK
Format: In-Person or Zoom
Free Registration
Language: Primarily Conducted in English
Highlights
• Keynote lectures by internationally renowned sleep medicine experts, including Prof. Charles M. Morin, Prof. Yuichi Inoue, and Prof. Lin Lu.
• Cutting-edge research and clinical practice sharing on insomnia.
• Potential and challenges in integrating CBT-I community-based primary care with emerging technologies.
Accreditation
CPD (HKSWA, 4 Points) | CME (HKCPsych, 5 Points)
CEU (HKPS; Pending) | CME (HKAM & MCHK, 3-5 Points; Pending)
We appreciate your confirmation of attendance by 5 September 2026 via the following link:
https://forms.cloud.microsoft/r/w4AZhK5Lnm
For more details:
https://conference.jcsleepwell.com
If you have any inquiries or require assistance, please feel free to contact us. Looking forward to your participation!
Email: jcsleepwell@cuhk.edu.hk
Tel: 39710550
Best regards,

title: 【Earn HK$500 coupon】 Recruiting adults (aged 18-65) to participate in research on online therapy for insomnia 【可獲得 500元現金券】招募成年人 (18-65歲)參與失眠的數碼化治療研究
bodyText:

Announcements
【Earn HK$500 coupon】 Recruiting adults (aged 18-65) to participate in research on online therapy for insomnia 【可獲得 500元現金券】招募成年人 (18-65歲)參與失眠的數碼化治療研究 - Psychiatry
From: Charis
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
你是否經常在床上輾轉難眠，夜醒或早醒？你並不孤單——許多人都面臨著同樣的問題。我們誠邀您參與研究，讓專業數碼化治療助你改善睡眠！
研究目的
本研究旨在評估市民對數碼化失眠認知行為治療聊天機器人的遵從性，以及其對改善睡眠問題的效果。
治療方式
· 由專業臨床心理學家及精神科醫生設計的電子化治療
· 完全免費
參與資格
· 18至65歲能說廣東話流利溝通（能流利閱讀並理解廣東話）的香港居民
· 在過去一個月內，每週至少三晚出現睡眠困擾
· 最近四周或以上無需長期服藥
參與研究，獲得獎勵！
完成所有治療及後續測試後，您可獲得高達500港幣。
如何加入？
請點擊以下連結進行註冊，並回答幾條簡單問題。研究員將聯絡適合的參加者，詳細解釋研究內容：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4UPFh054GtJGXX0
聯絡我們
如有任何疑問，請於辦公時間內致電 6115-0322 與研究助理聯絡。
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Do you often toss and turn in bed, wake up frequently at night, or wake up too early? You are not alone—many people experience the same challenges. We invite you to participate in our study and explore professional digital treatment to improve your sleep!
Purpose of the Study
This research aims to evaluate the public’s adherence to a digital insomnia cognitive behavioural therapy chatbot and assess its effectiveness in improving sleep problems.
Treatment Method
· A professionally designed digital therapy created by clinical psychologists and psychiatrists
· Completely free of charge
Eligibility Criteria
· Hong Kong residents aged 18 to 65 who can speak in Cantonese fluently, read and understand Cantonese
· Experienced sleep disturbances at least 3 nights per week in the past month
· No need for long-term medication for the past four weeks or more.
Receive Rewards for Participating!
Upon completion of all treatment sessions and follow-up assessments, participants will receive up to HKD 500.
How to Join?
Click the link below to register and answer a few simple questions. Our researchers will contact suitable participants to provide further details:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4UPFh054GtJGXX0
Contact Us
If you have any questions, please call 6115-0322 during office hours to speak with our research assistants.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Department of Psychiatry is now recruiting Chinese Seniors with subjective cognitive decline to participate in a research study involving cognitive training.

Purpose
: Improve cognitive function and slow down neurodegeneration

Eligibility
:
55-75 years old
Right-handed
Experiencing subjective cognitive decline, but without dementia

Study Details
:
Randomly assigned to Calligraphy Practice or Health Education group
Training lasts for six months, with two hours per week, totaling fifty-two hours
Assessments before and after training (including MRI brain scan)
Training and assessments are free of charge

Location
: Chen Wai Wai Vivien Foundation Therapeutic Physical Mental Exercise Centre of the Chinese University of Hong Kong (next to Shek Mun Station)
Register NOW:
https://forms.gle/spTmzAPEQpUZRQPF9
For further enquiries, please contact Miss Kwok from the Department of Psychiatry, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, at 5506 1959 or
ontokwok@cuhk.edu.hk
. Thank you!

From: Reimagining Yung Shue Au

榕樹凹文化與沙頭角導賞及沙頭角公共圖書館分享
Yung Shue Au Cultural & Sha Tau Kok Tour and Sharing at Sha Tau Kok Public Library
活動詳情 / Activity Details
日期 / Date：2026年8月19日(星期三)  / 19 August 2026 (Wed)
時間 / Time ：1230 - 1600
地點 / Venue：榕樹凹、沙頭角及沙頭角公共圖書館 / Yung Shue Au, Sha Tau Kok and Sha Tau Kok Public Library
集合地點 / Meeting Point：沙頭角避風塘 Sha Tau Kok Typhoon Shelter
https://share.google/POni3sD7Hm9uTNH64
費用 / Fee：全免 / Free of charge
名額 / Quota：12
報名 / Registration
：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13737301
如活動受天氣影響而取消，將順延至一星期後（8月26日）舉行，其他安排維持不變。
If the event is cancelled due to adverse weather conditions, it will be postponed for one week (26 August 2026), while all other arrangements will remain unchanged.
About / 簡介:
中大建築學院將與沙頭角公共圖書館合辦「榕樹凹文化與沙頭角導賞 及 沙頭角公共圖書館分享活動」。參加者將先由榕樹凹文化大使帶領走訪榕樹凹，認識其當地文化與歷史景點。其後走訪沙頭角禁區，了解沙頭角禁區發展，再前往沙頭角公共圖書館，由助理館長江晉賢先生介紹與沙頭角及榕樹凹相關的館藏書籍，從不同角度加深對兩地文化與歷史的了解。分享環節更會介紹香港公共圖書館的電子書館藏，讓參加者可隨時隨地在線上閱讀。
The CUHK School of Architecture is collaborating with the Sha Tau Kok Public Library to present the “Yung Shue Au Cultural Guided Tour and Sha Tau Kok Public Library Sharing Session.” Participants will begin with a guided tour at Yung Shue Au, led by the Yung Shue Au Cultural Ambassadors, to explore the village’s local culture and historical landmarks. The tour will then continue to the Sha Tau Kok Frontier Closed Area, where participants will learn about the architecture and development of Sha Tau Kok. The programme will then continue at the Sha Tau Kok Public Library, where Assistant Librarian Mr. Alferd Kong Chun-yin will introduce library collections related to Sha Tau Kok and Yung Shue Au, offering deeper insights into the history and culture of both areas. The sharing session will also introduce the Hong Kong Public Libraries’ e book collections, enabling participants to access online reading resources anytime and anywhere.
注意 / Notice：
參加者需自行安排來往沙頭角之交通
Participants should arrange their own transportation to Sha Tau Kok。
參加者需自行上網申請邊境禁區許可證：
Participants must apply for the Closed Area Permit online themselves:
https://www.es.police.gov.hk/
是次活動是香港中文大學建築學院「重塑榕樹凹故事」項目的一部分，並由鄉郊保育辦公室、鄉郊保育資助計劃資助。
This activity is a part of "Re-telling the Yung Shue Au Story", a project by CUHK School of Architecture, sponsored by the  Countryside Conservation Office and Countryside Conservation Funding Scheme.

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

title: 【World Café：My second home, Hong Kong】 【世界咖啡館：香港 也是我家】
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/08/14
»
Events / Activities
【World Café：My second home, Hong Kong】  【世界咖啡館：香港 也是我家】 - School of Architecture
From: Happy Ageing Lab Foundation
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
kelvinchui@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【
World
Café:
My second home, Hong Kong
】
What was it like when you first arrived in Hong Kong? Exciting? Uncertain? Full of hope?
Living and working far from home is not always easy. There are language differences, cultural adjustments, and moments of homesickness. But there are also friendships, shared laughter, and small victories that make this city feel a little more familiar each day.
We invite  Non-Cantonese Speakers living in Hong Kong to join us for a warm and welcoming sharing gathering.
Come meet new friends, share your journey, and connect with others who understand your experience.
Different backgrounds. Different stories. One shared city.
Because no matter where we come from, Hong Kong can be our home too.⏱
【世界咖啡館：香港 也是我家】  圍埋傾計第三場
你剛到香港時是什麼樣的？ 興奮？ 不確定？ 充滿希望？
在離家很遠的地方生活和工作並不總是那麼容易。 有語言差異、文化適應和思鄉的時候。 但也有友誼、笑聲和得著，讓這座城市每天都感覺更加熟悉。
我們誠意邀請外藉居港人加入我們，共同參加這場溫暖的分享會。
來認識新朋友，分享你的旅程，並與和你有共同經歷的人聯繫。
不同的背景。 不同的故事。 一個共同的都市。⏱
What is World Café?
World Café is a discussion format that generates group wisdom through flexible small group discussions, sincere conversations, and relaxed atmosphere. It regards dialogue as a core process from a new perspective, creating a conversational context that encourages participants to open the conversation barrier, fully engage in dialogue, explore issues together, and develop deep thinking. During the conversation, participants not only express their own opinions, but more importantly, listen to the other person, and then recombine through connections to find new perspectives or blind spots that they have never noticed before, thereby forming consensus and insights, and finding new opportunities for action.
甚麼是世界咖啡館 (World Café) ？
世界咖啡館 (World Café) 是一種在輕鬆的氛圍中，透過彈性的小團體討論，真誠對話，產生團體智慧的討論方去式。它以全新的角度把對話當作一個核心流程，透過 匯談情境的營造，讓參加者都願意打開話閘子，全心投入對話，共同探索議題，發展深層思考。在談話的過程中，參與者不僅僅是表達自己看法，更重要的是聆聽對方，然後透過連結重新組合，找到新的觀點或從未察覺的盲點，進而形成共識與洞見，找到新的行動契機。
Event Information
◊ Date | August 28, 2026 (Friday)
◊ Time | 7pm to 9pm
◊ Location | Luk Heung Campus, Tai Po (Google Map：
https://maps.app.goo.gl/mPfJRAToYYokCJk59
）
◊ Target |   Non-Cantonese Speakers living in Hong Kong or any interested individuals!
◊ Quota | 8-20 people
◊ Fee | HK$50 (including light F&B)
◊ Registration |
https://forms.gle/6uearJM4sQqKiyEm6
If you have any inquiries, please feel free to check on WhatsApp+852 3943 6582.
||
Partner/Host:
Shirley Lam (@ worldcafecat): Shirley is a facilitation advocate dedicated to making it easier for others to learn and apply guidance. By writing the LinkedIn newsletter 'Facilitation Snippet' and hosting the World Café event, we aim to spark meaningful conversations. World Caf é CAT is a spontaneous community program that organizes "World Cafe" themed events in local small shops and spaces, allowing participants to participate in discussions, listen to their own ideas, stories of others, and gather collective wisdom while exploring and supporting the sustainable operation of community spaces. Since December 2023, over 65 events have been held.
合作夥伴/主持：
Shirley Lam (@worldcafecat)：Shirley是一位促進引導 (facilitation) 倡議者，致力於讓他人更容易學習與應用引導。透過撰寫 LinkedIn 電子報《Facilitation Snippet》，並主持世界咖啡（World Café）活動，以激發有意義的對話。World Café CAT是一個自發的社區計劃，透過在本地小店、空間舉辦不同主題的「世界咖啡館」(World Cafe) ，讓參加者參與討論，聆聽自己的想法、他人的故事，和凝聚大家的集體智慧之餘，發掘及支持社區空間的持續營運。由2023年12月開始，至今已舉辦超過 65場活動。
Note:
- Due to limited space in the venue, if there is a high demand for registration, we will allocate spots through random drawing.
- Successful applicants will receive a WhatsApp confirmation notification; If no response is received by then, it will be considered as unsuccessful registration.
- During the event, photography will be conducted for recording and promotional purposes, and attendees will be deemed to have agreed to the organizer's use of their portrait. The image copyright belongs to Luk Heung Commons.
備註：
- 場地空間有限，如報名踴躍，我們將以隨機抽籤方式分配名額。
- 成功報名者會收到 WhatsApp 確認通知；若屆時未收到回覆，則視為未能成功報名。
- 活動期間將進行攝錄作紀錄及宣傳用途，出席者即視為同意主辦機構使用其肖像。影像版權歸「Luk Heung Commons」所有。
⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐ ⭐
About the Project
關於計劃
Luk Heung Commons
is a 30-month culture-led placemaking project starting in at Luk Heung Campus, Tai Po. Funded by ZeShan Foundation, the project is delivered through a strategic collaboration between Happy Ageing Lab Foundation (HALF) and Evangelical Lutheran Church Social Service – Hong Kong (ELCSS-HK). The project aims to transform the existing Luk Heung Campus into Luk Heung Commons, a community hub that connects people, builds community capacity, and promotes well-being through creative, participatory means. Luk Heung Commons will serve as a collaborative platform for creative community-based practices to develop capacity and resources in the community for promoting positive neighbourhood transformation. This project represents the coming to life of a long-held vision: a physical and social space where residents can meet, create, share resources, and weave resilient bonds of mutual support and care.

From: Happy Ageing Lab Foundation
kelvinchui@cuhk.edu.hk

【
World
Café:
My second home, Hong Kong
】
What was it like when you first arrived in Hong Kong? Exciting? Uncertain? Full of hope?
Living and working far from home is not always easy. There are language differences, cultural adjustments, and moments of homesickness. But there are also friendships, shared laughter, and small victories that make this city feel a little more familiar each day.
We invite  Non-Cantonese Speakers living in Hong Kong to join us for a warm and welcoming sharing gathering.
Come meet new friends, share your journey, and connect with others who understand your experience.
Different backgrounds. Different stories. One shared city.
Because no matter where we come from, Hong Kong can be our home too.⏱
【世界咖啡館：香港 也是我家】  圍埋傾計第三場
你剛到香港時是什麼樣的？ 興奮？ 不確定？ 充滿希望？
在離家很遠的地方生活和工作並不總是那麼容易。 有語言差異、文化適應和思鄉的時候。 但也有友誼、笑聲和得著，讓這座城市每天都感覺更加熟悉。
我們誠意邀請外藉居港人加入我們，共同參加這場溫暖的分享會。
來認識新朋友，分享你的旅程，並與和你有共同經歷的人聯繫。
不同的背景。 不同的故事。 一個共同的都市。⏱
What is World Café?
World Café is a discussion format that generates group wisdom through flexible small group discussions, sincere conversations, and relaxed atmosphere. It regards dialogue as a core process from a new perspective, creating a conversational context that encourages participants to open the conversation barrier, fully engage in dialogue, explore issues together, and develop deep thinking. During the conversation, participants not only express their own opinions, but more importantly, listen to the other person, and then recombine through connections to find new perspectives or blind spots that they have never noticed before, thereby forming consensus and insights, and finding new opportunities for action.
甚麼是世界咖啡館 (World Café) ？
世界咖啡館 (World Café) 是一種在輕鬆的氛圍中，透過彈性的小團體討論，真誠對話，產生團體智慧的討論方去式。它以全新的角度把對話當作一個核心流程，透過 匯談情境的營造，讓參加者都願意打開話閘子，全心投入對話，共同探索議題，發展深層思考。在談話的過程中，參與者不僅僅是表達自己看法，更重要的是聆聽對方，然後透過連結重新組合，找到新的觀點或從未察覺的盲點，進而形成共識與洞見，找到新的行動契機。
Event Information
◊ Date | August 28, 2026 (Friday)
◊ Time | 7pm to 9pm
◊ Location | Luk Heung Campus, Tai Po (Google Map：
https://maps.app.goo.gl/mPfJRAToYYokCJk59
）
◊ Target |   Non-Cantonese Speakers living in Hong Kong or any interested individuals!
◊ Quota | 8-20 people
◊ Fee | HK$50 (including light F&B)
◊ Registration |
https://forms.gle/6uearJM4sQqKiyEm6
If you have any inquiries, please feel free to check on WhatsApp+852 3943 6582.
||
Partner/Host:
Shirley Lam (@ worldcafecat): Shirley is a facilitation advocate dedicated to making it easier for others to learn and apply guidance. By writing the LinkedIn newsletter 'Facilitation Snippet' and hosting the World Café event, we aim to spark meaningful conversations. World Caf é CAT is a spontaneous community program that organizes "World Cafe" themed events in local small shops and spaces, allowing participants to participate in discussions, listen to their own ideas, stories of others, and gather collective wisdom while exploring and supporting the sustainable operation of community spaces. Since December 2023, over 65 events have been held.
合作夥伴/主持：
Shirley Lam (@worldcafecat)：Shirley是一位促進引導 (facilitation) 倡議者，致力於讓他人更容易學習與應用引導。透過撰寫 LinkedIn 電子報《Facilitation Snippet》，並主持世界咖啡（World Café）活動，以激發有意義的對話。World Café CAT是一個自發的社區計劃，透過在本地小店、空間舉辦不同主題的「世界咖啡館」(World Cafe) ，讓參加者參與討論，聆聽自己的想法、他人的故事，和凝聚大家的集體智慧之餘，發掘及支持社區空間的持續營運。由2023年12月開始，至今已舉辦超過 65場活動。

Luk Heung Commons
is a 30-month culture-led placemaking project starting in at Luk Heung Campus, Tai Po. Currently enrolled student, preferably in
Computer Science, Information Systems, Design
, or related fields
Experience with UI/UX design tools (e.g., Figma) and/or mobile app development (iOS/Android, React Native, or Flutter)

bodyText:

The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Chung Chi College 75th Anniversary “Ink Echoes: A Shared Path with Kan Tai-keung and Students” 香港中文大學崇基學院七十五週年校慶「師我．我師 - 靳埭強師生畫展」 - Chung Chi College
From: Jennifer Ng
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
jenniferng@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
傳統水墨絕不沉悶。在孩童筆下，「點、線、面」化作游魚、花鳥與小屋，甚至能以破筆揮灑出流暢山水。當代水墨畫家和平面設計師靳埭強博士融匯東西方美學。近年，他將師承自香港「新水墨運動」奠基者呂壽琨的「師古、師自然、師我」心法，轉化為啟迪孩童的美學泉源，引導外孫女阮迎及多位小小藝術家觀察日常、大膽創新。
本次師生展以「師我．我師」為題，呈現靳博士的新作、學生佳作與教學心得，深刻體現大師與孩童互為老師、共同成長的「教學相長」精神。
展覽主題亦與崇基學院之育人理念互相呼應，學院致力推動全人教育，重視師生同行。適逢崇基創校七十五周年，學院特邀靳氏師生聯袂展出，作為校慶展覽之一。展覽既見證薪火相傳的精神，也寄託對未來的期盼，透過藝術啟迪創意、涵養人文。
Traditional ink is far from lifeless. Beneath a child’s playful brush, simple dots, lines, and washes bloom into darting fish and quiet cottages, while even a frayed brush sweeps across paper to release the flowing spirit of mountains and rivers.
Contemporary master Dr. Kan Tai-keung has long blended Eastern aesthetics with Western design thinking. Channelling the "learning from tradition, nature, and self" philosophy of New Ink Movement pioneer Lui Shou-kwan, he transforms it into a wellspring of inspiration, guiding his granddaughter, Xenia Yuen, and other young artists to observe the everyday and paint with boundless imagination.
Under the theme "Ink Echoes: A Shared Path" (師我．我師), this joint exhibition showcases Dr. Kan’s latest creations alongside student works, beautifully capturing the spirit of mutual learning and growth.
The theme of this exhibition also resonates deeply with Chung Chi College’s educational mission and commitment to whole-person development, where holistic education and the value of learning through teacher-student companionship have long been cherished. In celebration of Chung Chi College’s 75th Anniversary, the College is honoured to invite Dr. Kan and his students to present their works. Through this exhibition, the enduring spirit of generational continuity is brought to the fore, while aspirations for the future are reflected. Through art, the exhibition seeks to inspire creativity and cultivate humanistic values.

From: Donald Liu

donaldliu@cuhk.edu.hk

靜觀課程對有慢性壓力的長者的微生物群成效研究: 隨機對照試驗
Effects of mindfulness-based training on the microbiome of older adults with chronic stress: A randomised controlled trial
現正誠邀合資格人士報名參加
We are now recruiting participants to join our programme.
賽馬會公共衛生及基層醫療學院 現誠邀60歲以上人士參加一項靜觀課程研究
研究將會探討靜觀課程對有慢性壓力的長者的微生物群的影響。
很多長者受慢性壓力困擾，如未能適當處理壓力，對他們的心理及生理皆有嚴重影響。研究發現慢性壓力會破壞腸道微生物群的平衡。靜觀證實可有效改善心理健康，卻甚少研究探究靜觀課程如何改善參與者的微生物群。這項研究將在社區招募138名年滿60歲人士，邀請他們參與為長者而設的靜觀課程與健康教育控制課程，比較兩者於改善壓力、負面情緒及腸道微生物的成效。
參加者將會被隨機分派入兩組其中一組：
a) 靜觀練習組：
分派入本組的參加者將接受為期八周，每週一次，每次大約一小時三十分鐘的靜觀課程。每堂靜課程將會錄音，以作審視課程的保真度。
b) 健康教育組：
分派入本組的參加者會接受為期八周，每週一次，每次大約一小時三十分鐘的健康教育課程，課程內容包括營養，運動，維持生活習慣。每堂靜課程將會錄音，以作審視課程的保真度。
招募對象:
i) 年齡60歲以上;
ii) 能聽講廣東話;
iii) 需要持續照顧有長期病患的親屬;
iv) 照顧者負荷指數達 7分或以上;
v)沒有經醫生診斷有精神病患或認知問題;
vi) 沒有嚴重的身體或精神問題;
vi)不是正接受心理治療;
vii) 兩年內沒有參加過正規的靜觀課程;
viii) 被照顧親屬並非剛離世;
ix) 三個月內沒有使用抗生素或益生菌
課堂詳情
時間：10月尾開始 星期三或四的 上午
地點：沙田瀝源健康院 - 本活動共8節, 每週1次, 每次1.5小時
兩組參加者均須在課程開始前、結束後，及結束後3個月填寫共次3問卷調查及提供3次糞便樣本。
*費用全免*
參與是次研究不需繳付任何費用。
每次提供樣本及填寫問卷將會獲得價值$100 的現金卷，最高可獲300元現金卷。
歡迎將以上資訊廣傳給親朋好友。
如需了解更多本研究資訊或查詢，請聯絡：

電話：2252-8463  Whatsapp: 5264 6865

很多長者受慢性壓力困擾，如未能適當處理壓力，對他們的心理及生理皆有嚴重影響。研究發現慢性壓力會破壞腸道微生物群的平衡。靜觀證實可有效改善心理健康，卻甚少研究探究靜觀課程如何改善參與者的微生物群。這項研究將在社區招募138名年滿60歲人士，邀請他們參與為長者而設的靜觀課程與健康教育控制課程，比較兩者於改善壓力、負面情緒及腸道微生物的成效。
參加者將會被隨機分派入兩組其中一組：
a) 靜觀練習組：
分派入本組的參加者將接受為期八周，每週一次，每次大約一小時三十分鐘的靜觀課程。每堂靜課程將會錄音，以作審視課程的保真度。
b) 健康教育組：
分派入本組的參加者會接受為期八周，每週一次，每次大約一小時三十分鐘的健康教育課程，課程內容包括營養，運動，維持生活習慣。每堂靜課程將會錄音，以作審視課程的保真度。
招募對象:
i) 年齡60歲以上;
ii) 能聽講廣東話;
iii) 需要持續照顧有長期病患的親屬;
iv) 照顧者負荷指數達 7分或以上;
v)沒有經醫生診斷有精神病患或認知問題;
vi) 沒有嚴重的身體或精神問題;
vi)不是正接受心理治療;
vii) 兩年內沒有參加過正規的靜觀課程;
viii) 被照顧親屬並非剛離世;
ix) 三個月內沒有使用抗生素或益生菌
課堂詳情
時間：10月尾開始 星期三或四的 上午
地點：沙田瀝源健康院 - 本活動共8節, 每週1次, 每次1.5小時
兩組參加者均須在課程開始前、結束後，及結束後3個月填寫共次3問卷調查及提供3次糞便樣本。
*費用全免*
參與是次研究不需繳付任何費用。
每次提供樣本及填寫問卷將會獲得價值$100 的現金卷，最高可獲300元現金卷。
歡迎將以上資訊廣傳給親朋好友。
如需了解更多本研究資訊或查詢，請聯絡：
廖先生/魏先生 (研究助理)
電話：2252-8463  Whatsapp: 5264 6865
如有興趣參與研究，請使用以下連結報名。
報名：https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_8cu06nvBsZqwVBY
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

bodyText:

Announcements
[Earn up to HK$1100 cash] Recruiting participants aged 18 or above for Study on Sleep–Wake Patterns and Depressive Mood [最高可獲$1100現金] 誠邀18歲或以上人士參與作息模式與憂鬱情緒研究 - Psychology Department
From: Public Mental Health Laboratory
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
pmhlab@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -

【作息模式與憂鬱情緒研究】

成日夜晚瞓唔著，眼光光到天光？半夜又成日醒，醒咗又瞓唔返？
朝早覺得好倦，無動力去做野？又覺得情緒低落，無希望？
香港中文大學公共心理健康研究室現正進行一項有關作息型態及憂鬱情緒的研究。符合資格的參加者會於首4星期連續佩戴手錶式腕動計及完成評估問卷。 4星期後，研究人員會與參加者再次進行評估，符合資格的參加者將有機會獲得8-12節睡眠及作息治療，期間需要繼續佩戴手錶式腕動計及完成評估問卷。完成整個為期約14星期的研究後最高有機會總共獲得現金港幣$1100作為答謝金。
現誠邀符合以下條件的您參加研究：
18-65歲的香港居民
受憂鬱情緒及睡眠困擾的人士
能閱讀中文及理解廣東話
使用iOS/Android系統的智慧型電話
如有興趣參與，請填妥網上初步評估問卷（約5分鐘完成）：
https://esurvey.psy.cuhk.edu.hk/jfe/form/SV_ey6IheYeo7CLhRQ
研究人員將以電話/WhatsApp聯絡符合資格的參與者參加研究，並解釋研究計畫詳情。
如果有任何問題或想了解更多，歡迎與研究人員聯絡！
電話：3943 6575
WhatsApp：9405 4715
電郵：pmhlab@cuhk.edu.hk / evanpcy99@link.cuhk.edu.hk
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Study on Sleep–Wake Patterns and Depressive Mood

Do you often have trouble falling asleep at night?
Do you wake up frequently during the night and find it difficult to fall back asleep?
Do you feel exhausted in the morning and lack motivation to do things?
Do you often feel low in mood or hopeless?
The
Public Mental Health Laboratory at The Chinese University of Hong Kong
is conducting a research study on
sleep-wake patterns and depressive mood
.
Eligbible participants will be required to wear a
watch-type actigraphy device continuously for the first 4 weeks
and complete assessment surveys.
After 4 weeks, participants will undergo another assessment. Those who remain eligible may receive
8–12 sessions of sleep and circadian rhythm therapy
, during which they will continue wearing the actigraphy device and completing questionnaires.
Participants who complete the entire study (approximately
14 weeks
) may receive
up to HKD $1,100 in cash
as a token of appreciation.
We are now inviting individuals who meet the following criteria
Hong Kong residents aged 18–65
Experience depressive mood and sleep difficulties
Able to read Chinese and understand Cantonese
Use a smartphone with iOS or Android operating system
If you are interested, please complete the online preliminary screening questionnaire (about 5 minutes):
https://esurvey.psy.cuhk.edu.hk/jfe/form/SV_ey6IheYeo7CLhRQ
Research staff will contact eligible participants via
phone or WhatsApp
to explain the study details.
If you have any questions or would like to know more, feel free to contact us:
Phone: 3943 6575
WhatsApp: 9405 4715
Email: pmhlab@cuhk.edu.hk / evanpcy99@link.cuhk.edu.hk
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

/weekly/

2026-2027 Voluntary User-Pay Dental Service Scheme (VUPDSS)
Voluntary User-Pay Dental Service Scheme (VUPDSS) is a voluntary and self-paid dental service between the University’s members and the service providers, Health & Care Dental Services Limited and Quality HealthCare Dental Services Limited. Its primary purpose is to provide participants the additional convenience of receiving dental service at contracted dental clinics outside campus at concessionary rate. Full-time students, full-time staff and dependents, eligible retirees and dependents can enroll in the Scheme. The Scheme is open for application. Membership is valid from 1 September 2026 to 31 August 2027.
Details of the Scheme is available at:
https://www.umso.cuhk.edu.hk/form-download/
2026-2027 自費牙科服務計劃
「自費牙科服務計劃」為一個自願性付費形式的牙齒保健計劃。 合資格大學成員可參加由恒健牙科服務有限公司及卓健牙科服務有限公司所提供的牙科保健服務。 本計劃旨在為參加者提供一個具彈性及享有優惠價格之牙科服務。 全日制學生、全職職員及家屬、合資格退休員工及家屬均可參加。 計劃現正接受申請，會籍有效期由2026年9月1日至2027年8月31日。
計劃詳情，請瀏覽網頁:

[Co-op@CUHK Student Stories: Different Paths, Shared Growth!]
By bridging the gap between academic knowledge and real-world practice, the Co-operative Education Programme (Co-op@CUHK) enables students to gain hands-on experience across diverse industries, explore opportunities beyond their degree disciplines, and even take their learning beyond Hong Kong through non-local placements.
Whether you already have a clear career aspiration or are still exploring future possibilities, Co-op@CUHK offers a unique platform to discover your potential and develop professional competencies.
Check out the stories of our Co-op students and see how one experience can open doors to new opportunities, perspectives and possibilities for your future!
1. Turning Classroom Knowledge into Real-World Practice
2. Exploring Beyond My Major & Discovering New Possibilities
3.
Learning Without Borders with Co-op Non-Local Placements
Inspired by Co-op students’ experiences? Now it's your turn to create your own Co-op story! Whether you aspire to put your learning into practice, broaden your horizons beyond your field of study, or challenge yourself through a non-local placement, the Co-op Programme offers opportunities to grow both personally and professionally!
Applications for the 6th Co-op@CUHK cohort are now open.
Apply here
and take the first step towards an unforgettable learning journey. Students from all disciplines, both local and non-local, are eligible to apply!
If you have any questions regarding the Co-op Programme, feel free to reach out to our team at
coop@cuhk.edu.hk
or call 3943 5674 / 3943 1422. We look forward to receiving your application!

Weed Removal in the College Piazza (18 August 2026)
The weed removal and treatment at the College Piazza are scheduled for
18 August 2026 (Tuesday).
This treatment is part of our ongoing efforts to manage the weed growth and maintain a clean environment.
On the day of the treatment, warning signs will be placed around the Piazza and at the main entrance driveway while the service provider applies the weed control chemical.  The College Piazza
will be blocked from 2:00 pm to 6:30 pm on 18 August 2026 (Tuesday).
No vehicles except those pre-registered with the College Office will be allowed to enter or park at the College Piazza during this time.
For your safety, we kindly request that all individuals and pets refrain from entering the treated areas and avoid any direct contact with the surfaces for at least 24 hours following the completion of the work on 18 August 2026.

Location:

bodyText:

Announcements
Student Helpers Recruitment – School Liaison and Research Support  - SYEEM
From: Frankie Wong
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
frankiewong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
JC GoAI
JC GoAI is a city-wide education project created and funded by The Hong Kong Jockey Club Charities Trust, in collaboration with the Chinese University of Hong Kong. In an era where generative AI is reshaping how we learn and work, JC GoAI aims to empower teachers to teach confidently using AI for all subjects, while nurturing AI literacy in students and cultivating them to learn creatively, effectively, and responsibly. With a comprehensive project design that emphasizes the ethical use of AI, we are ready to empower schools, teachers, and students to thrive in tomorrow’s AI-driven world. (Learn More: https://www.jcgoai.hk/). We are recruiting student helpers to provide school liaison and research support for the project.
Responsibilities:
Contact schools, teachers, students, and other project participants by telephone for project coordination and follow-up
Transcribe interview and research data in Cantonese, Chinese, or English
Assist with data cleaning, checking, matching, and the identification of missing, duplicated, or inconsistent records
Provide related research and administrative support as assigned
Maintain the confidentiality of all project and participant information
Requirements:
Current full-time undergraduate or postgraduate student at CUHK
Good command of spoken Cantonese and written Chinese and English
Clear and professional telephone communication skills
Careful attention to detail and the ability to work accurately with transcripts and datasets
Basic proficiency in Microsoft Excel or similar data-processing software
Student helper registration is required. Non-local students must hold a valid No Objection Letter
Immediate availability is preferred
Working Arrangement and Remuneration:
Flexible working hours, subject to the University's requirements
HKD 64 per hour
Application:
Please email your curriculum vitae and any relevant supporting documents to Dr. Liang at
siyaliang@cuhk.edu.hk

https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Seminars / Forums / Programmes / Workshops
The Independent Learning Centre (ILC) offers a wide range of workshops and activities to support learning of language and communication skills. Visit our website for more information: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ (20260817)  - ILC
From: ILC
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ilc-counsel@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【Weekly Highlights - English Section 】
A. Communication, Study Skills and Job Preparation Workshops
The Independent Learning Centre offers English workshops 17 August to 21 August: (1) Job Preparation Series: Writing Impressive Resumes, (2) Job Preparation Series: Writing Impressive Application Letters, (3) Saying What You Mean - English Pronunciation for Cantonese and Mandarin Speakers, (4) Academic Reading: Strategies for Success, and (5) Job Preparation Series: Ace Your In-person and Video Job Interviews. These workshops are now available for registration at: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/workshops.aspx
B. Consultation Service in English
Consultation service is available during the following time:
17 August (Mon): 14:30 – 16:30
18 August (Tue): 10:30 – 12:30
19 August (Wed): 14:30 – 16:30
20 August (Thu): 10:30 – 12:30
21 August (Fri): 14:30 – 16:30
Online Booking:
https://ilccuhk.as.me/schedule.php
More Timeslot please check our website：
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EH/consultation.aspx
====================================
【Weekly Highlights - Chinese Section 】中文部本週活動
A. Chinese Workshops 中文工作坊
The Independent Learning Centre offers Chinese workshops 17 August to 21 August: (1) JRE Argumentative Writing I, (2) Academic Writing: Research Proposal (PTH), (3) Grammar for the CRE, and (4) Self- Learning Cantonese II. These workshops are now available for registration at: https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/workshops.aspx
自學中心八月十七日至八月二十一日舉辦 (1) 古今一揆——古代中國思想與現代生活 (粵), (2) JRE 議論文寫作 (一), (3) 學術寫作：如何編撰研究計劃 (普), (4) 公務員綜合招聘試系列(CRE)：病句分析基礎, 及 (5) 自學粵語 (二)等工作坊，歡迎報名。
登記連結： https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/workshops.aspx
B. Consultation Service in Chinese 自學中心中文輔導服務
Consultation service is available during the following time:
自學中心於八月十七日至八月二十一日提供以下中文輔導時段。
17 August (Mon): 10:30 – 12:30
18 August (Tue): 14:30 – 16:30
19 August (Wed): 10:30 – 12:30
20 August (Thu): 10:30 – 12:30 and 14:30 – 16:30
網上預約：
https://ilccuhk.as.me/schedule.php
更多中文輔導時段。
====================================
C. “The Power of Words” 「書寫力量」
This is a reading and writing event organized by the ILC, Hong Kong Literature Research Centre, the Office of Arts Administrator (OAA) and Tolopoem. Activities we have this semester include Blackboard / Glass Wall Poems, Talks of Dialogue in the Arts and Workshops.
自學中心、香港文學研究中心、藝術行政主任辦公室及吐露詩社合辦的大型閱讀及寫作活動。這個學期的活動，除黑板詩及玻璃詩外，還有藝文縱談及各式工作坊。各項活動的資料可以參看：https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/Event/thepowerofwords.aspx
====================================
【Independent Online Learning Resources】自學中心網上自學資源
A. Independent Online Learning Resources in English
- Academic Writing
Visit this link on academic writing skills and convention for different citation styles:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/Writing_Writing.aspx
- Vocabulary
Visit this link for both General Vocabulary and Specific Vocabulary (e.g. For Business and Medical Professionals) lists and practices:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/Writing_Vocab.aspx
- Job Search and Interviews
Visit this link to identify your capabilities and personality types, learn how to prepare job search documents and personal statements, and how to get ready for job interviews:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/JobSearching.aspx
B. Independent Online Learning Resources in Chinese中文網上自學材料
- Academic Writing論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on academic writing, with highlights on structure, expressions, common grammatical mistakes, etc.
針對大學生撰寫學術論文時所遇到的困難，提供實用的知識和練習。內容包括：學期論文的結構與寫作步驟、常見語法錯誤、表達與語言邏輯等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/AWOnline/general1.html
- ‘Pulewang’ Online Putonghua Platform「普樂網」網上普通話平台
An online Putonghua learning platform designed for CU students. Essential knowledge of Putonghua is introduced with interactive exercises and games. Extended conversational exchanges on selected topics of social affairs and student life are available for oral practice with texts and pinyin.
針對本校同學學習需要的網上普通話平台，內容圍繞大學生的學習與日常生活，設計深入淺出，每單元均有練習與遊戲，互動有趣，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Chinese/plw/index.html
- Argumentative Writing議論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on the structure, the content and the language of argumentative writing.
介紹議論文的結構及寫作要求，以解說、例子及練習，呈現寫作議論時要注意的內容及語言特點：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/arguWriting/001.html
- Cantonese Pronunciation粵語拼音速遞
This guide is designed for mainland students as an effective way to learn Cantonese pronunciation. Basic knowledge of Cantonese syllables is introduced with exercises. Comparison of Cantonese and Putonghua pronunciation is also highlighted
協助內地同學迅速掌握粵語發音。內容包括：語音基礎、粵普對比、難點練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/cantontones/_home/index.html
- Cantonese Express港式粵語速遞
An interactive introduction to Hong Kong style Cantonese. Daily expressions and situational conversations are introduced with interactive exercises.
以有趣互動的方式介紹港式粵語，包括日常生活用語、情景會話、互動練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/canton_express/others/frontpage.html
- Online Cantonese for Foreigners
A free online platform for international students to learn basic Cantonese. The texts are clear and simple, and interactive exercises easy to use: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/can_eng/layout.html
- Online Putonghua for Foreigners
Do you know how to make orders in a Chinese restaurant and learn how to bargain when you travel in China? Here are some situational conversations and basic knowledge of Putonghua to learn online: https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/CHResources/Lang_PTH_EnglishSpk.aspx
- Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) 中國語言及文化自學資源網
Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) is a biliterate (English and Chinese) online platform that contains reviews of learning materials suitable for autodidactic study in the 5 big areas of Mandarin, Cantonese, Chinese Characters, Chinese Culture, and Hong Kong Culture. Electronic learning materials that is good for self-learning would be review. Each review consists of a description and other useful information. Users can search for resources by various criteria, rate the resources, and write their own comments. A self-assessment system is also provided so as to recommend an entry point to the users according to their current level.
中國語言及文化自學資源網(OPSCL)為一推薦自學資源之網上平台。平台為有意學習普通話、粵語、漢字、中國文化或香港文化等五大範疇的人士提供中文及英文雙語之學習資源，以推動自主學習與終身學習。平台內推薦的資源均附有簡介及評語，使用者可按自身需要搜尋學習資源，並在使用後給予評分或評論，以備其他使用者參考。此外，平台設有「自評系統」，使用者可通過完成自評，確定自身的學習起步點，從而尋找適合自己程度的學習資源。
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Workshop/ChineseLanguageAndCulture/EN/index.aspx
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Workshop/ChineseLanguageAndCulture/TC/index.aspx
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Workshop/ChineseLanguageAndCulture/SC/index.aspx
====================================
Contact us 聯絡我們
The Independent Learning Centre  自學中心
Address: Wu Chung Library, United College
Tel. No.：3943-8733 / 3943-8764
E-mail：ilc-counsel@cuhk.edu.hk
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

To prepare for the new academic year, remember to check or upgrade your personal green gear and take action to support CUHK’s waste reduction and sustainability efforts.

Reusable water bottle–Make use of campus water stations and say no to single‑use bottled water

From: Queenie Chow
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
literacy@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
誠邀閣下與子女參與一項關於華語兒童中英數能力的跨學科大型研究，詳情如下：
對象：
幼稚園高班至六年級單生兒和雙胞胎學生（包括同卵雙生和異卵雙生）
學童家長
學童需以廣東話為母語，並在香港居住 2.5 年以上
目的：
建立學童在中、英文讀寫和數學能力發展的多模態模型，以及設計能夠全面反映兒童在這三方面表現的網上測試工具
研究內容：
第一部分
學童：中英文和數學能力的測試
，分成網上測試和面對面測試兩部分。網上測試分為六個區域，各需時約40分鐘。網上測試毋須一次完成，參加者可自行安排時間分段執行，在四星期內完成所有項目即可。
面對面測試在網上測試完成後另約時間進行，約需45分鐘
家長：
在網上測試平台接受
約
15
分鐘的語文及數學測試
，及填寫關於學童學習情況與家庭語言環境的
問卷
*
現在報名的幼稚園高班至六年級學童只需完成今年一次測試
第二部分（可選擇是否參與）
學童：腦電圖測試（EEG），約2小時
報酬：每年測試完結後將收到：
(1) 測試結果的個人報告；(2) 港幣200元超級市場現金券；(3) 小禮物，
參與腦電圖 (EEG) 部份的學生另有250元超級市場現金券
研究詳情及報名請見以下網頁：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4OWk4Rmnmb0M20e
如對是項研究有任何疑問或查詢，歡迎聯絡本項目的首席研究員Urs Maurer教授（電郵: umaurer@cuhk.edu.hk）或研究小組（電話：3943-4379；電郵：
lifespandevlab.cuhk@gmail.com
）。
We are recruiting for a multi-disciplinary study about the Chinese, English, and Mathematical abilities among Chinese-speaking children in Hong Kong. Details are as below:
Target participants:
Singletons and twins (both identical and fraternal) from K3 to P6 in the 2025/26 school year
Students’ parents
The child participant must be a native Cantonese speaker and have lived in Hong Kong for more than 2.5 years.
Content:
Part 1
Students
: A series of assessments on Chinese, English, and mathematics on the project’s online testing platform. The tasks are divided into six portions; each takes about 40 minutes to finish. Online testing can be completed at your own pace, as long as all tasks are completed within 4 weeks.
A follow-up face-to-face session (45 minutes) will be arranged upon completion of the online testing.
Parents
: Short online testing on language and mathematics abilities (15 minutes), as well as a set of questionnaires on children’s learning and home language environment
*For current registration
s, students from K3 to P6 only need to complete the test once this year.
Part 2 (optional)
Students: electroencephalography (EEG) test (~2 hour)
Rewards: After each round of testing, participants will receive:
(1) Personal performance report; (2) $200 supermarket vouchers; (3) a gift (for students); EEG participants will receive an additional $250 worth of supermarket vouchers
The details of the study and the registration form can be found in the following link:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4OWk4Rmnmb0M20e
Should you have any enquiries, please contact Prof. Urs Maurer, the principle investigator (umaurer@cuhk.edu.hk) or the research team (3943-4379 or lifespandevlab.cuhk@gmail.com).

title: [Opportunity to get $50 Coupon!] Lung Cancer Screening Study for High-Risk Non-Smokers — Call for Participants 【有機會獲得價值 $50 禮券！】高危非吸煙者肺癌篩查研究 — 問卷招募
bodyText:

Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/08/14
»
Announcements
[Opportunity to get $50 Coupon!] Lung Cancer Screening Study for High-Risk Non-Smokers — Call for Participants 【有機會獲得價值 $50 禮券！】高危非吸煙者肺癌篩查研究 — 問卷招募 - The Jockey Club School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: Sammi Ng
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
samming001@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學醫學院腫瘤學系及賽馬會公共衛生及基層醫療學院現正進行一項研究，通過問卷探討香港市民對肺癌篩查及人工智能（AI）輔助肺癌篩查的知識、態度、需求、接受程度、促成因素與障礙。
只要你符合以下條件，就可以填寫問卷並獲得價值50元的現金券：
參加資格：
年齡介乎 50–75 歲
吸煙 (或一生中吸少於 100 支煙，不計算二手煙)
從未參與「香港中文大學醫學院腫瘤學系高危非吸煙者肺癌篩查研究」
父母、兄弟姊妹或子女擁有肺癌的疾病史
報名方式：
請點擊以下連結填寫網上問卷及報名，或直接掃描附圖的 QR Code：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_9Kp7c92ozYqJf3U
【請幫忙轉發】
歡迎將此訊息轉發給你的親友或相熟群組，一個簡單的轉發，就能幫助大學研究在香港推行AI輔助肺癌篩查！再次感謝你對研究的支持
The Department of Clinical Oncology at CUHK’s Faculty of Medicine, in collaboration with the Jockey Club School of Public Health and Primary Care, is currently conducting a study to explore Hong Kong citizens' knowledge, attitudes, needs, acceptance, facilitators, and barriers regarding lung cancer screening and Artificial Intelligence (AI)-assisted screening.
If you meet the criteria below, you are invited to complete the questionnaire and receive a HK$50 voucher:
Eligibility:
Aged between 50 and 75.
Non-smoker (or have smoked fewer than 100 cigarettes in your lifetime, excluding secondhand smoke).
Have never participated in the "CUHK Faculty of Medicine Lung Cancer Screening Study for High-Risk Non-Smokers."
Have a family history of lung cancer (parent, sibling, or child).
How to Participate:
Please click the link below to complete the online questionnaire and register, or scan the QR code in the attached image:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_9Kp7c92ozYqJf3U
Please Share!
We would appreciate it if you could forward this message to your friends, family, or relevant groups. A simple share helps support our university’s mission to implement AI-assisted lung cancer screening in Hong Kong. Thank you once again for your support of this research.

bodyText:

Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students

Announcements
Participant Recruitment: Intervention Study on Health Coaching and Wearable Devices 參加者招募：健康指導及可穿戴裝置介入研究 - Department of Sports Science and Physical Education
From: Hanwen Zhang
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ham.zhang@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
參加者招募：健康指導及可穿戴裝置介入研究
香港大學（港大）Youngwon Kim教授正與香港中文大學（中大）楊懌健教授合作，招募中央肥胖的成年人士參與研究。本研究旨在探討可穿戴裝置功能及健康指導對活動行為與心臟代謝風險因素的影響。
參與研究包括甚麼？
前往實驗室三次。每次到訪包括約1小時的評估，例如收集人口統計資料、量度血壓、抽取血液樣本及填寫問卷。
在指定研究期間連續24小時佩戴研究級可穿戴裝置。
接受其中一種介入方案：僅使用Fitbit可穿戴裝置功能，或使用相同功能並在一年內接受至少22節健康指導課程。
在約20個月內完成整個研究方案。
參與研究可能帶來甚麼益處？
了解心臟代謝疾病，並提供建議的生活方式調整。
獲得有助了解個人健康及體適能狀況的報告，包括Fitbit數據及血脂分析。
完成整個研究方案後，可獲港幣500元超市禮券。
哪些人士可能符合參加資格？
如您符合以下全部條件，便可能具備參加資格：
東亞裔，年齡為40歲或以上。
腰圍達90厘米或以上（男性），或80厘米或以上（女性）。
現時的體能活動量未達世界衞生組織建議水平。
使用智能手機。
能以中文或英文溝通。
能夠進行一般日常生活活動。
現時並未參與其他改變生活方式的研究或運動計劃。
如何登記或查詢更多資料？
如您有興趣參加，請聯絡研究團隊。
電話／
WhatsApp
：
52447300
電郵：
pastudy@hku.hk
實驗室地址：
香港薄扶林沙宣道5號賽馬會跨學科研究大樓3樓305室運動生理學實驗室。
抽血注意事項：
抽血前須禁食8小時，即不可進食或飲用任何飲品，包括茶、咖啡及酒精；期間可以飲用清水。
如有查詢，請透過上述聯絡方法與Youngwon Kim教授及港大研究團隊聯絡。歡迎您將此招募資料轉發予可能符合參加資格的人士。
Participant Recruitment: Intervention Study on Health Coaching and Wearable Devices
Professor Youngwon Kim at The University of Hong Kong (HKU), in collaboration with Professor Yijian Yang at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK), is recruiting adults with central obesity. The study will examine how wearable-device functions and health coaching affect movement behaviours and cardiometabolic risk factors.
What does participation involve?
Attend three laboratory visits. Each visit includes an approximately 1-hour assessment, such as collecting demographic information, measuring blood pressure, drawing blood, and administering questionnaires.
Wear a research-grade wearable device continuously for 24 hours during designated study periods.
Receive one of two interventions: Fitbit-based wearable functions alone, or the same wearable functions combined with at least 22 health-coaching sessions delivered over 1 year.
Complete the full study protocol over approximately 20 months.
What are the potential benefits?
Learn about cardiometabolic diseases and recommended lifestyle changes.
Receive reports that may help you understand your health and fitness status, including Fitbit data and a lipid profile.
Receive an HK$500 supermarket coupon after completing the full study protocol.
Who may be eligible?
You may be eligible if you meet all the following criteria:
Are East Asian and aged 40 years or above.
Have a waist circumference of at least 90 cm (men) or at least 80 cm (women).
Do not currently meet the World Health Organization-recommended levels of physical activity.
Use a smartphone.
Can communicate in Chinese or English.
Can perform usual activities of daily living.
Are not currently participating in another lifestyle-change research study or exercise programme.
How can I register or obtain more information?
If you are interested, please contact the research team.
Phone/WhatsApp:
52447300
E-mail:
pastudy@hku.hk
Laboratory address:
Exercise Physiology Lab (Room 305), 3/F, Jockey Club Building for Interdisciplinary Research, 5 Sassoon Road, Pokfulam, Hong Kong.
Important note for blood collection:
An 8-hour fast is required before the phlebotomy session. This means no food or drinks, including tea, coffee and alcohol. Water may be consumed freely.

Participant Recruitment: Intervention Study on Health Coaching and Wearable Devices 參加者招募：健康指導及可穿戴裝置介入研究 - Department of Sports Science and Physical Education
From: Hanwen Zhang
ham.zhang@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
參加者招募：健康指導及可穿戴裝置介入研究
香港大學（港大）Youngwon Kim教授正與香港中文大學（中大）楊懌健教授合作，招募中央肥胖的成年人士參與研究。本研究旨在探討可穿戴裝置功能及健康指導對活動行為與心臟代謝風險因素的影響。
參與研究包括甚麼？
前往實驗室三次。每次到訪包括約1小時的評估，例如收集人口統計資料、量度血壓、抽取血液樣本及填寫問卷。
在指定研究期間連續24小時佩戴研究級可穿戴裝置。
接受其中一種介入方案：僅使用Fitbit可穿戴裝置功能，或使用相同功能並在一年內接受至少22節健康指導課程。
在約20個月內完成整個研究方案。
參與研究可能帶來甚麼益處？
了解心臟代謝疾病，並提供建議的生活方式調整。
獲得有助了解個人健康及體適能狀況的報告，包括Fitbit數據及血脂分析。
完成整個研究方案後，可獲港幣500元超市禮券。
哪些人士可能符合參加資格？
如您符合以下全部條件，便可能具備參加資格：
東亞裔，年齡為40歲或以上。
腰圍達90厘米或以上（男性），或80厘米或以上（女性）。
現時的體能活動量未達世界衞生組織建議水平。
使用智能手機。
能以中文或英文溝通。
能夠進行一般日常生活活動。
現時並未參與其他改變生活方式的研究或運動計劃。
如何登記或查詢更多資料？
如您有興趣參加，請聯絡研究團隊。
電話／
WhatsApp
：
52447300
電郵：
pastudy@hku.hk
實驗室地址：
香港薄扶林沙宣道5號賽馬會跨學科研究大樓3樓305室運動生理學實驗室。
抽血注意事項：
抽血前須禁食8小時，即不可進食或飲用任何飲品，包括茶、咖啡及酒精；期間可以飲用清水。
如有查詢，請透過上述聯絡方法與Youngwon Kim教授及港大研究團隊聯絡。歡迎您將此招募資料轉發予可能符合參加資格的人士。
Participant Recruitment: Intervention Study on Health Coaching and Wearable Devices
Professor Youngwon Kim at The University of Hong Kong (HKU), in collaboration with Professor Yijian Yang at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK), is recruiting adults with central obesity. The study will examine how wearable-device functions and health coaching affect movement behaviours and cardiometabolic risk factors.
What does participation involve?
Attend three laboratory visits. Each visit includes an approximately 1-hour assessment, such as collecting demographic information, measuring blood pressure, drawing blood, and administering questionnaires.
Wear a research-grade wearable device continuously for 24 hours during designated study periods.
Receive one of two interventions: Fitbit-based wearable functions alone, or the same wearable functions combined with at least 22 health-coaching sessions delivered over 1 year.
Complete the full study protocol over approximately 20 months.
What are the potential benefits?
Learn about cardiometabolic diseases and recommended lifestyle changes.
Receive reports that may help you understand your health and fitness status, including Fitbit data and a lipid profile.
Receive an HK$500 supermarket coupon after completing the full study protocol.
Who may be eligible?
You may be eligible if you meet all the following criteria:
Are East Asian and aged 40 years or above.
Have a waist circumference of at least 90 cm (men) or at least 80 cm (women).
Do not currently meet the World Health Organization-recommended levels of physical activity.
Use a smartphone.
Can communicate in Chinese or English.
Can perform usual activities of daily living.
Are not currently participating in another lifestyle-change research study or exercise programme.
How can I register or obtain more information?
If you are interested, please contact the research team.

Exercise Physiology Lab (Room 305), 3/F, Jockey Club Building for Interdisciplinary Research, 5 Sassoon Road, Pokfulam, Hong Kong.
Important note for blood collection:
An 8-hour fast is required before the phlebotomy session. This means no food or drinks, including tea, coffee and alcohol. Water may be consumed freely.

Preliminary evidence has suggested a synergistic interaction effect of intermittent dieting (INTD) and high intensity interval exercise (HIIE) on cardio-metabolic health and weight loss. This study aims to examine the effects of INTD and HIIE and intermittent dieting for cardiometabolic and cardiovascular fitness in physically inactive adults with central obesity.

(The application below is conducted in Chinese only.)
日期：2026年8月28日（星期五）
時間：下午12時半至2時
地點：香港中文大學利黃瑤璧樓5樓505室
語言：廣東話
免費登記：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13738179
講者：張順光先生（香港收藏家協會前會長）
講座簡介：
收藏向來是一種怡情養性的嗜好。現今全球最普及的收藏活動是集郵，其次是鈔票及錢幣收藏。自1992年區域市政局邀請張順光先生和同好舉辦明信片展覽後，香港收藏明信片的風氣逐漸興盛，而現於全球位列第四。
是次講座，張先生將以個人經驗為主軸，分享其四十多年的收藏生涯，以及在拍賣場上既驚險又刺激的經歷。回顧多年的收藏心得，張先生歸納出一個問題：究竟怎樣才能成為一名收藏家？他認為收藏家須具備四項基本條件：知識、金錢、時間和緣份。而當中最重要的就是緣份，因為縱然具備其他三項條件，若欠缺緣份，終究也只是有緣無份。
講者簡介：
張順光先生，工商管理碩士，註冊為英國特許土木工程測量師學會資深會員、英國皇家特許測量師學會會員、香港測量師學會會員、香港地產行政師學會會員。香港收藏家協會前會長，香港藏書票協會會員，中國郵學會及香港郵學會會員。著作有《香港電車》、《明信片上的香港：1950’s-1990’s遊樂時光》。合著作品包括《香港歷史明信片精選》、《香港明信片精選1940’s-1970’s》、《消失中的城市建築：香港歷史圖像精選1880s-1990s》、《坐困愁城：日佔香港的大眾生活》、《遊歷港島：香港電車軌跡》、《有瓦遮頭》及《點紙咁簡單：趣談香港紙本藏品》等。

根據衛生署數據，前列腺癌是本港男性常見的癌症之一。透過及早篩查，可以有效降低相關的健康風險。本次活動由中大何善衡泌尿中心舉辦，為合資格人士提供免費的前列腺特異抗原 (PSA) 檢測服務。
活動地點： 沙田區（詳細地址將於成功報名後通知）
活動內容：(所需時間約一小時)
1. 影片講解：深入淺出地介紹前列腺增生及前列腺癌的檢查與治療知識。
2. 前列腺篩查：合資格人士可獲免費前列腺特異抗原（PSA）測試乙次.
• 測試方式：我們將以指尖採血方式為參加者抽取血液樣本，並透過PSA檢測機進行現場測試，約十分鐘即可得知結果。
參加資格：
• 性別：男性
• 年齡：50-75歲
• 從未接受前列腺相關檢查

From: Alice Kwok & Henry Lip
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155211477@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
各位好：
我們是香港中文大學公共衞生學的本科生 Henry 和 Alice。誠邀您參與我們的問卷調查，主題為「市民對醫院管理局公營醫療收費調整的態度研究」。
本問卷適用於年滿18歲或以上的香港永久性居民，預計需時約5分鐘。參與純屬自願，所有回覆將絕對保密，本研究亦已獲香港中文大學調查與行為研究倫理委員會批准。
請按以下連結參與：
https://forms.gle/jLx3S8mz1RxmwQdaA
感謝您的支持！
研究員一
Alice Kwok
1155211477@link.cuhk.edu.hk
研究員二
Henry Lip
1155202625@link.cuhk.edu.hk
香港中文大學
賽馬會公共衞生及基層醫療學院
Greetings,
We are Henry and Alice, Public Health undergraduate students at CUHK. We sincerely invite you to participate in our survey on “A Study on Public Attitudes Towards the Hospital Authority's Public Healthcare Fee Adjustment”.
The survey is open to Hong Kong permanent residents aged 18+ and takes about 5 minutes. Participation is voluntary, all responses are confidential, and the study is approved by the CUHK Survey and Behavioural Research Ethics Committee.
Please click the link below to participate:
https://forms.gle/jLx3S8mz1RxmwQdaA
Thank you for your support!
Regards,

title: [Max. HKD$1200] Recruiting Native Cantonese-speaking Grandparents with hearing loss and Grandchildren for an Interaction Experiment [長者認知及聽力測試報告👂 + 兒童IQ智商測試報告🧠] 招募聽力損失長者及其孫子女參與互動實驗
bodyText:

Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/08/14
»
Announcements
[Max. HKD$1200] Recruiting Native Cantonese-speaking Grandparents with hearing loss and Grandchildren for an Interaction Experiment [長者認知及聽力測試報告👂 + 兒童IQ智商測試報告🧠] 招募聽力損失長者及其孫子女參與互動實驗 - Brain and Mind Institute
From: LEUNG Mei Yee
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
meiyeeleung424@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
我們是
香港中文大學大腦與認知研究所（BMI）
的研究團隊。我們團隊誠摯邀請有聽力損失的長者及其孫子女來參與一項互動研究。
參與者需符合以下條件：
長者：
65歲或以上，存在聽力損失，
無其他已知認知障礙症狀，
且有意願配戴助聽器
孩童：
6-9歲，
無其他已知發展問題，母語為廣東話
實驗內容：本實驗共分為兩節（每節約1.5至2小時）：
- 第一節：長者將獨自參與一項
認知及聽力檢測
（當日孫子女無需到場）
- 第二節：長者將與孫子女一同進行
簡單遊戲
，期間我們將使用安全且非侵入性的
「近紅外光譜儀」（fNIRS）
進行腦部掃描
- 請注意：參與者必須先完成第一節的實驗，且結果符合研究要求，方會獲邀參與第二節的實驗
完成整個實驗後，您可獲得：
- 長者：一份
認知能力測試報告
+ 一份
純音聽力測試報告
- 孩童：一份
非語言智商測試報告
+ 一份
價值HKD$80的禮物
報酬：現金
HKD$400-1200
，以及免費停車券（如適用）
實驗地點：香港中文大學大腦與認知研究所（位於校園內）
如您對本研究感興趣，請點擊以下連結填寫報名表格：
https://ci.cuhk.edu.hk/surveys/?s=LJEXMFLMR79XA7TX
如祖孫兩位初步符合條件，我們將會儘快與您聯絡！
如有疑問，請發送電郵至 meiyeeleung424@cuhk.edu.hk，
亦可致電或Whatsapp 95867123 查詢。
我們期待你的參與！
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
We are researchers from the
Brain and Mind Institute (BMI) at the Chinese University of Hong Kong
. Our team sincerely invites grandparents with hearing loss and their grandchildren for a social interaction study.
Participants need to be:
- Grandparent:
65+ years old with hearing loss
, with no other diagnosed cognitive impairment, interested in fitting hearing aids
- Grandchild:
6-9 years old
with no other developmental problems; speaking Cantonese as the first language
What is involved? The experiment consists of two sessions (approx. 1.5-2 hours each):
- Session 1: The grandparent will participate alone in a
cognitive and hearing test
. (The grandchild does not need to attend)
- Session 2: The grandparent and grandchild will participate together in some
simple games
while using
fNIRS
(functional near-infrared spectroscopy, safe and non-invasive!!!) brain scanning device
- NOTE: Participants must first complete Session 1 and meet the study's requirements to be invited to Session 2
What you'll get (upon completion of the entire study):
- For the grandparent:
A cognitive test report
and
a pure-tone audiometry
(hearing test)
report
- For the child:
An non-verbal IQ test report
and
a gift (~HKD$80)
Reward:
HKD$400-1200
allowance and free parking ticket.
Location: Brain and Mind Institute, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (In campus).
If you are interested in our study, please fill in the form below via the following link:
https://ci.cuhk.edu.hk/surveys/?s=LJEXMFLMR79XA7TX
We will contact you afterwards if the dyad are suitable.
For inquiries, please contact: meiyeeleung424@cuhk.edu.hk,
call or Whatsapp 95867123.
We look forward to your participation!
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

Announcements
Join Woo Sing Choir! Auditions Now Open for Lee Woo Sing College & CUHK Students 和聲合唱團2026-27年度團員招募｜歡迎和聲書院及中大學生報名參與試音！ - Lee Woo Sing College
From: Fung Hoi Kuen
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
henryfung@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
和聲合唱團
現正展開2026-27年度成員招新！
我們誠摯邀請各位和聲同學及中大同學參與試音，成為和聲合唱團的一份子，令和諧之聲匯聚一堂。
和聲合唱團於2012年2月正式成立，即將迎來成立15週年。合唱團每年約有40至50名團員，是大學其中一個歷史悠久、規模最大的學生合唱團。團員每週於和聲音樂中心進行訓練，並積極參與書院高桌晚宴、迎新活動及不同典禮的演出。為展現團員一整年的學習成果，合唱團於每年下學期舉辦年度音樂會，與大學成員分享精彩的音樂演出。團員來自不同背景，包括本地生、內地生及國際生，大家各展所長，以歌手或樂手的身分一同演出，攜手組成和諧共融的音樂大家庭。
無論你是專業的歌者，又或只是對唱歌抱有熱愛之心，和聲合唱團都真誠地歡迎你，供你在活動中提升音樂水平，在台前表演，以及結交到學園中志同道合、一同熱愛歌唱的好友知音。
試音時間：
第一節：8月25日 (二) 下午1:00-2:30
第二節：9月8日 (二) 下午1:00-2:30

UGEC2941
Islam in Hong Kong
伊斯蘭在香港
課程簡介
本課程旨在簡介伊斯蘭在香港發展和本地化的歷史進程。課程會讓同學了解伊斯蘭的基本教義及文化知識，以及伊斯蘭在當代全球化世界的角色及地位。此外，課程會集中探討不同穆斯林社群如印度裔、巴基斯坦裔、印尼裔、非洲裔和華裔等穆斯林社群在香港發展的歷史，以及他們之間的互動及與本地社會的聯繫。

Venue: LT4, Lee Shau Kee Building (LSK LT4)

Language: Cantonese

地點：LSK LT4

語言：廣東話

Announcements
Let's listen to some music!! Recruiting Young Music Lovers | AI and Popular Song Emotion 一齊聽歌!!招募音樂愛好青年｜人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Xiuyang Meng
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
招募音樂愛好青年｜人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究
我們正在尋找熱愛音樂的你，參與人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究，用你的聽感為 AI 模型注入真實的青年情緒視角。
研究目的
本研究旨在運用人工智能技術，從青年視角對粵語流行歌曲進行情緒分類標註，評估青年群體對音樂情緒的主觀感知特徵，並為個性化音樂推薦系統及情緒調節相關研究提供數據支持。
招募條件
18 至 24 歲，熱愛音樂且經常聆聽流行音樂，能流暢使用粵語及英語進行溝通與表達的青年。
參與內容
聆聽 50 首粵語流行歌曲，並完整聽畢每首參與標註的曲目，依據自身主觀體驗與即時情緒感受，將歌曲進行情緒分類。
如何加入？
請點擊以下連結進行註冊，並回答幾條簡單問題。研究員將聯絡適合的參加者，詳細解釋研究內容：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5pU67FrIxYilalw
聯絡我們
如有任何疑問，請於辦公時間內致電 6115-0322 與研究助理陳小姐 或 蒙先生聯絡。
Recruiting Young Music Lovers | AI and Popular Song Emotion Categorization Research
We are looking for music lovers like you to participate in our research on AI and popular song emotion categorization, contributing your listening experience to inject authentic youth emotional perspectives into our AI model.
Purpose of the Study
This study aims to use artificial intelligence technology to annotate the emotion categories of Cantopop songs from a youth perspective, evaluate the subjective emotional perception characteristics of young people towards music, and provide data support for personalized music recommendation systems and emotion regulation-related research.
Eligibility Criteria
Young people aged 18 to 24 who love music, listen to popular music regularly, and are able to communicate fluently in Cantonese and English.
Participation Content
Listen to 50 Cantopop songs in full, and categorize each song according to your subjective experience and immediate emotional feelings.
How to Join?
Please click the link below to register and answer a few simple questions. Our researchers will contact eligible participants to explain the study details in full:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5pU67FrIxYilalw
Contact Us
If you have any questions, please call 6115-0322 during office hours to speak with our research assistants Ms. Chan or Mr. Meng.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

!招募音樂愛好青年｜人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究 - Department of Psychiatry From: Xiuyang Meng mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - 招募音樂愛好青年｜人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究 我們正在尋找熱愛音樂的你，參與人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究，用你的聽感為 AI 模型注入真實的青年情緒視角。 研究目的 本研究旨在運用人工智能技術，從青年視角對粵語流行歌曲進行情緒分類標註，評估青年群體對音樂情緒的主觀感知特徵，並為個性化音樂推薦系統及情緒調節相關研究提供數據支持。 招募條件 18 至 24 歲，熱愛音樂且經常聆聽流行音樂，能流暢使用粵語及英語進行溝通與表達的青年。 參與內容 聆聽 50 首粵語流行歌曲，並完整聽畢每首參與標註的曲目，依據自身主觀體驗與即時情緒感受，將歌曲進行情緒分類。 如何加入？ 請點擊以下連結進行註冊，並回答幾條簡單問題。研究員將聯絡適合的參加者，詳細解釋研究內容： https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5pU67FrIxYilalw 聯絡我們 如有任何疑問，請於辦公時間內致電 6115-0322 與研究助理陳小姐 或 蒙先生聯絡。 Recruiting Young Music Lovers | AI and Popular Song Emotion Categorization Research We are looking for music lovers like you to participate in our research on AI and popular song emotion categorization, contributing your listening experience to inject authentic youth emotional perspectives into our AI model.

Cantonese and Putonghua Online Taster Courses  廣東話及普通話網上體驗科目 - Yale-China Chinese Language Academy
From: Yale-China Chinese Language Academy
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
CLA_UPD@CUHK.EDU.HK
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
CLA is offering a series of 1-credit asynchronous Online Taster Courses for students who are interested in learning Cantonese and Putonghua (Mandarin) at their own pace. Students will learn in a low-pressure environment by watching prerecorded videos and completing online exercises. They will acquire a basic understanding of Cantonese/Putonghua upon completion of the course(s). These courses are ideal for students who would like to have a taste of language learning before taking a full 3-credit language course.
Please find the links below to register for the taster courses on KEEP:
1)
CLCC1001 Cantonese Taster Course for CUHK International Students
2)
CLCC1101 Cantonese Taster Course for CUHK Chinese-speaking Students
3)
CLCP1001 Putonghua as a Second Language Taster Course for International Students
4)
CLCP1101 Putonghua Taster Course for Local Students
More details:
Please visit the CLA website
Enquiry:
cla_upd@cuhk.edu.hk/
3943-8224
University Programme Section
Yale-China Chinese Language Academy
雅禮中國語文研習所新開設一系列一學分的非同步網上體驗科目給有興趣學習粵語、普通話的同學們。學生可通過觀看預先錄製的視頻以及完成網上練習，按照自身學習進度學習。完成課程後，同學們會對粵語/普通話應用有基本的瞭解。本科目適合想在參加完整的3學分科目之前體驗一下語言學習的學生。

Announcements
A Valuable GE Course to Explore Chinese Language and Culture with Local and Non-local Students 中外同學難得一起探討中國語言和文化的通識科目 - Yale-China Chinese Language Academy
From: Yale-China Chinese Language Academy
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
CLA_UPD@CUHK.EDU.HK
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
UGED1146 is double-coded with CLCE1103. The course is designed for all CUHK students who want to explore the relationship between language and culture. Prior knowledge of the Chinese language is not required. Course details are as follows:
Course outline:
Introduce the relationship between language and culture
Examine theories and practices in teaching and learning Chinese as a second language
Outline the language policies in Hong Kong and Mainland China
Discuss Cantonese and its relationship with other major dialects in China and Hong Kong
Medium of instruction:
English & Putonghua
Registration:
CUSIS
(Please register for UGED1146* if the study credits are for fulfilling your university's general education requirement)
For more details:
Please visit the CLA website
Enquiry:
cla_upd@cuhk.edu.hk
/ 3943-8224
*Not suitable for students who have taken CLCE1103, CCSS1010, or UGED2760.
University Programme Section
Yale-China Chinese Language Academy
UGED1146與CLCE1103列為雙重編號科目，為對中國語言及文化有興趣的中大學生而設，不受中文背景多寡限制。科目資料如下：
科目大綱：
介紹語言及文化的關係
探討對外漢語的教與學的現狀
概述香港與中國內地的語言政策
討論粵語及其與中國和香港其他主要方言的關係

Announcements
Recruitment of participants aged 6-80 years old with LONG COVID 誠邀 6-80 歲有長新冠症狀的患者參加「中醫/西醫治療長新冠症狀」的研究 - Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine
From: Wendy LI
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
hkiimresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學香港中西醫結合醫學研究所現正進行一項為期8周，以內服中藥(沖劑)或西藥改善長新冠患者症狀的臨床研究，以下是研究安排：
研究對象：
年齡介乎6至80歲；
願意接受中醫或西醫治療4星期；
每星期一次覆診跟進病程；
目的         : 比較中藥與西藥對治療長新冠患者在改善生活質量、臨床症狀和生活社等治療效果和安全性。
研究內容：中/西醫評估*、問卷評估、抽血檢查、服用中藥或西藥等。
*注意: 本研究會隨機分「中藥組」或「西藥組」
研究地點： (a)中藥組: 沙田威爾斯親王醫院; (b)西藥組: 指定西醫診所 (中環)。
參與方式： 若有興趣，歡迎
1.透過以下方式報名：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13670048
2.亦歡迎您致電或WhatsApp我們6082-2583/ 2873-3245了解詳情。
Research Introduction:
The novel coronavirus has caused a global pandemic since the end of 2019. People are increasingly paying attention to the long-term effects of COVID-19 infection.People whose symptoms last for more than four weeks after COVID-19 infection are called [Long COVID]. The main symptoms include severe fatigue, shortness of breath, heart damage (such as myocarditis), cognitive impairment, sleep disorders, post-traumatic stress disorder syndrome, Muscle pain, decreased concentration, headache, impaired taste and smell, etc. affect the respiratory system, cardiovascular system, digestive system, urinary system, immune system, etc.
The Hong Kong Institute of Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western Medicine at the Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently conducting an 8-week clinical study on the improvement of symptoms of patients with COVID-19 by taking Chinese medicine (infusion) or Western medicine.
Target
: Age 6-80 who have recovered from COVID-19 infection.
Purpose
: To compare the therapeutic effects and safety of traditional Chinese medicine and Western medicine on improving the quality of life, clinical symptoms and social functions of long-term COVID-19 patients.
Research Content
: Visits, questionnaire assessment, blood draw before and after taking medicine,taking research Chinese medicine or Western medicine, etc.
Study Location
:(a) Chinese medicine group: Prince of Wales Hospital, Shatin;
(b) Western medicine group: designated western medicine clinic.
Participation
： Free of charge. If interested, please
1. sign up through the following ：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13670048
2. You are also welcome to call or WhatsApp us at 6082-2583/ 2873-3245 for details.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

[Clinical safety, efficacy and multiomic evaluation of a novel Chinese Medicine formula in Type 2 diabetes: Effects on beta-cell function and insulin resistance
.]
Department of Medicine and Therapeutics and Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine, CUHK are jointly conducting a 36-week clinical study on the use of oral traditional Chinese medicine (granule form) for treating type 2 diabetes.
Eligibility Criteria: Ethnic Chinese individuals aged 18 to 70 years
No major illnesses, not currently taking any traditional Chinese medicine, and with a Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥ 18 kg/m² (kg ÷ metre ÷ metre)
Non-smokers or those who have quit smoking for at least 12 months; females must not be currently pregnant
Diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for less than 6 years and have not used any glucose-lowering medications (including insulin) in the past 3 months
Must have at least one of the following risk factors:
Family history of diabetes (especially if parents or siblings were diagnosed before age of 40)
Metabolic syndrome (three highs: high blood sugar, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol)
Overweight or obesity
Fatty liver
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
History of gestational diabetes
If you are unsure whether you have diabetes, a 75g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) will be arranged for you.

Study Procedures Include:
Chinese and Western medical assessments, Electrocardiogram (ECG), Liver fibrosis scan, Blood tests, Questionnaire completion, Taking either the study Chinese medicine or a placebo
Location: Ward 3M, 3/F, Old Block, Diabetes and Endocrinology Research Centre, Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin, New Territories
Free of charge to participate.
Successful participants may receive an allowance of up to HKD $1,000.
Limited quota – first come, first served!

Family history of diabetes (especially if parents or siblings were diagnosed before age of 40)

Fatty liver
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
History of gestational diabetes

Announcements
( Receive up to HK$400 Allowance!) Recruiting young adults (aged 18–24) for online sleep and mental health intervention with individualized support ~誠邀18至24歲青年參加網上睡眠及心理健康課程，仲有個人化的指導（最高可獲得$400津貼！） ~ - Department of Psychiatry
From: Karyn Ng
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
kayanng002@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學精神科學系正進行一項研究，旨在評估手機應用程式的認知行為治療結合晝夜節律改善大學生的睡眠及情緒。現招募年齡介乎18歲至24歲在學青年研究。詳情如下:
我們誠邀符合以下條件的人士參與本次研究：
1. 18歲至24歲大專生
2. 有失眠症狀及遲睡傾向(凌晨12點後才睡覺)
3.  過去三個月沒有接受失眠及情緒心理治療或藥物治療
您需要做什麼？
∎ 填寫網上評估問卷
∎佩戴睡眠手錶及填寫睡眠日記
∎完成 7 日簡短錄音錄影紀錄當下狀態（每日兩次，每次約１—２分鐘）
∎手機應用程式上的網上治療課程​ ，共6個單元，​每一星期睇一個單元 （15-30分鐘）
∎在完成治療​後的一星期及６個月後，會邀請你再填寫網上評估問卷及和配戴睡眠手錶
如有興趣，請即登記並填寫簡單的網上篩查問卷：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_09uYGHApXoC8CDY
研究小組將會聯絡適合參與本研究的人士並進一步解釋研究詳情。閣下登記時留下的資料僅供研究用途，絕對保密。如閣下對是項研究有任何查詢，請電郵
sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
或 WhatsApp: (+852 47544464 吳小姐) 查詢。
The Department of Psychiatry at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is conducting a research study to evaluate the effectiveness of a mobile app-based cognitive behavioral therapy program combined with a circadian rhythm intervention in improving sleep and mental health among college/university students. We would like to invite participants aged between 18 and 24 to join the study. Details are as follows:
Inclusion criteria:
1.  College or university students aged between 18-24 years
2. Reporting symptoms of insomnia and a delayed sleep pattern, typically falling asleep after midnight.
3. Do not receive psychological, behavioural, or pharmacological treatment for insomnia or emotional problems in the past three months.
What you need to do?
∎ Complete online questionnaires
∎ Wear the actigraphy watch and keep a sleep diary
∎ Record brief audio and video entries about your current state for 7 consecutive days (twice daily, 1–2 minutes each)
∎ Complete a  6-week intervention program through a mobile app-based  (one module per week,   15–30 minutes per module).
∎ Complete follow-up assessments and wear the actigraphy watch one week and six months after the intervention.
If you are interested, please register and complete a short screening questionnaire here:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_09uYGHApXoC8CDY
The research team will contact eligible participants and further explain the details of the study. Information collected will be only used for research purpose and will be kept strictly confidential. If you have any enquiries, please contact us via email
sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
or WhatsApp: (+852 47544464 Miss Ng).

From: Reimagining Yung Shue Au
