榕樹凹文化與沙頭角導賞及沙頭角公共圖書館分享
Yung Shue Au Cultural & Sha Tau Kok Tour and Sharing at Sha Tau Kok Public Library
活動詳情 / Activity Details
日期 / Date：2026年8月19日(星期三)  / 19 August 2026 (Wed)
時間 / Time ：1230 - 1600
地點 / Venue：榕樹凹、沙頭角及沙頭角公共圖書館 / Yung Shue Au, Sha Tau Kok and Sha Tau Kok Public Library
集合地點 / Meeting Point：沙頭角避風塘 Sha Tau Kok Typhoon Shelter
https://share.google/POni3sD7Hm9uTNH64
費用 / Fee：全免 / Free of charge
名額 / Quota：12
報名 / Registration
：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13737301
如活動受天氣影響而取消，將順延至一星期後（8月26日）舉行，其他安排維持不變。
If the event is cancelled due to adverse weather conditions, it will be postponed for one week (26 August 2026), while all other arrangements will remain unchanged.
About / 簡介:
中大建築學院將與沙頭角公共圖書館合辦「榕樹凹文化與沙頭角導賞 及 沙頭角公共圖書館分享活動」。參加者將先由榕樹凹文化大使帶領走訪榕樹凹，認識其當地文化與歷史景點。其後走訪沙頭角禁區，了解沙頭角禁區發展，再前往沙頭角公共圖書館，由助理館長江晉賢先生介紹與沙頭角及榕樹凹相關的館藏書籍，從不同角度加深對兩地文化與歷史的了解。分享環節更會介紹香港公共圖書館的電子書館藏，讓參加者可隨時隨地在線上閱讀。
The CUHK School of Architecture is collaborating with the Sha Tau Kok Public Library to present the “Yung Shue Au Cultural Guided Tour and Sha Tau Kok Public Library Sharing Session.” Participants will begin with a guided tour at Yung Shue Au, led by the Yung Shue Au Cultural Ambassadors, to explore the village’s local culture and historical landmarks. The tour will then continue to the Sha Tau Kok Frontier Closed Area, where participants will learn about the architecture and development of Sha Tau Kok. The programme will then continue at the Sha Tau Kok Public Library, where Assistant Librarian Mr. Alferd Kong Chun-yin will introduce library collections related to Sha Tau Kok and Yung Shue Au, offering deeper insights into the history and culture of both areas. The sharing session will also introduce the Hong Kong Public Libraries’ e book collections, enabling participants to access online reading resources anytime and anywhere.
注意 / Notice：
參加者需自行安排來往沙頭角之交通
Participants should arrange their own transportation to Sha Tau Kok。
參加者需自行上網申請邊境禁區許可證：
Participants must apply for the Closed Area Permit online themselves:
https://www.es.police.gov.hk/
是次活動是香港中文大學建築學院「重塑榕樹凹故事」項目的一部分，並由鄉郊保育辦公室、鄉郊保育資助計劃資助。
This activity is a part of "Re-telling the Yung Shue Au Story", a project by CUHK School of Architecture, sponsored by the  Countryside Conservation Office and Countryside Conservation Funding Scheme.

bodyText:

Microsoft Copilot Chat Tips Proofread & Polish Your Writing  - ITSC
From: ITSC
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
itsc@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Before you hit send on that important email, report, or message — let
Copilot
give it a once-over! Just paste your text and ask Copilot to proofread and improve it. It’ll catch typos, grammar issues, awkward phrasing, and suggest better word choices — all while keeping
your
voice intact.

Try this prompt — copy & paste it!
"Please proofread and improve the following text. Fix any grammar or spelling errors, improve clarity, and suggest better word choices where needed. Keep my original meaning and tone. Here’s the text: [paste your text here]"
Why this works:
Clear instructions about WHAT to fix (grammar, clarity, word choice) and WHAT to keep (meaning, tone) give you useful edits without changing your voice. It’s like having a trusted editor on standby!

Bonus tip:
You can also ask
“What are the 3 weakest sentences in this text and how would you improve them?”
for targeted feedback instead of a full rewrite.
More Tips & Resources
Looking for more ways to level up your Copilot game? Check out previous
All IT - Microsoft Copilot Chat Usage Tips
for even more helpful guidance and best practices.

Our team is currently recruiting typically developed children (as control) for a laboratory study on the walking patterns of children with Developmental Coordination Disorder.
Target participants: Children aged 7–10, with
typical motor coordination and no special educational needs (SEN)

Join Singing & Handicraft Workshops with Stroke Survivors! Students and Staff Welcome!   誠邀各位同學及教職員參加「以歌會友」及「風中手作」體驗活動！ - The Nethersole School of Nursing
From: Chloe Cheung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
chloe.cheung@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
誠邀各位同學及教職員參加「以歌會友」及「風中手作」活動！
日期： 2026年8月28日（星期五）及2026年9月24日（星期四）
⏰ 時間： 下午2時至5時
地點： 威爾斯親王醫院（PWH）賽馬會公共衛生學院 209室 或 線上參與「以歌會友」活動 (連結於報名後發放)
透過歌舞及二手衣物裝飾製作，與中風人士交流互動，了解他們的復康心路歷程，一同度過滿載歡樂與創意的下午。
二手衣物裝飾作品將在 9月開始在不同醫院巡迴展出，並於 12月大型展覽 中公開展示，向公眾分享你們與中風人士的創作成果。
另歌舞表演將於11月及12月於中學舉行，你都一齊參與演出啦！
報名/查詢： 5726 1028 (WhatsApp) 與 張小姐 聯絡

Students and Staff Welcome!

⏰

Room 209, Jockey Club School of Public Health and Primary Care, Prince of Wales Hospital (PWH)

Handicraft will be showcased at hospitals from September onwards and at a large public exhibition in December.

title: HK$250 Stipend: Two-Person fNIRS Experiment for Chinese Mainland Students-Come with your travel companion! 250港币酬劳: 双人近红外实验机会，面向中国大陆学生 – 与你的旅行朋友一起来体验吧！
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/08/07
»
Announcements
HK$250 Stipend: Two-Person fNIRS Experiment for Chinese Mainland Students-Come with your travel companion! 250港币酬劳: 双人近红外实验机会，面向中国大陆学生 – 与你的旅行朋友一起来体验吧！ - Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
From: Xiaohui RAO
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155197282@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
你对自己的大脑了解吗？你知道你跟小伙伴在交流对话过程中的共脑表现吗？不要错过这样一次难得的双人实验机会噢！！
本实验室使用临床级安全的近红外脑图系统，收集人大脑局部的耗氧变化，不会对人体产生伤害。有任何安全顾虑都可以和研究人员联系了解：
Miss RAO,
1155197282@link.cuhk.edu.hk
实验日期：2026年7月28日至8月30日
实验时长：每次60-65分钟，共两次，可分别在同一天的上下午完成（包括实验准备20分钟，任务30-35分钟，填问卷5分钟）。
实验内容：1）佩戴近红外设备，参加互动实验，；2）填写一些问卷。
实验地点：中文大学梁銶琚楼G层（语言学系）G34实验室。
实验结束后，会通过转数快/现金/百佳优惠券来支付250港元被试费用。
参与者需要符合以下要求：
1. 母语为汉语普通话；
2. 视力（矫正后）正常，听力正常；
3. 无脑损伤、癫痫等神经类疾病，无头皮外伤或感染；
4. 右利手（写字，用筷子等习惯使用右手）；
5. 实验当天不化妆，实验当天或前一晚在家自行洗头；
6. 可以接受在实验过程上戴上类似脑电设备的头套（实验结束后无需洗头）
7. 有共同旅游经历的两位同性别朋友，共同线下参与实验
8. 旅游经历发生在近两个月内，且旅行时间跨度2天1晚及以上
报名链接：
https://www.wjx.top/vm/huu9JXm.aspx#
香港中文大学语言学及现代语言系
如有问题，请联系饶女士（1155197282@link.cuhk.edu.hk）
This research is endorsed by
Prof. CAI Zhenguang
zhenguangcai@cuhk.edu.hk
Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
English Version:
Do you know your own brain? Are you curious about the inter-brain synchrony between you and your partner during communication and conversation? Don't miss out on this rare opportunity to participate in a two-person experiment!
Our laboratory utilizes a clinical-grade, safe functional Near-Infrared Spectroscopy (fNIRS) system to collect localized oxygenation changes in the human brain. This process is completely safe and does not cause any harm to the human body.
Experiment Date
: July 28 to August 30, 2026
Duration:
60-65 minutes per session, two sessions in total. Sessions can be completed consecutively in the morning and afternoon of the same day (including 20 mins preparation, 30-35 mins tasks, and 5 mins questionnaire).
Content:
1) Wear an fNIRS device and participate in an interactive experiment; 2) Complete questionnaires.
Location:
Room G34, G/F, Leung Kau Kui Building (Department of Linguistics), The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK).
Compensation:
Upon completion, a stipend of HK$250 will be paid via FPS, cash, or ParknShop vouchers.
Participants need to meet the following requirements:
1. Native Mandarin speaker;
2. Normal vision (after correction) and normal hearing;
3. No brain injury, epilepsy, or other neurological diseases; no scalp trauma or infection;
4. Right-handed (e.g., writing, using chopsticks);
5. No make-up on the day of the experiment; wash hair at home on the day of or the night before the experiment;
6. Comfortable wearing an EEG-like cap during the experiment (no need to wash hair afterwards);
7. Two same-gender friends/colleagues with a shared travel experience, participating in the experiment together in person;
8. The travel experience occurred within the last two months, and the trip lasted for at least 2 days and 1 night.
Enrolment link:
https://www.wjx.top/vm/huu9JXm.aspx#
Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
If you have any questions, please contact Miss Rao (1155197282@link.cuhk.edu.hk)
This research is endorsed by
Prof. CAI Zhenguang
zhenguangcai@cuhk.edu.hk
Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
The Chinese University of Hong Kong

If you have any safety concerns, please contact the researcher for further information: Miss RAO, 1155197282@link.cuhk.edu.hk.

This is a spoken-interaction experiment. Participants will wear a safe, non-invasive functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS) device during the experiment and complete questionnaires. The total duration is approximately 2.5 hours, and the participation fee is HK$220.

NEWLY LAUNCHED! - UGEB2996 Getting to Know Speech and Language Impairment and the Role of Speech Therapist (Fully Online & Asynchronous Learning) 全新推出！UGEB2996 初探言語障礙與言語治療師角色 (全網上非同步學習) - Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery
From: CHEUK KIT CHING
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
cynthiacheuk@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
🆕
全新推出！
你是否曾遇過有溝通困難的人士，卻不知道如何與他們互動？你是否想了解言語障礙如何影響一個人的學習、社交及日常生活？
本課程將介紹言語及語言障礙（Speech and Language Impairment）的基本知識，以及言語治療師在支援有溝通需要人士方面的重要角色。課程透過由經驗言語治療師及教授團隊預備的動畫教學、模擬及真實臨床資料、及互動學習活動，幫助同學認識言語及語言障礙的影響，同時培養尊重、同理心及共融價值觀。
課程特色
自主安排學習時間，按個人進度完成課程
互動學習模式
真實及模擬臨床資料
提升對特殊教育需要（SEN）的認識
培養同理心、尊重與共融精神 適合任何學科背景同學修讀

課程編號：
UGEB2996

課程名稱：
初探言語障礙與言語治療師角色

授課模式：
網上非同步學習（Online Asynchronous）

學分：
1 學分
NEWLY LAUNCHED!
Have you ever wondered how communication disorders affect a person's daily life and learning? Would you like to understand the role of Speech Therapists and learn how to communicate more effectively with individuals with communication needs?
This course introduces the fundamentals of Speech and Language Disorders (types of Special Educational Needs), and the important role of the Speech Therapist in supporting individuals with such communication needs. Through animated tutorials by our experienced team of Speech Therapists and Professors, the use of simulated and/or real clinical data, and interactive learning activities, students will gain both knowledge and awareness of the impact of Speech and Language Disorders, whilst developing empathy, respect and inclusive values.
Course Highlights
Flexible self-paced online learning
Interactive learning activities
Real and simulated clinical data
Enhance awareness of Special Educational Needs (SEN)
Foster empathy, respect, and inclusion

UGEB2996

Course Title:
Getting to Know Speech and Language Impairment and the Role of Speech Therapist

Mode:
Online Asynchronous

Credits:
1 Unit

Announcements
⭐ [CUHK Ophthalmology & Visual Sciences] Invitation for Thyroid Disease Patients for Free Thyroid Eye Screening ⭐⭐【中大眼科】招募甲狀腺疾病人士參與免費甲狀腺眼篩檢 - Department of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences (OVS)
From: Hanson Wong (OVS)
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
yiumanwong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
⭐⭐
【中大眼科】招募甲狀腺疾病人士參與免費眼科篩檢
【香港中文大學眼科研究】招募甲狀腺疾病人士參與免費眼科篩檢及臨床研究
香港中文大學醫學院眼科及視覺科學學系現正進行一項臨床研究，誠邀已確診或懷疑患有甲狀腺疾病人士參與免費眼科篩檢，以評估是否患有甲狀腺眼病（Thyroid Eye Disease, TED），以及是否適合參與後續臨床研究。
什麼是甲狀腺眼病？
甲狀腺眼病是常見於甲狀腺疾病（如格里夫氏症）的眼部併發症，可引致以下情況：
眼乾、刺痛或流淚
眼皮腫脹或向上收縮
眼球突出（俗稱「眼凸」）
外觀改變，甚至影響視力
及早發現及治療，有助減低病情惡化的風險。
招募對象
符合以下條件人士歡迎參加：
年齡介乎
18
至
80
歲
已確診或懷疑患有甲狀腺疾病（包括甲亢或甲減）
輕至中度甲狀腺眼病患者（已確診或懷疑）
未曾接受甲狀腺眼病相關治療
非懷孕或非哺乳人士
能理解粵語、普通話或英語，並能閱讀中文或英文
即使未確定是否患有甲狀腺眼病，只要曾患甲狀腺疾病，亦歡迎參加篩檢。
研究內容及安排
免費全面眼科檢查
由專業眼科醫生評估及跟進
所有研究相關檢查及評估費用全免
符合資格者將獲邀參與為期約
12
個月
的臨床藥物研究
地點（由研究團隊安排）：
香港中文大學眼科中心（九龍）
或 香港中文大學醫院（沙田）
（最終是否符合研究資格將由研究團隊作進一步評估）
報名及詳情
請透過以下連結登記參與甲狀腺眼病篩檢：

立即登記篩檢
研究團隊將與合資格人士聯絡，安排進一步篩查。
查詢
香港中文大學醫學院眼科及視覺科學學系
電話：3943 0790（何小姐）
WhatsApp：5642 7952
請註明：「查詢 SAVEMORETED 甲狀腺眼疾藥物臨床研究」
您的參與不僅有助及早了解自身眼睛健康狀況，亦有助推動甲狀腺眼病的醫學研究，為未來患者帶來更多治療可能。
The Department of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) is currently conducting a clinical study on Thyroid Eye Disease (TED). We warmly invite individuals with confirmed or suspected thyroid disorders to participate in a
free comprehensive eye screening
to assess for TED and potential eligibility for further clinical research.
What is Thyroid Eye Disease (TED)?
Thyroid Eye Disease is a condition commonly associated with thyroid disorders such as Graves’ disease. It may lead to:
Dryness, irritation, or excessive tearing
Eyelid swelling or retraction
Protrusion of the eyes (proptosis)
Changes in appearance and, in some cases, vision impairment
Early detection and appropriate management are important to reduce the risk of disease progression.
Eligibility Criteria
Individuals who meet the following criteria are welcome to participate:
Aged
18 to 80 years
Diagnosed with or suspected of having thyroid disorders (hyperthyroidism or hypothyroidism)
Diagnosed with or suspected of having
mild to moderate Thyroid Eye Disease
Have
not received prior treatment
specifically for Thyroid Eye Disease
Not pregnant or breastfeeding
Able to understand Cantonese, Mandarin, or English, and read Chinese or English
Individuals who are unsure whether they have Thyroid Eye Disease are also encouraged to join the screening if they have a history of thyroid conditions.
Study Details
Participants will receive:
Free comprehensive ophthalmic examination
Professional assessment and follow-up by ophthalmologists
All study-related examinations at no cost
Eligible participants may be invited to join a
12-month clinical drug study
, subject to further screening and eligibility assessment.

Study locations (by arrangement):
CUHK Eye Centre (Kowloon)
CUHK Medical Centre (Sha Tin)
Registration and Further Information
To register for the Thyroid Eye Disease screening, please visit:

Register for TED Screening
Our research team will contact eligible applicants to arrange further screening.
Enquiries
Department of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences
Faculty of Medicine, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Tel: 3943 0790 (Ms. Ho)
WhatsApp: 5642 7952
Please specify: “SAVEMORETED Clinical Study Enquiry”
Participation in this study not only helps you better understand your eye health, but also contributes to advancing research and improving treatment options for patients with Thyroid Eye Disease.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

CU303社區服務計劃現正招募中大義工參與由東華三院樂盈外展綜合健康服務舉辦的長者康樂活動。樂盈外展綜合健康服務一直為居於港島區院舍的長者提供外展社交、康樂及健康支援服務，協助長者維持身心健康及社會聯繫。
分別來自兩間院舍的長者早前透過筆友計劃互相認識，今次活動將安排他們一同參觀博物館及共進午餐，讓他們透過實體聚會延續書信交流建立的友誼。

⏰ 時間：10:15am–2:00pm
地點：稻香飲食文化博物館（火炭）
CU303會員將獲優先考慮
作為義工，你將全程陪伴長者參與活動，包括：
一對一支援長者參與活動

報名連結：

The CU303•Care & Unite Programme is now recruiting CUHK volunteers for an elderly recreational activity organized by the Tung Wah Group of Hospitals Lok Ying Outreaching Allied Health Service. The service provides outreach social, recreational and allied health support to elderly residents living in residential care homes, helping them maintain their well-being and social connections.
Sixteen elderly residents from two care homes were previously connected through a pen-pal programme. This activity will bring them together for a museum visit and lunch gathering, allowing them to strengthen the friendships they have built through written correspondence.
Date: 15 September 2026 (Tuesday)
⏰ Time: 10:15am–2:00pm
Venue: Tao Heung Museum of Food Culture, Fo Tan
Priority consideration will be given to CU303 members
As a volunteer, you will accompany elderly participants throughout the event and:
Provide one-on-one support to elderly participants
Accompany residents during the guided museum tour
Engage with residents and create meaningful interactions
Assist with participant safety and, where necessary, provide wheelchair support
We welcome participation from CUHK staff, students and alumni. CUHK staff who wish to join may apply for
time release for community service
, where applicable. Please note that approval from your supervisor should be obtained before attending the event.
As places are limited, registration does not guarantee participation. Selected volunteers will receive a confirmation email with detailed arrangements closer to the event date.
We warmly invite you to join our volunteer team and take part in this special activity with elderly participants

title: [Blood pressure management !] Recruiting Post-Menopausal Women with Elevated/Stage I Hypertension for Participation in a Ten-Week Oral NR Supplementation (Market Value: 4200 HKD) and Aerobic Exercise Study 【血壓健康管理計劃 】招募停經後且患有血壓偏高/第一期高血壓女性參與為期十週的NR補充劑 (市場價值: 4200 HKD) 與有氧運動研究
bodyText:

Announcements
[Blood pressure management !] Recruiting Post-Menopausal Women with Elevated/Stage I Hypertension for Participation in a Ten-Week Oral NR Supplementation (Market Value: 4200 HKD) and Aerobic Exercise Study 【血壓健康管理計劃 】招募停經後且患有血壓偏高/第一期高血壓女性參與為期十週的NR補充劑 (市場價值: 4200 HKD) 與有氧運動研究 - Department of Sports Science & Physical Education; Program Director: Prof. Stephen Heung-sang WONG
From: ZHANG Jiaqi
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155189512@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
高血壓是香港常見的慢性疾病。衞生署2020至2022年度人口健康調查顯示，65至84歲人士的高血壓患病率為57.4%，而超過四成患者未察覺自己血壓偏高。若未能妥善控制，高血壓可增加中風、冠心病、心臟衰竭及腎臟疾病等風險。
女性進入更年期後，隨著雌激素水平下降，可能出現血管功能改變、彈性減弱、體脂分布及血脂變化，令血壓及心血管風險逐漸上升尤。因此，更年期後女性，尤其是缺乏日常運動習慣者，更應及早關注血壓、代謝及整體心血管健康。
近年研究指出，NAD在細胞能量代謝及減少炎症過程中扮演重要角色。隨著年齡增長，體內NAD水平可能逐漸下降。部分研究顯示，提升體內NAD水平或有助於支持血管內皮功能，維持心血管健康。然而，相關作用及其臨床效益仍有待進一步研究確立。
因此，本研究旨在探討規律運動結合NAD補充對更年期後女性代謝及心血管健康指標的潛在影響。研究結果或有助於加深了解運動及NAD補充在更年期後健康管理的作用。
參與資格：
停經超過一年；
華裔；
符合《2025 年美國心臟病學會/美國心臟協會成人高血壓預防、檢測、評估與管理指南》中對血壓升高/高血壓一期的標準（即血壓≥120/80 mmHg 且 <140/90 mmHg，基於≥2 次測量的平均值）；
無運動習慣。

排除標准：
存在不適合參加運動訓練的健康狀況；
子宮切除病史；
正在食用維生素B或NAD補充劑。

參加方法：
點擊海報或通過以下鏈接作網上登記【
https://forms.gle/ggPtpRDCdes3xuhE8
】；
研究團隊會進行初步篩選，以了解您是否符合基本參加資格；
成功通過初步篩選後，預約檢查時間；
前往香港中文大學汾陽體育館參加檢查；
如果符合參加條件，將會被隨機分組，正式開展後續正式的研究計劃。

計劃內容：
隨機分組：急步行結合 NR 補充劑組 (NRBW)；急步行結合安慰劑組 (PLBW)；僅使用 NR 補充劑組 (NR)；僅使用安慰劑組 (PL)；
10星期 NR補充劑/有氧運動（根據隨機分組後的內容）；
需到實驗室做3次檢查（第0週、第10週、第20週），檢查包括身體成分、血壓和採集靜脈血；
定期隨訪實驗室領取NR補充劑；
根據隨機分組內容，食用NR補充劑/參加運動班。

參與地點：
香港中文大學汾陽體育館G02
如您有任何疑問，可通過以下渠道聯絡這項研究的相關人員：
張小姐
WhatsApp: 93741382
電郵: z.jiaqi@link.cuhk.edu.hk
[
數據安全聲明
]
所有檢測結果加密儲存，僅供研究團隊匿名分析，您可隨時要求刪除個人資料
[
歡迎邀請身邊患有血壓升高
/
高血壓一期更年期後女性參加
]
Despite guideline-recommended pharmacological treatment strategies, hypertension remains highly prevalent worldwide and is a major risk factor for cardiovascular disease. In China, approximately one-third of adults have hypertension, yet fewer than 5% achieve well-controlled blood pressure. Postmenopausal women, in particular, face a significantly increased risk of developing hypertension due to the combined effects of aging and the menopausal transition.
Recent research suggests that restoring NAD levels may serve as a therapeutic approach to improve endothelial function and alleviate vascular dysfunction in individuals with hypertension. NAD is one of the most important molecules in the human body, playing a critical role in regulating major biological processes, and its levels decline with age. Therefore, this randomized controlled trial aims to investigate whether increasing NAD levels through oral nicotinamide riboside (NR) supplementation and/or aerobic exercise can improve hypertension symptoms in postmenopausal women with elevated blood pressure or Stage I hypertension.
Participation in this study is free of charge. You will not need to pay for any study-related items or services, and no material compensation (including monetary incentives) will be provided.

Eligibility Criteria:
Absent of menstruation for more than one year;
Chinese;
Meet the criteria for elevated blood pressure or Stage I hypertension according to the
2025 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults
(i.e., blood pressure ≥120/80 mmHg and <140/90 mmHg, based on the average of at least two measurements);
No regular exercise habit.

How to Participate:
Click the poster or register online via the following link:
https://forms.gle/ggPtpRDCdes3xuhE8
The research team will conduct an initial screening to determine whether you meet the basic eligibility criteria;
If you pass the preliminary screening, you will schedule an appointment for assessment;
Attend the assessment at the G02, Kwok Sports Building, CUHK;
If eligible, you will be randomly assigned to a study group and begin the formal study program.

Study Plan:
Participants will be randomly assigned to one of the following groups:
Brisk walking combined with NR supplementation group (NRBW);
Brisk walking combined with placebo group (PLBW);
NR supplementation only group (NR);
Placebo only group (PL).
The study includes:
10 weeks of NR supplementation and/or aerobic exercise (according to group assignment);
Three laboratory visits (Week 0, Week 10, and Week 20), including body composition measurement, blood pressure assessment, and venous blood collection;
Regular laboratory visits to ensure adherence;
Taking NR supplements and/or attending exercise sessions based on group assignment.

Study Location:
G02, Kwok Sports Building, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
If you have any questions, please contact:
Ms. ZHANG
WhatsApp: 93741382
E-mail: z.jiaqi@link.cuhk.edu.hk
[Data Security Statement]
All test results will be securely encrypted and stored. Data will be used only for anonymous analysis by the research team. You may request deletion of your personal data at any time.
[Feel free to invite post-menopausal women with elevated blood pressure or Stage I hypertension to participate.]

近年研究指出，NAD在細胞能量代謝及減少炎症過程中扮演重要角色。隨著年齡增長，體內NAD水平可能逐漸下降。部分研究顯示，提升體內NAD水平或有助於支持血管內皮功能，維持心血管健康。然而，相關作用及其臨床效益仍有待進一步研究確立。
因此，本研究旨在探討規律運動結合NAD補充對更年期後女性代謝及心血管健康指標的潛在影響。研究結果或有助於加深了解運動及NAD補充在更年期後健康管理的作用。
參與資格：
停經超過一年；
華裔；
符合《2025 年美國心臟病學會/美國心臟協會成人高血壓預防、檢測、評估與管理指南》中對血壓升高/高血壓一期的標準（即血壓≥120/80 mmHg 且 <140/90 mmHg，基於≥2 次測量的平均值）；
無運動習慣。

排除標准：
存在不適合參加運動訓練的健康狀況；
子宮切除病史；
正在食用維生素B或NAD補充劑。

參加方法：
點擊海報或通過以下鏈接作網上登記【
https://forms.gle/ggPtpRDCdes3xuhE8
】；
研究團隊會進行初步篩選，以了解您是否符合基本參加資格；
成功通過初步篩選後，預約檢查時間；
前往香港中文大學汾陽體育館參加檢查；
如果符合參加條件，將會被隨機分組，正式開展後續正式的研究計劃。

計劃內容：
隨機分組：急步行結合 NR 補充劑組 (NRBW)；急步行結合安慰劑組 (PLBW)；僅使用 NR 補充劑組 (NR)；僅使用安慰劑組 (PL)；
10星期 NR補充劑/有氧運動（根據隨機分組後的內容）；
需到實驗室做3次檢查（第0週、第10週、第20週），檢查包括身體成分、血壓和採集靜脈血；
定期隨訪實驗室領取NR補充劑；
根據隨機分組內容，食用NR補充劑/參加運動班。

參與地點：
香港中文大學汾陽體育館G02
如您有任何疑問，可通過以下渠道聯絡這項研究的相關人員：
張小姐
WhatsApp: 93741382
電郵: z.jiaqi@link.cuhk.edu.hk
[
數據安全聲明
]
所有檢測結果加密儲存，僅供研究團隊匿名分析，您可隨時要求刪除個人資料
[
歡迎邀請身邊患有血壓升高
/
高血壓一期更年期後女性參加
]
Despite guideline-recommended pharmacological treatment strategies, hypertension remains highly prevalent worldwide and is a major risk factor for cardiovascular disease. In China, approximately one-third of adults have hypertension, yet fewer than 5% achieve well-controlled blood pressure. Postmenopausal women, in particular, face a significantly increased risk of developing hypertension due to the combined effects of aging and the menopausal transition.
Recent research suggests that restoring NAD levels may serve as a therapeutic approach to improve endothelial function and alleviate vascular dysfunction in individuals with hypertension. NAD is one of the most important molecules in the human body, playing a critical role in regulating major biological processes, and its levels decline with age. Therefore, this randomized controlled trial aims to investigate whether increasing NAD levels through oral nicotinamide riboside (NR) supplementation and/or aerobic exercise can improve hypertension symptoms in postmenopausal women with elevated blood pressure or Stage I hypertension.
Participation in this study is free of charge. You will not need to pay for any study-related items or services, and no material compensation (including monetary incentives) will be provided.

Eligibility Criteria:
Absent of menstruation for more than one year;
Chinese;
Meet the criteria for elevated blood pressure or Stage I hypertension according to the
2025 American College of Cardiology/American Heart Association Guideline for the Prevention, Detection, Evaluation, and Management of High Blood Pressure in Adults
(i.e., blood pressure ≥120/80 mmHg and <140/90 mmHg, based on the average of at least two measurements);
No regular exercise habit.

How to Participate:
Click the poster or register online via the following link:
https://forms.gle/ggPtpRDCdes3xuhE8
The research team will conduct an initial screening to determine whether you meet the basic eligibility criteria;
If you pass the preliminary screening, you will schedule an appointment for assessment;
Attend the assessment at the G02, Kwok Sports Building, CUHK;
If eligible, you will be randomly assigned to a study group and begin the formal study program.

Study Plan:
Participants will be randomly assigned to one of the following groups:
Brisk walking combined with NR supplementation group (NRBW);
Brisk walking combined with placebo group (PLBW);
NR supplementation only group (NR);
Placebo only group (PL).
The study includes:
10 weeks of NR supplementation and/or aerobic exercise (according to group assignment);
Three laboratory visits (Week 0, Week 10, and Week 20), including body composition measurement, blood pressure assessment, and venous blood collection;
Regular laboratory visits to ensure adherence;
Taking NR supplements and/or attending exercise sessions based on group assignment.

Study Location:
G02, Kwok Sports Building, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
If you have any questions, please contact:
Ms. ZHANG
WhatsApp: 93741382
E-mail: z.jiaqi@link.cuhk.edu.hk
[Data Security Statement]
All test results will be securely encrypted and stored. Data will be used only for anonymous analysis by the research team. You may request deletion of your personal data at any time.
[Feel free to invite post-menopausal women with elevated blood pressure or Stage I hypertension to participate.]
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Announcements
Recruiting Hong Kong Primary School Students and Parents for a Leadership Study 【完成可獲HKD100報酬】誠意邀請香港小學生及家長參與領導力相關心理學研究 - Gender Studies Programme
From: HE Chuting
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
conniehe@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
你想了解孩子對於學校或日常生活裡的“領導”的看法嗎？想知道孩子對於“當領導”的意願嗎？不要錯過這次有趣又有意義的研究機會，而且還有報酬可領喔~~
招募對象
：
在香港就讀小1到小6的小學生以及其父親或母親
研究項目：
小學生、家長及老師的領導認知與刻板印象
研究內容：
1.孩子：1對1線上訪談（需錄音），約需1小時。
2.家長：填寫1份網上問卷，約需1小時。
報酬：
家長和孩子完成各自的研究項目後，可獲得共100港幣報酬。
參與條件：
1.兒童參加者為在港就讀小1到小6的小學生，家長參加者為該兒童的父親或母親。
2.兒童能講流利廣東話或普通話，家長能閱讀和書寫中文。
3.兒童可使用有互聯網、視頻和音頻功能的電腦或平板參與研究。
4.請留意參加者需在此前沒有參與過本研究的“預實驗”或“教師部分”（如不清楚是否參與過也可先留下聯繫方式，稍後我們的研究人員將與您聯繫進行確認）。
如對本實驗感興趣，請通過以下鏈接報名
，我們的研究人員將盡快聯繫您：https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_6KzWB6HhTtOhwou
參與純屬自願性質，所收集的資料只作研究用途及保密處理。如有任何疑問，請聯繫何小姐（conniehe@link.cuhk.edu.hk)。
We are inviting Hong Kong primary school students and parents to participate in the pilot study of a leadership cognition study.
Child:
One-on-one online interview (will be recorded), approximately 1 hour.
Parent:
Online questionnaire, approximately 1 hour.
Compensation:
Participants will receive HKD 100 in total.

For enquiries, please write to:

bodyText:

Announcements
[Brief Training Programme for Eating Disorders] Welcome Mandarin Speakers 「进食问题短期训练计划」诚邀普通话参与者 - Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory, Department of Psychology
From: Yanbin, XIE
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ybxie@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
招募参与者：进食问题短期训练计划
香港中文大学临床心理科学实验室团队现正推行一项针对进食问题的短期训练计划，诚邀符合资格的人士参与。
六周指导式自助练习，处理社会评价与自我批评
打破自我批评的恶性循环
找回自我肯定的正向情绪
香港中文大学校园内，全程免费
进食问题很多时候并非只是一个关于食物、身材偏好或者意志力的问题，而关乎我们如何看待自己，以及如何处理和他人的关系。目前，针对进食问题的治疗多采用认知行为取向，研究证实能有效控制非适应性进食行为的出现。本计划是团队基于实证研究开发的新训练方案，采用社会情绪取向，聚焦于处理自己与他人的关系。本项目遵循阶梯式照护模式，定位为指导式自助短期介入方案，旨在以较少的时间投入及心理负担为参加者提供支援。
训练为期6周，包括「每周1次实体会面 + 自助练习 + 线上心理评估访谈及问卷」；训练完成后1个月及6个月进行跟进评估。
「招募要求」
年满18岁或以上；普通话流利；
受进食问题困扰，例如，对进食、体重或体型有过度的关注，进食后感到强烈自责或羞愧，反复出现无法控制的暴食行为，或伴有反复出现的代偿行为（催吐、使用泻药或利尿剂、过度运动等）并因此影响日常生活或情绪；
目前并未接受其他形式的心理治疗或精神科药物治疗；
能够亲身前往香港中文大学校园参与训练。
「报名链接」
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0pJvKNUXXEGYx4G
报名后，我们将联络您安排筛选问卷及访谈，以确认是否适合参加本计划，并邀请符合条件者参与训练。
如有疑问请联络研究团队：epplab.ed@cuhk.edu.hk。
所有个人资料仅用作研究用途，并会严格保密。
临床心理科学实验室团队
Recruiting Participants: Brief Training Programme for Eating Disorders
The Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory at CUHK is currently running a brief training programme for individuals struggling with eating disorders. We are now inviting eligible participants to join.
We all care about how we look. But eating disorders are often about much more than food, body shape, or willpower—they are deeply tied to how we see ourselves and how we relate to others. While cognitive-behavioural therapy (CBT) is the most widely used and evidence-based treatment for eating disorders, our team has developed a new training protocol grounded in recent research, drawing on a socioemotional framework that focuses specifically on self-perception and interpersonal relationships. Following a stepped-care model, this programme is designed as a brief guided self-help intervention, offering meaningful support with a relatively low time commitment and psychological load.
  The programme runs for 6 weeks:
Weekly in-person sessions on campus
Guided self-help practice tasks to complete between sessions
Online assessment interviews and questionnaires
Follow-up evaluations will be conducted at 1 month and 6 months post-training.

Who We're Looking For
Are aged 18 or above;
Are fluent in Mandarin;
Are currently struggling with eating disorder symptoms, for example, excessive evaluation or concerns on food, weight, or body shape, intense guilt or shame after eating, recurrent episodes of binge eating that feel out of control, with compensatory behaviours such as self-induced vomiting, laxative or diuretic misuse, or excessive exercise;
Are not currently receiving any other form of psychological therapy or psychiatric medication;
Are able to attend in-person sessions on the CUHK campus

Sign Up Here
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_0pJvKNUXXEGYx4G
After you sign up, we will contact you to complete a screening questionnaire and a brief interview to see if this programme is a good fit for you. If eligible, you will be invited to join the 6-week training.
 For any questions, feel free to reach out to us at:
epplab.ed@cuhk.edu.hk
All information you provide will be kept strictly confidential and used solely for research screening and intervention purposes.
Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory

For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

Are you the next CUHK Outstanding Student? Apply now for 2026! 香港中文大學傑出學生獎2026－現正接受報名！ - Office of Student Affairs
From: Office of Student Affairs

你是否曾在藝術、創新、體育或社會服務方面發揮所長，創造影響力？歡迎申請
2026 傑出學生獎，與大家分享你的成就和故事！
除了追求學術成就外，香港中文大學(中大)學生亦積極在非學術範疇發揮所長。為表揚在不同領域有傑出表現，並持續為大學社群及社會作出積極貢獻的學生，中大設立「傑出學生獎」，以肯定其成就與貢獻，並鼓勵同學追求卓越、勇於突破自我。
【獎項類別】
藝術
創新與發明
社會服務
體育
特別表現
【申請資格】
在2025–26學年就讀於香港中文大學的全日制本科生或研究生，如於有關學年在上述其中一個範疇取得卓越成就或作出重大貢獻，均符合申請資格。
【截止日期】
2026年9月18日（星期五）中午12時正。
歡迎以個人或團隊形式申請。
【詳情及報名】
https://www.osa.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/osa-application-guideline/
【查詢】
潘小姐(電話：3943 7210；電郵：
gladys@cuhk.edu.hk
)或
陳小姐(電話：3943 1843；電郵：
kimichan@cuhk.edu.hk
)。
誠邀你把握機會展示卓越成就，分享成長歷程，並以自身經驗啟發同儕。
我們期待收到你的報名！

The CUHK Outstanding Students Awards 2026 aim to celebrate students who have demonstrated outstanding achievements and made a positive impact on the University community and society through their dedication, talent, and perseverance.

Arts

Full-time undergraduate and postgraduate students enrolled at CUHK during the 2025–26 academic year who have demonstrated outstanding achievements or made significant contributions in one of the above categories within the same academic year are eligible to apply.

.

除了追求學術成就外，香港中文大學(中大)學生亦積極在非學術範疇發揮所長。為表揚在不同領域有傑出表現，並持續為大學社群及社會作出積極貢獻的學生，中大設立「傑出學生獎」，以肯定其成就與貢獻，並鼓勵同學追求卓越、勇於突破自我。
【獎項類別】
藝術
創新與發明
社會服務
體育
特別表現
【申請資格】
在2025–26學年就讀於香港中文大學的全日制本科生或研究生，如於有關學年在上述其中一個範疇取得卓越成就或作出重大貢獻，均符合申請資格。
【截止日期】
2026年9月18日（星期五）中午12時正。
歡迎以個人或團隊形式申請。
【詳情及報名】
https://www.osa.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/osa-application-guideline/
【查詢】
潘小姐(電話：3943 7210；電郵：
gladys@cuhk.edu.hk
)或
陳小姐(電話：3943 1843；電郵：
kimichan@cuhk.edu.hk
)。
誠邀你把握機會展示卓越成就，分享成長歷程，並以自身經驗啟發同儕。
我們期待收到你的報名！
Are you the next CUHK Outstanding Student?
Apply now for 2026!
Have you made a mark in the arts, innovation, sports, or social service this year? It’s time to be recognized for your passion and achievements!
The CUHK Outstanding Students Awards 2026 aim to celebrate students who have demonstrated outstanding achievements and made a positive impact on the University community and society through their dedication, talent, and perseverance.
【
Award Categories
】
Arts
Innovation and Invention
Social Service
Sports
Special Achievement
【Eligibility】
Full-time undergraduate and postgraduate students enrolled at CUHK during the 2025–26 academic year who have demonstrated outstanding achievements or made significant contributions in one of the above categories within the same academic year are eligible to apply.

Application Deadline
】
18 September 2026 (Friday), 12:00 noon
.
(Applications are welcome from both individuals and teams.)
【

https://www.osa.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/osa-application-guideline/

gladys@cuhk.edu.hk

We look forward to receiving your application!

Announcements
[HK$300]Brain Health Study  [HK$300]中大醫學院邀您參與腦部健康研究 - CUHK Psychiatry Sleep Assessment Unit
From: Wong Yuen Tung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
yuentungwong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
便秘？嗅覺變差？睡覺拳打腳踢？有腦退化家族史？
這些看似平常的小毛病，其實可能是柏金遜症等大腦退化的早期先兆！
提早了解大腦健康，預防神經退化！
中大醫學院睡眠研究小組推出全新手機篩查App，誠邀您參與醫學研究！
研究對象：
年齡介乎
50 至 65 歲
的華人
未確診
任何腦神經退化疾病（如柏金遜症、阿爾茲海默症/失智症等）
參加者需完成以下程序：
參與研究
費用全免
，成功完成相關研究程序者最多可獲
HK$300元超市禮券
作為津貼
階段一：
下載手機程式並完成問卷 （約需 15–20 分鐘）
完成後可獲得早期柏金遜病風險分數
符合資格並完成問卷者可獲 HK$100元超市禮券
階段二：
部分參加者將獲邀進一步參與臨床評估
包括身體檢查、臨床訪談、居家睡眠測試及神經認知測試
符合資格並完成階段二者，可額外獲 HK$200元超市禮券
立刻掃描海報右下方
二維碼 (QR Code)
或
點擊連結
下載程式「柏健通」參與研究
IOS用戶：
https://apps.apple.com/hk/app/%E6%9F%8F%E5%81%A5%E9%80%9A/id1626241589
Android用戶：
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=edu.cuhk.parkinapp.v2
查詢（致電或WhatsApp）：3919 7792 / 5282 5786（研究助理 黃小姐）
Constipated？Weakened sense of smell？Acting out dream during sleep (punching and kicking) ？Having a family history of neurodegenerative disease？
Common issues like these can actually be early warning signs of brain degeneration, including neurodegenerative diseases such as Parkinson’s disease.
Understand your brain health early to prevent neurodegeneration.
Sleep Assessment Unit - Psychiatry, CUHK has launched a brand-new screening App, and we sincerely invite you to join our medical research study.
Target participants：
Chinese aged between 50 to 65 years old
Have NOT been diagnosed
with any neurodegenerative disease (e.g. Parkinson’s disease, Alzheimer’s disease/ Dementia, etc.)
What you will need to do:
Participation is completely free. Those who successfully complete the study procedure can receive up to HK$300 in supermarket voucher as an allowance.
Phase 1:
Download the mobile app "柏健通" and complete the questionnaires (take approximately 15-20 minutes)
An early Parkinson’s disease risk score will be provided upon completion
Eligible participants who complete the questionnaires will receive HK$100 supermarket voucher
Phase 2:
Selected participants will be invited to undergo further clinical assessments
Assessments include physical examination, clinical interviews, sleep studies, and neurocognitive assessments
Eligible participants who complete Phase 2 will receive an additional HK$200 supermarket voucher
Interested parties are welcome to participate by
clicking the links below
or
scanning the QR Code
in the poster to download the "柏健通" mobile application:
IOS users:
https://apps.apple.com/hk/app/%E6%9F%8F%E5%81%A5%E9%80%9A/id1626241589
Android users:
https://play.google.com/store/apps/details?id=edu.cuhk.parkinapp.v2
For details and registration enquiries, please contact our hotline: 39197792 or 5282 5786 (WhatsApp) (Research Assistant, Ms Wong)
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

Calling all CUHK students Join COP31 as a Student Delegate through self-funded participation and gain first-hand insights into global climate action
Successful candidates will attend COP31 for at least four days, with guidance from Professor Amos Tai of the Department of Earth and Environmental Sciences and Professor Yuan Xu of the Department of Geography and Resource Management. Participants will have the chance to connect with global sustainability experts, gain exposure to international climate negotiations, and explore emerging solutions to climate challenges
COP31 dates: 9–20 November 2026
Location: Antalya, Türkiye
ℹ Details and Registration:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13736695
Registration Deadline: 18 September 2026
Should you have any questions, please contact the Social Responsibility and Sustainable Development Office (
srsdo@cuhk.edu.hk
).
各位中大同學注意 歡迎報名成為 COP31中大學生代表，以自費形式參與會議，親身了解全球氣候議題
獲選的同學將有機會參與至少四天的會議，在地球與環境科學系戴沛權教授及地理與資源管理學系徐袁教授的指導下，與全球可持續發展專家交流，了解國際氣候談判，並探索應對氣候挑戰的方案
聯合國氣候變化大會日期：2026年11月9至20日
地點：土耳其安塔利亞
ℹ 詳情及報名：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13736695
截止報名日期：2026年9月18日
如有任何疑問，請聯絡社會責任及可持續發展處（
srsdo@cuhk.edu.hk
）。

From: The Office of the Arts Administrator

cuoaa@cuhk.edu.hk

2026-27 The Friends of the Arts (FTA) 開始接受報名啦！
FTA 定期舉辦多元化藝術活動，帶你走進豐富多彩的藝術世界。從表演藝術、展覽參觀、本地文化遊到藝術工作坊，讓你以不同方式探索藝術、開拓視野。
不論你是資深藝文愛好者，還是初次接觸藝術，都歡迎加入，一同成為 Friends of the Arts！

早鳥會員專屬福利
2026年8月31日或之前完成報名，即可額外獲得 1 個活動名額！
早鳥會員可享：
2張本地演出門票
1張展覽門票
1次文化工作坊/本地文化遊
1個自選 FTA 活動（**睇多套演出，得！睇展覽，得！玩工作坊，得！本地遊，都得！）
其他專屬福利：
會員專屬藝術資訊平台，接收最新藝文訊息
與藝術文化導賞員或資深藝術家交流
與不同科系背景的藝文同好交流
優先參與藝術行政主任辦公室主辦活動
豐富校內學生發展組合(Student Development Portfolio) 紀錄

中大全日制學生

$250

為配合李兆基建築學大樓的建築吊運工程，車站路一段行車道(介乎大學道回旋處及池旁路路口)，將於

相關臨時封路及關閉停車場措施的告示及標誌，將會在受影響路段及停車場入口附近展示及設置。各大學成員及駕駛人士請多加留意屆時的特別交通安排。有關詳情，請參閱附圖。

& Suspension of Carparks at Station Road (2330 hrs on 7 Aug – 0600 hrs on 8 Aug 2026)
To facilitate construction lifting work at Lee Shau Kee Architecture Building, a section of vehicular passage on Station Road (between the roundabout off University Avenue and the road junction at Pond Crescent) will be temporarily closed from
2330 hrs on 7 Aug
(Fri) to 0600 hrs on 8 Aug (Sat)
.
During this period, the section of road affected and carparks at Wu Ho Man Yuen Building, Lee Shau Kee Architecture Building & Shanghai Fraternity Association Research Services Centre will be closed to all vehicular traffic but pedestrians could still walk through the area affected.
Notices and traffic signs for the temporary road closure and suspension of carparks will be displayed in the vicinity of the affected areas and carpark entrances during this period.  Members of the University and all drivers are reminded to pay extra attention to this special traffic arrangement.  Please refer to the attached layout plan for details.

Announcements
【Public Health and Health Service Research】 Student Helper Recruitment | Literature Review, Data Extraction and Fieldwork  - JC School of Public Health and Primary Care
From: Ng Sammi
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
samming001@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
The
JC School of Public Health and Primary Care, CUHK
is recruiting student helpers to support several research projects about health promotion, evidence-based medicine, and Chinese medicine, led by Prof. Martin Chi-sang WONG, Prof. Jason Junjie HUANG, Prof. Claire Chenwen ZHONG.
The main responsibilities may include, but are not limited to:
Data extraction and data entry
Literature review and article screening
Fieldwork and survey data collection
Interview transcription and data management
Other research-related and administrative duties as assigned
This position provides an excellent opportunity for students who are interested in gaining hands-on experience in public health and health services research.
Requirements:
Training will be provided. Students should be responsible, detail-oriented, and committed to completing assigned tasks reliably and on time.
Good communication and organizational skills
Proficiency in English and Chinese
Prefer BSc Public Health, Community Health, & Chinese Medicine, and students from the Faculty of Medicine.
Working arrangements:
Flexible working schedule (We do not have a specific reporting schedule for students. We will reach out personally to coordinate the working schedule)
On-site work (work from home can be arranged depending on project needs)
Training will be provided
Expected Working Period: August 2026 to 2027
Salary (in hourly rate): 64
Application deadline
: Recruit on an ongoing basis
If you are interested, please send your
CV
,
academic programme/year of study
, and
weekly availability
to
samming001@cuhk.edu.hk
. Should you have any questions regarding the position, please feel free to contact us at the same email address.

Announcements
CUHK Mooncakesare now available for order ⭐⭐⭐ 中大愛心月餅現已接受訂購 - Communications and Public Relations Office
From: Communications and Public Relations Office
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
souvenirs@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
中大月餅．愛心傳承
中秋佳節將至，您計劃如何度過這個團圓時刻？不妨與摯愛一同共賞月色、共享溫馨時光，同時也為社會盡一份心意。今年，香港中文大學（中大）特別呈獻一份貼心選擇——「
中大愛心月餅
」。
中大今年再次推出「
中大愛心月餅
」，由社會企業明愛天糧*製作。月餅禮盒以中大重要地標——科學館為主題，在皎潔明月的映襯下，展現中大校園恬靜閒適的醉人景致。
「中大愛心月餅」為一盒四個低糖雙黃白蓮蓉月餅，每盒糖份只有10.8克，
售價
HK$300
。每售出一盒，中大．關懷義工隊就會為沙田、大埔及馬鞍山的獨居長者送上一個「中大愛心月餅」，而收益亦撥捐至「香港中文大學教育基金」，支持大學推動創新教育與體驗式學習項目，旨在優化學生學習體驗，並進一步豐富校園生活，推動全人發展。
當閣下與親友品嚐「
中大愛心月餅
」共賀佳節之時，不但是支持香港社會企業及中大學生，也是分享助人為樂之精神。今年同樣提供速遞送貨服務，數量有限，請即訂購！
*
明愛天糧為社會企業，透過經營烘焙業務，為精神復元人士及其他殘疾人士提供就業及職前訓練機會，協助融入社區生活。
訂購表格:
https://mooncake.cpr.cuhk.edu.hk/ordering/
詳情:
https://mooncake.cpr.cuhk.edu.hk/
查詢: 3943-8642 /
souvenirs@cuhk.edu.hk
截止日期: 2026年8月23日
CUHK Mooncake - Sharing Happiness and Reaching Everyone
Mid-Autumn Festival is just around the corner. How do you plan to spend this joyful time with your loved ones? You can enjoy the beautiful moonlight with the people closest to you, share wonderful moments together, and at the same time extend a helping hand to society. This year, The Chinese University of Hong Kong (CUHK) is bringing you a special choice that can fulfill all these wishes – the
CUHK Mooncakes
.
CUHK has joined hands again with the social enterprise Caritas La Vie* to launch “
CUHK Mooncake
“. The mooncake gift box features the Science Centre, an iconic CUHK landmark, showcasing the tranquil scenery of the CUHK campus under the glow of a bright full moon.
The CUHK Mooncakes come in a box of 4 low-sugar dual-yolk white lotus paste mooncakes, with only 10.8g of sugar per box,
priced at HK$300
. For each box sold, the CUHK • Care Service Team will deliver a free mooncake to the elderly living alone in Shatin, Tai Po and Ma On Shan. Proceeds from the sales will be donated to the “CUHK Education Fund” which provides support to develop education and experiential learning initiatives that aim at enhancing study experience and enriching campus life.
By enjoying “
CUHK Mooncakes
” with your family and friends, you not only support local enterprises and CUHK students but also share the spirit of giving to the community. The CUHK Mooncakes are limited in stock, so please order now!
* Caritas La Vie is a social enterprise that provides job opportunities for the recovering mentally-disabled and self-reliance of people with disabilities through its baking workshop.
Order form:
https://mooncake.cpr.cuhk.edu.hk/ordering/

CUHK Mooncakes

title: ”Forest of Books, Phoenix in Flight: The Art and Life of Ye Lingfeng” Exhibition Talk 3 「藝林擷葉 靈鳳于飛：葉靈鳳的美術與人生」展覽講座（三）
bodyText:

Events / Activities
”Forest of Books, Phoenix in Flight: The Art and Life of Ye Lingfeng” Exhibition Talk 3 「藝林擷葉 靈鳳于飛：葉靈鳳的美術與人生」展覽講座（三） - CUHK Library
From: The Chinese University of Hong Kong Library
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
spc@lib.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
日期：2026年8月20日（星期四）
時間：下午3時至5時
地點：香港中文大學圖書館地下數碼學術研究室
主持：香港中文大學香港文學研究中心主任黃念欣教授
語言：粵語
講題一：【謎一樣的葉靈鳳】
關於葉靈鳳的生平，還有不少細節有待探索和釐清。比方，葉靈鳳最受影響的比亞茲萊作品，在香港中文大學圖書館的葉靈鳳藏書室中不見蹤影；葉靈鳳曾沉迷的藏書票，除了他為自己設計的「鳳凰」藏書票，其他藏品要到2025年上海葉靈鳳誕生一百二十周年展才大量曝光，值得追問：為甚麼？此外，葉靈鳳與魯迅交惡，在一些評論中說成連場筆戰，事實是否如此？這些謎樣的問題，講者嘗試追尋答案。
講者：許迪鏘，香港浸會學院中文系畢業，歷年從事報刊及雜誌編輯工作，公餘參與《大拇指》雜誌、素葉出版社，出版文學期刊和叢書。散文結集有《南村集》、《形勢比人強》等，編有《盧瑋鑾文編年選輯》，另參與《葉靈鳳日記》、《葉靈鳳文存：霜紅室隨筆》、侶倫《向水屋筆語》足本的編訂。
講題二：【滬上眼光，香江版面：葉靈鳳「藏以致用」的文化實踐】
本講座從展覽中的珍貴畫冊與藏書票切入，重新審視南來文人葉靈鳳的報刊文化實踐。葉氏將早年在上海積累的深厚視覺品味與豐富藏書帶到香港，並秉持「藏以致用」的理念，將私人的美術收藏轉化為普及大眾的公共教育資源。
講座聚焦其於四十至五十年代主編的《星島日報》副刊〈藝苑〉與《星島週報》，探討他如何在報紙版面的客觀制約下，透過各種編輯策略，突破報紙線性閱讀的局限，為讀者建構出一個系統化的美術世界。他不降格以求，深信並尊重讀者的審美潛力。這份兼顧專業深度與普及耐心的編輯實踐，至今仍為香港的文學教育與知識普及帶來深刻啟示。
講者：張詠梅，香港中文大學中國語言及文學系高級講師。專研中國語文教學、香港文學。著有《北窗下呢喃的燕語──力匡作品漫談》、《邊緣與中心：論香港左翼小說中的「香港」(1950-1967)》；編《葉靈鳳文存卷一．霜紅室隨筆之藝海書林》（上下冊）、《歲月留情》、《鄉關何處》、《博聞廣識》（共五冊）（合編）及《醒世懵言——懵人日記選》；注釋《葉靈鳳日記》及侶倫《向水屋筆語》增訂注釋版等。
講座報名：
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13737547

[Register Now!] 11 Sept Areas of Excellence (AoE) Use data to transform diabetes care and patient lives Live Webinar Series (2026-2027)  - Hong Kong Institute of Diabetes and Obesity
From: LAU Wing Man
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
hkido@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Dear All,
You’re cordially invited to join
Areas of Excellence (AoE)
Use data to transform diabetes care and patient lives
Live Webinar Series (2026-2027)
with the details below:
Join us for the
Areas of Excellence (AoE) Live Webinar Series (2026-2027)
which we have invited global leaders and experts in biomedical-psychosocial-behavioral science to share the latest knowledge in epidemiology, diagnosis, prevention and treatment from early to late stage in pursuit of the vision of the Lancet Commission Report on diabetes.
In this monthly webinar, we have invited experts to discuss the challenges and opportunities of implementing data-driven diabetes prevention and care and explore opportunities of setting a Global Diabetes Register using the JADE Platform in our common goal of making healthcare sustainable and helping people live a healthy and better life.
Learning objectives
Understand what, why, how, by whom and for whom of setting up diabetes registers
Set up a network of collaborators to establish a multicounty JADE Register with automatic data anonymization, using common protocol to gather real world evidence, share best practices and improve quality of care
Enable researchers and care providers to work collectively to define the clinical profiles of their population, benchmark their care performance, establish biobanks and implement pragmatic clinical studies to address unmet needs
About the speaker
Professor Ronald Ma, Associate Dean (External Affairs) and S.H. Ho Professor of Diabetes, Department of Medicine & Therapeutics, Faculty of Medicine, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, HKSAR, China
Professor Juliana Chan, Professor of Medicine & Therapeutics, Faculty of Medicine, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, HKSAR, China and Director, Hong Kong Institute of Diabetes & Obesity, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, HKSAR, China
Date & time: 11 September 2026 (Friday) | 17:00-18:00 HKT (UTC+8)
Online: via Zoom — link provided upon registration

To learn more, please visit
HERE
Don’t miss this opportunity for setting up the JADE Register at your institution with access to the portal for a trial period to explore feasibility.

Aged 18–35 years
Native speaker of

title: [Brief Psychological Training Programme for Social Anxiety] call for participants [社交焦慮短期訓練] 誠邀符合條件的廣東話母語者參與
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/08/07
»
Announcements
[Brief Psychological Training Programme for Social Anxiety] call for participants [社交焦慮短期訓練] 誠邀符合條件的廣東話母語者參與 - Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory, Department of Psychology
From: Yanbin, XIE
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ybxie@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
招募參與者：社交焦慮短期介入訓練計劃
六週指導式自助練習，處理社會評價與自我批評
打破自我批評的惡性循環
找回自我肯定的正向情緒

香港中文大學校園內，全程免費
香港中文大學臨床心理科學實驗室團隊現正推行一項針對社交焦慮問題的短期介入訓練計劃，誠邀符合資格的人士參與。
社交焦慮不止影響我們如何應對社交場合，亦關乎我們如何看待自己，以及如何與他人建立聯繫。目前，社交焦慮問題的治療多採用認知行為取向，研究證實能有效改善個人在社交情境中的功能表現。本計劃則是團隊基於實證研究開發的新訓練方案，採用社會情緒取向，聚焦於處理個人與自我及他人的關係。本項目遵循階梯式照護模式 (stepped-care model)，定位為指導式自助 (guided self-help) 短期介入方案，旨在以較少的時間投入及心理負擔，為參加者提供有效支援。
訓練為期6週，包括「每週1次實體會面 + 自助練習 + 線上心理評估訪談及問卷」 ； 訓練完成後1個月和六個月進行隨訪評估
 「招募要求」
年滿18歲或以上；廣東話流利；
在社交焦慮方面感到困擾，例如在社交或公開場合強烈緊張焦慮、擔心自己被負面評價、迴避社交場合，並明顯影響工作或學習；
現時並未接受其他形式的心理治療或精神科藥物治療；
能夠親身前往香港中文大學校園參與訓練。

「參與流程」
報名後，我們將聯絡您安排篩選問卷及訪談，以確認是否適合參加本計劃，並邀請符合條件者參與訓練。

「報名連結」
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eDNm9u2HOUkR302
如有疑問，歡迎聯絡研究團隊：cdclabcuhk@gmail.com
本計劃已獲香港中文大學–新界東醫院聯網臨床研究倫理聯席委員會審批（CUHK-NTEC CREC 2025.796）。
所有個人資料僅用作研究篩選及介入用途，並會嚴格保密。
香港中文大學臨床心理科學實驗室團隊
Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory
Recruiting Participants: Brief Psychological Training Programme for Social Anxiety
The Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently conducting a brief intervention programme for individuals experiencing social anxiety difficulties. We invite eligible individuals to participate.
Social anxiety not only affects how we cope in social situations but also involves how we view ourselves and relate to others. While cognitive-behavioural approaches are widely used and evidence-based for treating social anxiety, our team has developed a novel training protocol grounded in empirical research that adopts a social-emotional approach, focusing on improving individuals’ relationships with themselves and with others. Following the stepped-care model, this programme is designed as a brief guided self-help intervention, aiming to provide effective support with minimal time commitment and psychological burden.
The training programme spans 6 weeks and includes:
Weekly in-person sessions (once per week)
Self-help practice exercises
Questionnaire assessments
Follow-up evaluations will be conducted one month and six months after the training.
「Eligibility Criteria」
Aged 18 or above
Fluent in Cantonese
Experiencing significant social anxiety-related distress (e.g., intense anxiety in social or public settings, fear of negative evaluation, avoidance of social situations, with noticeable impact on work or study)
Not currently receiving other forms of psychological therapy or psychiatric medication
Able to attend in-person sessions on the CUHK campus
「Procedures」
After registration, we will contact you to arrange a screening questionnaire and an interview to determine your suitability for the programme. Eligible participants will then be invited to join the training.
「Registration Link」
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eDNm9u2HOUkR302
For enquiries, please contact our research team at: cdclabcuhk@gmail.com
This study has been approved by the Joint CUHK-NTEC Clinical Research Ethics Committee (CUHK-NTEC CREC 2025.796).
All personal data collected will be used solely for research screening and intervention purposes and will be kept strictly confidential.
Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory
The Chinese University of Hong Kong

For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

title: [Tired of Nightmares and Insomnia?] Join Our Free Online Treatment Study 【成日發惡夢又瞓唔著？】全新網上治療研究，6周助你重拾安睡
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/08/07
»
Announcements
[Tired of Nightmares and Insomnia?] Join Our Free Online Treatment Study 【成日發惡夢又瞓唔著？】全新網上治療研究，6周助你重拾安睡 - Department of psychiatry
From: Reyane Ao
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
您是否正飽受
惡夢
與
失眠
的雙重困擾，覺得身心俱疲？
反覆的惡夢有機會加劇失眠問題，導致日頭精神大打折扣。
我們誠邀您參與一項
【網上認知行為療法治療噩夢與失眠共病】臨床研究
。本研究旨在評估一項手機應用程式的自助式網上療程，學習有效改善睡眠、減少惡夢的心理療法。
您的參與不僅有機會能幫助自己重獲優質睡眠，更能推動睡眠醫學的發展，為有同樣困擾的人士帶來新的證據。

我們正在招募
年齡介乎 18 至 64 歲
同時受失眠及惡夢問題困擾
能閱讀繁體中文並以粵語溝通

研究內容包括
臨床訪談及問卷篩查
為期6周網上認知行為治療課程（每週約20-30分鐘課程）
完成治療後的問卷和跟進評估
佩戴睡眠手錶

參與方法
如有興趣，請點擊以下連結，花1-2分鐘填寫篩選問卷：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_dbt7HLJzt16miEK

重要提示
初步符合條件者，我們的研究團隊將在
一個月
內與您聯繫，進行後續評估並詳細說明研究詳情。若未獲通知，暫不符合本次招募範圍，敬請諒解。

查詢及聯絡
如有任何疑問，歡迎通過以下方式聯繫研究團隊：
WhatsApp/電話：6763 1454
電郵：
sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
您提供的所有資料將會嚴格保密，僅供本研究使用。
歡迎將此信息轉發
給可能有需要的人士。感謝您的關注與支持！
Dear Sir/Madam,
Are you struggling with both nightmares and insomnia, feeling mentally and physically exhausted?
Recurring nightmares can make insomnia even worse, severely affecting your sleep quality and leaving you drained during the day.​
We invite you to take part in a clinical study on an
online cognitive behavioural therapy program for co-occurring nightmares and insomnia
. This study aims to evaluate an innovative mobile application–based treatment. Through this free and convenient self-help online program, you can learn evidence-based psychological techniques to improve your sleep and reduce nightmares.​
Your participation not only offers you a chance to achieve better sleep but also contributes to advancing sleep medicine, helping to build new evidence for others facing similar challenges.
Who we are recruiting
​
Aged between 18 and 64
Experiencing both insomnia and recurrent nightmares
Able to read Traditional Chinese and communicate in Cantonese​
What the study involves
​
Clinical interview and screening questionnaires
A 6-week online cognitive behavioural therapy program (requiring approximately 20-30 minutes per week)
Post-treatment questionnaires and follow-up assessments​
Wearing a research-grade sleep monitoring device (activity level tracker)
How to Participate
If you are interested, please click the link below to complete a brief screening questionnaire:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_dbt7HLJzt16miEK
Important Note
Only applicants who preliminarily meet the eligibility criteria will be contacted by our research team within one month for further assessment and a detailed study explanation. We appreciate your understanding.
Enquiries & Contact
For any questions, please feel free to contact our research team, via:
WhatsApp/Phone: 6763 1454
Email: sleepresearch@cuhk.edu.hk
All information you provide will be kept strictly confidential and used solely for research purposes.
Please feel free to share this opportunity
with anyone who might benefit. Thank you for your interest and support!
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

Health Talk organized by Robert Dan Health Education Centre, University Medical Service Office - Understanding Flu and Respiratory Viruses
Our daily environment is filled with airborne respiratory viruses, ranging from the common flu to Respiratory Syncytial Virus (RSV). Their early symptoms are often subtle and easily overlooked. However, they pose a severe threat to vulnerable groups like infants and the elderly, potentially triggering dangerous complications that demand our full attention. This seminar will introduce the characteristics of different respiratory viruses and offer practical defense strategies, empowering you to stay safe and healthy during peak infection seasons.

We are looking for enthusiastic students to join our team as helpers to visit hosiptals, facilitate follow-up and health talk flow! This flexible job opportunity is perfect for students who want to earn extra income in your spare time. This recruitment is for a project related to stroke aimed at raising public awareness about stroke rehabilitation.
Job Responsibilities:
Visit hospitals to assist in recruiting participants for research projects
Assist in promoting stroke prevention knowledge
Support the project team with simple liaison tasks
What We Offer:
Flexible Working Hours:
You can schedule your work hours around your class timetable
Training Sessions:
No prior experience is required; we will provide comprehensive training, including stroke-related knowledge and communication skills, to help you get started quickly
Requirements:
Good communication skills
Fluent in Cantonese
Proactive, willing to learn, and interested in health-related projects
Nursing students will be given priority consideration

研究項目：

Research Project:
Organ Donation Intentions in Hong Kong University Students
您好！我們誠邀香港中文大學的本科生（需為香港永久居民）參與一項關於器官捐贈意向的在線研究實驗。
Hello! We cordially invite
CUHK undergraduate students (must be Hong Kong permanent residents)
to participate in an online research study regarding organ donation intentions.
參與流程與重要說明：
為了確保研究數據的質量與您的填寫體驗，請務必閱讀以下細則：
設備建議：

強烈建議使用電腦
完成本研究。

本研究包含
兩個部分
。參與者必須完成全部兩個部分才能獲得現金補償。

完成第一部分後，需
間隔
24
小時

30-40
分鐘

To ensure the quality of research data and a smooth experience, please read the following details carefully:
Device Recommendation:
To ensure ease of completion and data quality, it is
strongly recommended to use a computer
to complete this study.

This study consists of
two parts
. Participants must complete both parts to be eligible for cash compensation.

24-hour interval
between the first and second parts. Please set aside sufficient time.

30-40 minutes
.

"You are not able to participant this study"
pops up during the process, it indicates that you have not passed the screening or have lost eligibility, and no compensation will be provided.

informed consent form
.

100
港幣

Upon completing both stages of the experiment, you will receive
HKD 100 in cash
as monetary compensation.
Note: If you have already participated in this experiment, please do not sign up again. Duplicate registrations will be considered invalid.

持有香港永久居民身份的香港中文大學在讀本科生 。

not

Multicultural Psychological Support Service: Counselling Service for Non-Local Students
No matter where we come from, we all desire to express our emotional needs with no barrier. Speaking in our mother tongue with someone who shares our cultural background not only allows us to better articulate ourselves but also fosters a deeper sense of understanding.
In order to support CUHK non-local students, the Wellness and Counselling Centre (WACC) of the Office of Student Affairs (OSA) offers Multicultural Psychological Support Service. This service allows students to receive counselling services in a comfortable environment.
The service is provided by St John’s Cathedral Counselling Service, and it is available to all CUHK full-time non-local students. The counsellors from St John’s Cathedral Counselling Service are capable of providing counselling services in English or Putonghua, as well as other languages including English, Putonghua, French, German, Dutch, Spanish, Hindi, Indonesian, Japanese, Portuguese, Korean, Urdu, Russian, Sindhi and Tagalog (subject to counsellor’s availability). Below are the specific details of the services provided:
Location:
St John’s Cathedral Counselling Service
Address:
10th Floor, Two Chinachem Plaza, 68 Connaught Road, Central
Website:
https://www.sjccs.hk/
Service Period:
July 2026 to June 2027
Opening hours:
9AM to 9PM Monday to Saturday, except on Public Holiday
Service Target:
All CUHK full-time non-local students, including exchange students.
Local students with extensive exposure to cultural experiences outside Hong Kong are also eligible (e.g. with international school backgrounds, or ethnic minorities born in Hong Kong).
Session:
6 counselling sessions
For more information about the Multicultural Psychological Support Service, please visit
OSA WACC website
or contact WACC staff at 3943 9951 or 3943 7208.
How can I make an appointment?
Enroll online by webform:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13733096
If you have an urgent need to see a counsellor, you may visit WACC during office hours. The Duty Counsellor will assess your needs and make appropriate arrangements with you. If you need emotional support during non-office hours, please call the CUHK 24-hour Emotional Support Hotline at 5400 2055 (exclusively for CUHK Full-time Students and Part-time PGDE Students).
Enquiries:
Contact number: 3943 9951/ 3943 7208
Email:
mpss@cuhk.edu.hk
/
wacc@cuhk.edu.hk
Best regards,
Multicultural Psychological Support Service (MPSS)
Wellness and Counselling Centre
Office of Student Affairs
3/F Pommerenke Student Centre, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shatin, N.T.
T: +852 3943 9951   E:
mpss@cuhk.edu.hk
多元文化心理支援服務
為非本地學生提供母語輔導服務
無論來自哪裡，我們都渴望輕鬆地表達感受。用母語與有相似文化背景的人交談，不僅讓我們能清楚表達自己，還可增強更深層次的理解。為支援非本地同學，學生事務處心理健康及輔導中心推出「多元文化心理支援服務」，讓同學可在舒服自在的情況下打開心扉。
輔導服務由中環聖約翰座堂輔導服務提供，服務對象為所有香港中文大學全日制非本地學生。輔導員除了能提供以英語或普通話為母語的輔導服務外，亦能以法語、德語、荷蘭語、西班牙語、印地語、印尼語、日語、葡萄牙語、韓語、烏爾都語、俄語、信德語和他加祿語等其他語言進行輔導。服務詳情如下：
服務提供者：
聖約翰座堂輔導服務中心
服務地址：
中環幹諾道中
68
號華懋廣場Ⅱ期
10
樓
網址：
https://www.sjccs.hk/
服務時段：
2026年7月至2027年六月
營業時間：
週一至週六上午 9 時至晚上 9 時，公眾假期除外
服務對象：
香港中文大學全日制非本地學生，包括交換生
本地學生如有豐富的非本地文化背景（如曾就讀國際學校，或在香港出生的少數族裔人士）亦可申請
輔導次數：
提供6次輔導服務
有關「多元文化心理支援服務」的詳情，請瀏覽
學生事務處心理健康及輔導中心網頁
或致電3943 9951或3943 7208向心理健康及輔導中心職員查詢。
如何預約輔導服務？
於網上預約:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13733096
如急需與輔導員見面，可於辦公時間內到訪位於龐萬倫學生中心2樓的心理健康及輔導中心。當值的輔導員會評估同學的需要，並作出適當的安排。如欲在非辦公時間尋求情緒支援，歡迎致電中大24小時情緒支援熱線5400 2055（僅供中文大學全日制學生及兼讀制學位教師教育文憑學生使用）。

本證書課程以參加國家語委普通話水平測試（PSC）為導向，旨在提高學員普通話應用水平，具體表現為：提高學員普通話朗讀能力，掌握普通話水平測試常用詞匯，掌握朗讀規定篇目的方法，讀準字音，讀通作品。同時，提高學員使用普通話所達到的流利程度和規範程度，掌握普通話水平測試應試的技巧，做好測試前的準備；並幫助參加過測試的應試人進一步提升等級，説話時，逐步做到語音標準，語調自然，表達流暢。本證書課程不是零起點課程，學員須具有基礎普通話能力。

title: Violinists, Cellists, Conductors & Audiences, We Need You! Join a Music & Brain Study: Earn HK$200 in 1–2 Hours 識拉小提琴／大提琴？識指揮？或者想聽音樂？參加音樂與大腦研究，1–2小時即享HK$200！
bodyText:

2026/08/07

Announcements
Violinists, Cellists, Conductors & Audiences, We Need You! Join a Music & Brain Study: Earn HK$200 in 1–2 Hours  識拉小提琴／大提琴？識指揮？或者想聽音樂？參加音樂與大腦研究，1–2小時即享HK$200！ - Brain and Mind Institute
From: Jim Lau
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
jimlau117@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學大腦與認知研究所將進行一項音樂研究，現正招募小提琴/大提琴演奏者，指揮家及聽眾。只需要親臨研究所1次，全程約一到兩個小時。
參加條件：
1）14歲或以上
2）慣用手為右手
3）無神經或精神疾病史
4） 如果作爲小提琴或大提琴演奏者報名，需要達到相關樂器的ABRSM Grade 8或同等水平
5）如果作爲樂隊指揮報名，需要具備相關專業資質，例如指揮課程項目、工作坊或培訓，并具有樂團指揮的相關經驗。
實驗內容：
參與我們的研究，您將有機會以音樂家的身份參與實驗室場景的小型音樂會。演奏者將在實驗前收到兩段樂譜，每段約5分鐘。他們需要事先練習樂譜，并在實驗中與另外的演奏者合作完成演奏。聽眾則會根據演奏表現，實時評分。實驗中，我們將使用安全無害的近紅外設備（LED光）記錄您的腦部神經活動。
參與報酬：
作爲演奏者或指揮參與研究可獲得200元。
作爲聽眾參與研究可獲得100元。
地點：
香港中文大學許讓成樓 4/F
如有興趣參加，可以通過以下鏈接報名，我們會聯絡您安排實驗的日期和時間:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_8jqjr7LjnZChmn4
The Brain and Mind Institute is conducting a brain study involving musical performance and is now recruiting violinists, cellists, conductors and audiences. Participation requires only one visit, lasting approximately one to two hours.
Requirements:
We are currently recruiting violinists, cellists, conductors and audiences, who meet the following criteria:
•           Age range: age 14 or above
•           Right-handed
•           No history of neurological or psychiatric diseases
•           If you are interested in signing up as a violinist or cellist, it is required that you have achieved ABRSM Grade 8 or an equivalent level of proficiency.
•           Conductors should have formal training (e.g., programs, workshops, seminars) and practical experience with ensembles or orchestras.
Study details:
Participate in our music study where you will have the opportunity to take part in a concert within laboratory settings as a musician. Musicians will be provided with two sections of music scores prior to the experiments, each lasting approximately 5 minutes. They will need to practice the scores and perform them with other musicians during the experiment. Audiences will listen to the performance, and rate it on the go. Throughout the study, we will utilize fNIRS (functional near-infrared spectroscopy) to record your brain activities. This will allow us to gain valuable insights into the neural processes involved in musical collaboration.
Compensation:
People who take part in this study as violinists, cellists, or conductors will receive
200 HKD
upon completion of the tasks.
People who take part in this study as audiences will receive
100 HKD
upon completion of the tasks.
Venue
:
4F, Hui Yeung Shing Building, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
If you are interested in participating in this study, please complete the form by clicking the following link:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_8jqjr7LjnZChmn4
Please contact Jim Lau at
jimlau117@cuhk.edu.hk
if you have any questions.

From: Xi Cheng

***Please Note that this study requires reading Chinese words, so we would like to invite students who are native Cantonese speakers to participate.***
教育心理學系謝志成教授一項關於中文複合詞的研究誠意邀請與會者參與。
對象：
**參加者需為粵語是母語的本港學生；
**參與者需要有良好的視力或矯正視力；
**參與者需慣性用右手。
**參與者年齡需大於18嵗。
研究內容：整個實驗將為期三節（每節之間間隔不超過一星期）進行，每節需要 1 至 1.5 小時，完成3節後可得到250港元作為現金補償。
地點：陳國本樓707E室
參與方式：如有興趣，請點此連結報名https://forms.gle/znR7QB79PVof2F87A
（報名時個人資料包括：姓名、學號、性別、年齡、學系、年級、聯絡電話、聯絡電郵。）
有興趣的同學請提供每週至少兩個時間段，以便安排。
*若閣下沒有收到我們的電郵，代表所選的時間已額滿，多謝！
*若已參加過【對於中文複合詞所表達的情感】的研究，請勿重複報名。
如果對實驗有任何疑問，歡迎聯絡
xicheng3@cuhk.edu.hk
。

心裡一直有把聲音告訴你不夠好？因此感到困擾，並想要減少批評自己？

Magic Chair Experiment – Recruitment of participants 
Is there an inner voice keep telling you that you are good enough? You feel distressed about this and wish to stop criticizing yourself?
Experimental Psychopathology and Psychotherapy Laboratory, Department of Psychology at CUHK, is inviting you to join this interesting study.
We would like to know more about how people’s inner voice and interaction within oneself when facing struggles, and how these inner voice affects individual’s mental health.
You will receive a personalized questionnaire report after finishing the study.
 Eligible participants:
Aged 18 or above
Able to speak and understand Cantonese
Distressed about self-criticism
Only
male
 Study Overview:
Online questionnaire before the experiment
In-person experiment at the laboratory (lasts for approximately 1.5 hour)
Follow-up online questionnaire at 2 weeks after the experiment
 Location: Room 102, Wong Foo Yuan Building, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shatin, N.T., Hong Kong SAR
 If you are interested in this study, please click the link below for application.
https://esurvey.psy.cuhk.edu.hk/jfe/form/SV_eJcE6LGxl0xhfW6
This study is approved by the Survey and Behavioral Research Ethics (SBRE) of the Chinese University of Hong Kong.

.

From: Queenie Chow
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
literacy@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
誠邀閣下與子女參與一項關於華語兒童中英數能力的跨學科大型研究，詳情如下：
對象：
幼稚園高班至六年級單生兒和雙胞胎學生（包括同卵雙生和異卵雙生）
學童家長
學童需以廣東話為母語，並在香港居住 2.5 年以上
目的：
建立學童在中、英文讀寫和數學能力發展的多模態模型，以及設計能夠全面反映兒童在這三方面表現的網上測試工具
研究內容：
第一部分
學童：中英文和數學能力的測試
，分成網上測試和面對面測試兩部分。網上測試分為六個區域，各需時約40分鐘。網上測試毋須一次完成，參加者可自行安排時間分段執行，在四星期內完成所有項目即可。
面對面測試在網上測試完成後另約時間進行，約需45分鐘
家長：
在網上測試平台接受
約
15
分鐘的語文及數學測試
，及填寫關於學童學習情況與家庭語言環境的
問卷
*
現在報名的幼稚園高班至六年級學童只需完成今年一次測試
第二部分（可選擇是否參與）
學童：腦電圖測試（EEG），約2小時
報酬：每年測試完結後將收到：
(1) 測試結果的個人報告；(2) 港幣200元超級市場現金券；(3) 小禮物，
參與腦電圖 (EEG) 部份的學生另有250元超級市場現金券
研究詳情及報名請見以下網頁：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_4OWk4Rmnmb0M20e
如對是項研究有任何疑問或查詢，歡迎聯絡本項目的首席研究員Urs Maurer教授（電郵: umaurer@cuhk.edu.hk）或研究小組（電話：3943-4379；電郵：
lifespandevlab.cuhk@gmail.com
）。
We are recruiting for a multi-disciplinary study about the Chinese, English, and Mathematical abilities among Chinese-speaking children in Hong Kong. Details are as below:
Target participants:
Singletons and twins (both identical and fraternal) from K3 to P6 in the 2025/26 school year
Students’ parents
The child participant must be a native Cantonese speaker and have lived in Hong Kong for more than 2.5 years.
Content:
Part 1
Students
: A series of assessments on Chinese, English, and mathematics on the project’s online testing platform. The tasks are divided into six portions; each takes about 40 minutes to finish. Online testing can be completed at your own pace, as long as all tasks are completed within 4 weeks.
A follow-up face-to-face session (45 minutes) will be arranged upon completion of the online testing.
Parents
: Short online testing on language and mathematics abilities (15 minutes), as well as a set of questionnaires on children’s learning and home language environment
*For current registration
s, students from K3 to P6 only need to complete the test once this year.
Part 2 (optional)
Students: electroencephalography (EEG) test (~2 hour)
Rewards: After each round of testing, participants will receive:

Announcements
Microsoft Copilot Chat Tips Create Perfect Meeting Agendas  - ITSC
From: ITSC
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
itsc@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Let's be honest — nobody loves a meeting that drags on with no direction!
Copilot Chat
can help you create structured, time-boxed agendas with clear talking points so every meeting is focused, productive, and (dare we say) actually enjoyable. Your team will thank you!
Try this prompt — copy & paste it!
“Create a 45-minute meeting agenda for a monthly project status review with 8 attendees. Include: opening & recap (5 min), progress updates from 3 workstreams, discussion of blockers, and action item assignment. For each section, include the time allocation, who should lead it, and key questions to address.”
Why this works:
Including the meeting duration, number of attendees, and specific sections gives Copilot the blueprint to create a truly useful agenda. The more structure you provide, the more polished the result!

Bonus tip:
Want to start your meeting on a high note? Add:
“Also suggest 2 icebreaker questions to start the meeting on a positive note!”
A little fun goes a long way!
More Tips & Resources
Looking for more ways to level up your Copilot game? Check out previous

for even more helpful guidance and best practices.

From: Jelina Wu

【靈感「卡」住咗｜圖卡對話，照見關係中的真實自我】
【OH! Inspiration | Image Card Dialogue: Reflecting the True Self in Relationships】
​喺人際互動入面，我哋成日不知不覺背負咗他人嘅期望、自己設下嘅框架。究竟呢啲無形嘅枷鎖，點樣影響我哋同自己、同他人嘅關係？「靈感卡住咗」工作坊將透過 OH卡嘅直覺連結，同你一齊揭開微妙情緒，重新探索：被隱藏嘅真實自我渴望點樣嘅對話？
In interpersonal interactions, we often unconsciously carry the expectations of others and the boundaries we set for ourselves. How do these invisible shackles affect our relationships with ourselves and others? The "Stuck on Inspiration" workshop uses the intuitive connections of OH Cards to uncover subtle emotions with you, re-exploring: What kind of dialogue does your hidden, true self long for?
​參與者只需帶住好奇心，喺安全嘅交流空間入面，一齊照見關係入面嘅自己。
Participants only need to bring their curiosity to reflect upon themselves within relationships in a safe space for exchange.
​ 對象 / Target Audience: 15–30歲｜名額8人 / Ages 15–30 | Capacity: 8 people
​ 日期 / Dates: 2026年8月4日、25日（星期二） / August 4 & 25, 2026 (Tuesdays)

Follow 1 Month 1 Art on Instagram (@1month1art) or Facebook, and like a post you find interesting to register at a special discounted price of $20! Participants must show proof before the activity begins.

填妥Google Form報名表，並按指示完成付款程序。名額有限，先到先得！

Prof. Nelson Yeung at the Jockey Club School of Public Health and Primary Care is conducting a study that need part-time research helpers with participant recruitment.
The study examines the supportive care needs of Chinese women who have experienced pregnancy loss. Supported by the Student Campus Training and Service Award Scheme 2026-2027 by the United College, we are recruiting part-time student helpers to assisted with the project. This position provides valuable hands-on experience in public health and health-related research.
Responsibilities may include:
Recruit study participants at the Department of Obstetrics and Gynaecology:
Prince of Wales Hospital (5/F, Block E)
Queen Mary Hospital (5/F, Block K)
Assist with data collection
Working hours are mainly on weekday mornings (approximately 7:45-9:00 a.m.)
Participating in training sessions provided before commencement of duties
Eligibility:
Undergraduate students affiliated with the United College (due to the terms and conditions of the Award Scheme).
Students who have psychological or health-related research experience are preferable.
Students who are able to work on regular basis are preferable.
Due to the project nature, female students who are fluent in Cantonese are preferable.
Up to HK$160 per successfully recruited participant with completed data collection.
Interested students may complete the attached google form for applications.

From: Wikie Chan

How can AI enhance educational feedback without replacing the human touch in teaching?
GenAI is shifting the dynamic in higher education—moving beyond simple automation towards hybrid intelligence, where educators and AI work together to deliver personalised, learner-centred feedback.
Join us for an upcoming talk with Dr Guanliang CHEN, Senior Lecturer at Monash University's Centre for Learning Analytics.
Drawing from systematic reviews and empirical studies, Dr CHEN will cover:
The evolution from AI-generated feedback to AI-supported analysis of feedback quality
How educators and AI can collaborate effectively in the classroom
Edvance, a state-of-the-art feedback platform that showcases how GenAI can augment teaching expertise rather than replace it
Date: Tuesday, 11 August 2026
Time: 12:15 pm – 1:30 pm (UTC+8) | 2:15 pm – 3:30 pm (UTC+10)

Announcements
【$200 Coupon】Recruiting Children (aged 4 or under) for the Gut Microbiome and At-risk Children's Brain Development Study 誠意邀請5歲以下兒童參加腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Dr. WONG Wing Ho, Oscar
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
hatch@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
家長您好，我們是香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系的研究團隊。本研究由香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系、內科及藥物治療學系統籌。
本研究團隊誠邀5歲以下兒童參與一項有關腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究。此研究希望透過收集小朋友之大便及口腔樣本，幫助了解腸道微生態與大腦發展的關係。
研究對象:
1) 確診/懷疑小朋友有自閉症傾向或其他發展問題
2) 4歲或以下的小朋友 (交齊問卷和樣本的日子未滿5歲即可)
3) 父母皆為華裔或亞裔人士
4) 小朋友18歲以下的兄弟姊妹
以下為是次研究需要完成的事項：
1) 簽署參加同意書
2) 網上問卷調查：網上問卷主要詢問小朋友的行為及腸道情況，填寫時間約45分鐘
3) 收集大便和口腔樣本：我們會給家長一個樣本收集包，請家長使用收集包內的物在家中資協助收集樣本
4) 飲食習慣的問卷：記錄小朋友的飲食習慣
完成研究後，參加者可以獲得$200的超市現金券、 G-NiiB益生菌試用裝和腸道健康報告作為答謝 另外，家長有機會被邀請進行面談並隨訪2年,如有需要我們會提供轉介信。是次研究是自願參與性質參與，這個研究期間所取得的資料都會被嚴格保密。
如家長有意願參與此項研究，請填寫以下網上篩選問卷(https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o)。收到問卷回覆後，我們會再與合適參加是次研究的小朋友之家長連絡。
如果家長對研究細節有任何疑問，歡迎透過WhatsApp 6099-3064或致電 2607-6057與我們聯絡。
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Parents,
We are a team of researchers from the Department of Psychiatry at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. We are conducting a research project jointly organised by the Department of Psychiatry, the Department of Medicine and Therapeutics of the Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Our team sincerely invites your children to participate in research on gut microbiome and children's brain development. Through collecting stool and buccal samples, we aim to investigate the relationship between gut microbiome and brain development.
A gut health report will be provided, A G-Niib probiotics trial pack and a $200 supermarket voucher will be awarded to participants.
Target participants:
1) The child is diagnosed/suspected to have autism or other developmental problems
2) The child is 4 years old or under (all questionnaires and samples are submitted before 5 years old)
3) Both parents are Chinese or Asian
4) Children’s brothers and sisters under 18 years old are also welcome to join
Procedures and details of this Study:
1) Research Consent
2) Online Questionnaire : A 45-minute questionnaire on children’s behaviors and their physical health condition
3) Stool and Buccal Sample Collection: Samples collection kit will be provided for sample collection at home
4) Dietary Questionnaire: Recording children's eating habits
You will receive a $200 supermarket voucher after completing all the research procedures. Participation is voluntary, and your responses will be kept confidential. The information you provide will be used solely for research purposes.
If you are interested in participating in our research study, please fill out the following online questionnaire (https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o). We will contact you afterwards if your children are suitable to join this study.
For inquiries, please contact 2607-6057 or WhatsApp 6099-3064.

From: Tong Shuk Fan
