實驗對象:
年齡介乎 18 至 60 歲
目前沒有肌肉骨骼疼痛或受傷
沒有髖關節、踝關節、足部或腰椎疼痛
具輕度至中等程度的身體活動量
每位參與者將進行一系列受控的下肢功能性任務，包括單腳下台落地測試、上落台階、深蹲、反向跳躍及步行。
本實驗共一節。 一節會持續2.5-3小時。 完成實驗可獲港幣$195 （$65/小時）。
如您有興趣參與本研究，請填寫以下網上申請表格。
https://forms.gle/6CPncrAofAWLdsqL7
本實驗名額有限。 我們會透過電郵/訊息來確認你是否獲接納。 如果你在報名後兩周沒有收到來自我們的消息，代表你的報名不成功。
如需知道更多詳情，可以透過電郵聯絡唐淑芬博士 (fannytong@cuhk.edu.hk）
Requirement:
Age 18-30 years
No current musculoskeletal pain or injury
No pain in the hips, ankles, feet, or lumbar spine
Mildely to moderately physically active
Each participant will perform a series of controlled lower-limb tasks, including single leg drop landing, step-up and step-down, squats, countermovement jump and walking.
The experiment consists of 1 session. The session lasts for 2.5-3 hours. Upon completion, participants will be rewarded with $195 HKD ($65/hour).
If you are interested in applying for the above position, please fill in the online application form below:
https://forms.gle/6CPncrAofAWLdsqL7
This study has a limited quota. We will contact you directly through email/messages if you are recruited. If you do not hear from us within two weeks after your application, you may consider the application unsuccessful.

Announcements
Part-time Teaching Assistants (Student Helper) for MSc in Sustainable Urban Planning – Term 1, 2026/27  - Department of Geography and Resource Management
From: Department of Geography and Resource Management
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
calvin.chung@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Part-time Teaching Assistants for MSc in Sustainable Urban Planning – Term 1, 2026/27
Application deadline: 10 Aug 2026
The Department of Geography and Resource Management (GRM) invites applications for Part-time Teaching Assistant (TA) positions for the following courses in the MSc in Sustainable Urban Planning (SUP) programme for Term 1 of the 2026/27 academic year:
SDUP5101 Sustainable Development and Planning – 1 TA
SDUP5104 Urban and Regional Economics – 1 TA
SDUP5201 Spatial Planning Studio I – 2 TAs
For course description and specific TA requirements, please see
here
.
Duties and Responsibilities
Assist in the design and preparation of teaching materials within the overall course framework.
Plan and facilitate tutorials, seminars, and/or computer-based laboratory sessions in accordance with the course objectives and guidance provided by the course teacher.
Mark student assignments and assessments, and provide timely and constructive feedback to support student learning and development.
Attend meetings and briefings organised by the course teacher and/or programme, including those related to course planning and administrative matters necessary for the effective delivery of the course.
Perform other course-related tasks as assigned by the course teacher and/or programme.
Requirements
Applicants should:
Be currently enrolled as a full-time PhD student at CUHK.
Have completed at least one workshop under the Improving Postgraduate Learning (IPL) programme offered by the Centre for Learning Enhancement And Research (CLEAR):
https://clear.cuhk.edu.hk/web/professional-development-pd/professional-development-course-for-tas/
Demonstrate excellent written and spoken English communication skills.
Possess strong organisational and time-management skills.
Have relevant knowledge and skills appropriate to the course(s) taught.
Show enthusiasm for teaching and supporting student learning.
A
ppointment Period and Workload
Successful applicants will be required to work for 40 hours between 1 September 2026 and 31 December 2026, according to the schedule determined by the course teacher. Duties may be required both within and outside scheduled class contact hours, subject to the operational needs of the course.
Remuneration and payroll arrangements
The total remuneration for each appointment is HK$6,400 for 40 hours of service, equivalent to HK$160 per hour. The remuneration will be arranged via Student Helper Engagement Scheme (SHES): https://www.osa.cuhk.edu.hk/programmes/student-helper-engagement-scheme/
Application Procedure
To apply, please complete the application form (
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13737529
) and submit the following documents by 10 August 2026:
A CV (1–2 pages), highlighting skills and experience relevant to the TA position; and
Written approval from your supervisor confirming support for the appointment
Applicants may indicate a preferred course. While preferences will be considered where possible, applications will be assessed against all available TA positions. Successful applicants may therefore be offered a course other than their stated preference, based on their qualifications and experience. Applicants will be notified of the outcome by email.
For enquiries, please send to Professor Calvin Chung, Acting Programme Director, at calvin.chung@cuhk.edu.hk.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

2026-2027 Voluntary User-Pay Dental Service Scheme (VUPDSS)
Voluntary User-Pay Dental Service Scheme (VUPDSS) is a voluntary and self-paid dental service between the University’s members and the service providers, Health & Care Dental Services Limited and Quality HealthCare Dental Services Limited. Its primary purpose is to provide participants the additional convenience of receiving dental service at contracted dental clinics outside campus at concessionary rate. Full-time students, full-time staff and dependents, eligible retirees and dependents can enroll in the Scheme. The Scheme is open for application. Membership is valid from 1 September 2026 to 31 August 2027.
Details of the Scheme is available at:
https://www.umso.cuhk.edu.hk/form-download/
2026-2027 自費牙科服務計劃
「自費牙科服務計劃」為一個自願性付費形式的牙齒保健計劃。 合資格大學成員可參加由恒健牙科服務有限公司及卓健牙科服務有限公司所提供的牙科保健服務。 本計劃旨在為參加者提供一個具彈性及享有優惠價格之牙科服務。 全日制學生、全職職員及家屬、合資格退休員工及家屬均可參加。 計劃現正接受申請，會籍有效期由2026年9月1日至2027年8月31日。
計劃詳情，請瀏覽網頁:
https://www.umso.cuhk.edu.hk/hk/form-download/

New ASEI Courses: ASEI3010 Rocket and Spacecraft Dynamics 火箭和航天器動力學 & ASEI3020 Earth & Space Sensor Systems 地球與太空觀測傳感器系統  - Aerospace Science and Earth Informatics & X Double Major Programme
From: Aerospace Science and Earth Informatics & X Double Major Programme
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
aseidm@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
The
Aerospace Science and Earth Informatics & X Double Major Programme (ASEIDM)
is pleased to announce the launch of two exciting new courses in
2026-27 Term 1
. These courses are designed to equip students with advanced knowledge and practical insights into the rapidly growing aerospace and space technology sectors.
ASEI3010 Rocket and Spacecraft Dynamics 火箭和航天器動力學
This course introduces the fundamental dynamics of rockets and spacecraft. It focuses on how to design and analyze orbital trajectories and maneuvers using the two‑body problem. Students will also learn the basics of spacecraft attitude representation, attitude determination, and the related dynamics. The course emphasizes analytical methods, complemented by commonly used numerical techniques.
Pre-requisite(s): ENGG1125 or MATH1010 or MATH1510 or MATH1520
Course Instructor: Dr. Boris Yim;
borisyim@cuhk.edu.hk
ASEI3020 Earth & Space Sensor Systems 地球與太空觀測傳感器系統
Sensors are humanity’s primary interface with the Earth, space environment, and the universe. From observing the Earth’s surface and atmosphere, to measuring the near-Earth space environment, exploring planetary surfaces, and detecting extremely weak signals from deep space, sensor systems enable scientific discovery and engineering applications across aerospace and Earth informatics. This course introduces the principles, system-level design considerations, and applications of sensor systems used for Earth observation, space environment monitoring, planetary exploration, and astronomical observation. Emphasis is placed on understanding sensing concepts through real-world constraints, uncertainty, and design trade-offs. By examining sensors across different physical environments, students will develop an integrated and practical understanding of how sensing systems are designed, deployed, and interpreted in aerospace missions. The course is designed for upper-level undergraduate students and aims to bridge foundational science with mission-oriented thinking, preparing students for advanced studies and interdisciplinary applications in aerospace science and Earth informatics.
Course Instructor: Prof. Zherong Wu;
zherongwu@cuhk.edu.hk
Whether you are passionate about space exploration, satellite systems, Earth observation, or cutting-edge technology, these courses offer a unique opportunity to broaden your horizons and strengthen your academic portfolio.
We warmly encourage eligible students to consider enrolling in ASEI3010 and ASEI3020 during the 2026-27 Term 1 course registration period.

title: Recruitment of insomnia patients for pilot trials – Examining acoustic stimulation for improving sleep quality (earn $600 coupon)
bodyText:
Mass Mail System
Mass Mail System
Digest of CUHK Mass Mails for Undergraduate Students
»
2026/08/07
»
Announcements
Recruitment of insomnia patients for pilot trials – Examining acoustic stimulation for improving sleep quality (earn $600 coupon)  - Department of Psychiatry
From: Orion Yeung; Chris Chan
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155249610@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
晚上睡不著好難受
?
吃安眠藥沒有用？快點來試試新方法
，失眠研究受試者招募中
聲音刺激 (acoustic stimulation) 是一種全新的干預手段，初步研究已表明經特殊處理的低頻聲波在深度睡眠期間出現，可有望改善睡眠品質。本研究用於調查聲音刺激是否能顯著改善失眠症狀，現招募符合以下條件的人群參與研究：
18至45歲成年人
無嚴重精神障礙疾病
確診患有失眠症（即出現失眠症狀，每週發作至少三次，持續不少於三個月，並對日間工作、學習或社交造成影響）
能閱讀繁體中文或廣東話
研究流程
:
佩戴14天體動手錶、填寫睡眠日記。
於第八日上午前往沙田醫院7樓睡眠研究室，進行全日檢測（認知測試、情緒睡眠評估、問卷填寫）, 當晚接受多導睡眠檢查。聲音刺激有機會在深度睡眠期出現。
翌日早晨出院 （可提供病假紙）。
完成整個研究，即可獲得一份由專家出具的專屬睡眠報告 & 價值600的購物禮券，如你對研究感興趣，可點選以下連結報名，我們將在兩個工作日以內聯繫符合條件的報名者。
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_e5S9kPsMPTcGbJQ
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Struggling to fall asleep at night? Feeling distressed by insomnia? Are sleeping medications not helping? We invite you to try a new approach!
Participant recruitment for an insomnia research study is now open.
Acoustic stimulation
is a novel intervention method. Preliminary studies suggest that specially processed low-frequency sound waves delivered during deep sleep may help improve sleep quality. This study aims to investigate whether acoustic stimulation can significantly alleviate symptoms of insomnia.
We are now recruiting participants who meet the following criteria:
Adults aged
18 to 45
No history of severe psychiatric disorders
Diagnosed with
insomnia disorder
(i.e., experiencing insomnia symptoms at least three times per week for a minimum of three months, with negative impact on daytime work, study, or social functioning)
Able to read Traditional Chinese or Cantonese
Study Procedures
Wear an
actigraphy watch for 14 days
and complete a
sleep diary
On the morning of Day 8, attend the
Sleep Research Laboratory, 7/F Sha Tin Hospital
for a full-day assessment, including:
Cognitive testing
Mood and sleep evaluations
Questionnaire completion
Overnight
polysomnography (sleep study)
Acoustic stimulation may be delivered during deep sleep
Discharge the following morning (
medical leave certificate can be provided
)
Participant Benefits
Upon completion of the entire study, you will receive:
A
personalized sleep report
prepared by experts
A
$600 supermarket shopping voucher

For enquiries, please write to:

Announcements
Male Mandarin Native Speakers: Language Processing Lab Study  【男性普通话母语者招募中】你的大脑是怎么读中文的？来实验室告诉我们 - Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
From: Yiting WANG
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
1155200974@link.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
你好！
想不想知道你的大脑如何读中文？
我们正在招募
男性普通话母语者
参与脑电实验，任务很简单：
来实验室看一些中文句子
。我们会记录你的脑电波，看看母语阅读时大脑有多忙碌！
本实验室使用临床级安全的脑电图系统，收集人自身产生的微弱生物电并绘制成波形图，不会对人体产生伤害。有任何安全顾虑都可以和研究人员联系了解：Miss WANG, 1155200974@link.cuhk.edu.hk
实验时长
：约1.5小时
实验内容：
1）佩戴脑电设备，参加互动实验，阅读一些汉语句子并用键盘按键做出反应；2）填写一些问卷。
实验地点：
中文大学梁銶琚楼G层（语言学系）G34实验室。
实验结束后，会通过转数快支付
120
港元
被试费用。
参与者需要符合以下要求
：
1.
男性
，
18-25岁
，来自中国大陆，母语为汉语普通话；
2. 视力（矫正后）正常，无干涩等眼部不适；
3. 听力正常；
4. 无脑损伤、癫痫等神经类疾病，无头皮外伤或感染；
5. 无身体残疾；
6. 近2个月内无染发，实验当天不化妆，实验当天在家自行洗头；
7. 可以接受在头发头皮上涂抹特质的导电膏体（实验室配备专门的洗头房，供您实验结束之后洗净吹干）；
8. 非心理学、语言学专业；
9. 右利手（写字、用筷子等习惯使用右手）；
10. 没有参加过此实验的相关实验（如果不确定可以联系主试确认：Miss WANG, 1155200974@link.cuhk.edu.hk)
报名链接
：https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_7PsFSB4SG9yxfN4
香港中文大学语言学及现代语言系
This research is endorsed by
Prof. CAI Zhenguang
zhenguangcai@cuhk.edu.hk
Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages
The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Hi there!
Ever wondered how does your brain read Chinese?
We’re recruiting
native Mandarin speakers
for an EEG experiment. The task is simple:
come to the lab and read some Chinese sentences
(silently—no reading aloud!). We’ll record your brainwaves to see how busy your brain gets when processing your native language.
Duration of the experiment
: The experiment duration is approximately 1.5 hours
Experiment content:
1) wearing EEG devices, reading some Chinese sentences and responding with keyboard keys; 2) filling out some questionnaires.
Experiment location
: Room G34, G/F, K.K. Leung Building, The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
The subject fee of
HK$120
will be paid via FPS at the end of the experiment.
Participants need to meet the
following requirements
:
1. male native Mandarin Chinese speaker, 18-25 years old;
2. have normal vision (after correction) and no eye discomfort such as dryness;
3. have normal hearing;
4. no brain injury, epilepsy or other neurological diseases, no scalp trauma or infection;
5. no physical disability;
6. no hair coloring in the last 2 months, no make-up on the day of the experiment, and washing hair at home by themselves on the day of the experiment;
7. can accept the application of special conductive paste on the hair scalp (the laboratory is equipped with a special hair washing room; participants can wash hair at the end of the experiment);
8. non-psychology/linguistics majors;
9. right-handed (writing, using chopsticks, etc.);
10. have not participated in the preparatory experiment for this experiment. If you are not sure, you can contact the experimenter to confirm: Miss WANG, 1155200974@link.cuhk.edu.hk
Enrolment link:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_7PsFSB4SG9yxfN4
Department of Linguistics and Modern Languages, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
This research is endorsed by

男性
，
18-25岁
，来自中国大陆，母语为汉语普通话；
2. 视力（矫正后）正常，无干涩等眼部不适；
3. 听力正常；
4. 无脑损伤、癫痫等神经类疾病，无头皮外伤或感染；
5. 无身体残疾；
6. 近2个月内无染发，实验当天不化妆，实验当天在家自行洗头；
7. 可以接受在头发头皮上涂抹特质的导电膏体（实验室配备专门的洗头房，供您实验结束之后洗净吹干）；

9. 右利手（写字、用筷子等习惯使用右手）；

zhenguangcai@cuhk.edu.hk

Hi there!
Ever wondered how does your brain read Chinese?
We’re recruiting
native Mandarin speakers
for an EEG experiment. The task is simple:
come to the lab and read some Chinese sentences
(silently—no reading aloud!). We’ll record your brainwaves to see how busy your brain gets when processing your native language.
Duration of the experiment
: The experiment duration is approximately 1.5 hours
Experiment content:
1) wearing EEG devices, reading some Chinese sentences and responding with keyboard keys; 2) filling out some questionnaires.
Experiment location
: Room G34, G/F, K.K. Leung Building, The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
The subject fee of
HK$120
will be paid via FPS at the end of the experiment.
Participants need to meet the
following requirements
:
1. male native Mandarin Chinese speaker, 18-25 years old;
2. have normal vision (after correction) and no eye discomfort such as dryness;
3. have normal hearing;
4. no brain injury, epilepsy or other neurological diseases, no scalp trauma or infection;
5. no physical disability;
6. no hair coloring in the last 2 months, no make-up on the day of the experiment, and washing hair at home by themselves on the day of the experiment;
7. can accept the application of special conductive paste on the hair scalp (the laboratory is equipped with a special hair washing room; participants can wash hair at the end of the experiment);
8. non-psychology/linguistics majors;
9. right-handed (writing, using chopsticks, etc.);
10. have not participated in the preparatory experiment for this experiment. If you are not sure, you can contact the experimenter to confirm: Miss WANG, 1155200974@link.cuhk.edu.hk

HIST2501GL    Hong Kong History in the Field
This course will introduce the history of Hong Kong by focusing on its “fields.” It will examine how various field sites such as temples, museums, historical trails, renovated historical buildings, and even internets could be used to understand the history of different places, events, and people in Hong Kong from the ancient period to the present.
⭐⭐⭐

From: Amber Lam

Experiencing Chinese Culture Series 2026-27 – Chinese Calligraphy Workshop (Elementary)
Date: 7, 14, 21 & 28 September; 5, 12 & 26 October, and 2, 9 & 23 November 2026 (Mondays; 10 lessons)
Time: 6:00 p.m. - 7:30 p.m.
Venue: Experiential Learning Space, 1/F, West Wing, Art Museum, CUHK
Language: Cantonese
Registration:
Click here
Enquiries: 3943 5976 /
ics-activities@cuhk.edu.hk
For details, please refer to the poster (Chinese version only).
活動簡介
：
本課程為中國書法基礎班，主要教授隸書，透過介紹和臨習漢魏隸書經典名碑，讓學員認識和掌握相關基本書寫技巧，了解中國書法的承傳與品鑒，建立基礎，加深對書法之認識，培養對中國文化之興趣。
導師簡介：
陳冠男博士，畢業於香港中文大學藝術系，現職中大文物館中國書畫主任（研究員），研究興趣為明清至近現代書畫。曾策劃多個展覽並編撰圖錄，最新近者是「香江藏珍——香港三大古書畫收藏」 （2025，與劉湘瀅合作）。其他曾參與撰寫之圖錄包括：《蓋蒂基金會贊助中國書畫在線圖錄》、「北山汲古系列：中國書法、中國繪畫、碑帖銘刻拓本」、《明畫全集．董其昌卷》等；另合編撰寫《丁衍庸書法》等專書。2018-19年度獲選為「利榮森紀念訪問學人」，任美國普林斯頓大學藝術與考古系唐氏東亞藝術中心及藝術博物館訪問學人。研究之餘也積極參與各種書畫展覽和比賽，並獲殊榮，作品為香港及海內外公私收藏。
日期：
2026年9月7、14、21、28日；10月5、12、26日；11月2、9及23日（逢星期一；共10堂）
時間
：晚上6時至 7時30分
地點
：香港中文大學文物館西翼一樓（藝術體驗空間）
對象
：香港中文大學學生、教職員及校友
名額：
16名
語言：
粵語
費用：
學費全免；材料工具費用港幣200元；按金港幣500元（須以支票繳付；出席八堂或以上，按金將獲全數發還）
報名方法：
填妥網上報名表格，經抽籤後
獲選學員將於2026年8月21日或之前收到通知
截止日期：2026年8月17日（星期一）
主辦機構：
香港中文大學中國文化研究所
支持單位：
香港中文大學文物館
活動贊助：
旭日慈善基金

Seminars / Forums / Programmes / Workshops
The Independent Learning Centre (ILC) offers a wide range of workshops and activities to support learning of language and communication skills. Visit our website for more information: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ (20260810)  - ILC
From: ILC
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
ilc-counsel@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
【Weekly Highlights - English Section 】
A. Communication, Study Skills and Job Preparation Workshops
The Independent Learning Centre offers English workshops 10 August to 14 August: (1) Listening to Learn: Academic Listening and Note-taking Skills, (2) Taking the IELTS Challenge: Reading & Writing, (3) Taking the IELTS Challenge: Speaking & Listening, (4) Job Preparation Series: Writing Impressive Application Letters, and (5) Building a Bigger and Better Vocabulary. These workshops are now available for registration at: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/workshops.aspx
B. Consultation Service in English
Consultation service is available during the following time:
10 August (Mon): 14:30 – 16:30
11 August (Tue): 10:30 – 12:30
12 August (Wed): 14:30 – 16:30
13 August (Thu): 10:30 – 12:30
14 August (Fri): 14:30 – 16:30
Online Booking:
https://ilccuhk.as.me/schedule.php
More Timeslot please check our website：
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EH/consultation.aspx
====================================
【Weekly Highlights - Chinese Section 】中文部本週活動
A. Chinese Workshops 中文工作坊
The Independent Learning Centre offers Chinese workshops 10 August to 14 August: (1) Academic Writing: An Initial Exploration of Using Generative AI (Cantonese), (2) JRE Argumentative Writing II, (3) CRE Vocabulary and the Use of Idioms, and (4) Self-learning Cantonese I. These workshops are now available for registration at: https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/workshops.aspx
自學中心八月十日至八月十四日舉辦 (1) 「天下之能事畢矣」——《易經》占筮簡介（粵）, (2) 學術寫作：使用生成式人工智能初探 (粵), (3) JRE 議論文寫作(II), (4) 「《易》道廣 大，無所不 包」——《易 經》解卦入門 （粵）, (5) 公務員綜合招聘試系列（CRE）：現代漢語詞匯與成語的運用, 及 (6) 自學粵語(一)等工作坊，歡迎報名。
登記連結： https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/workshops.aspx
B. Consultation Service in Chinese 自學中心中文輔導服務
Consultation service is available during the following time:
自學中心於八月十日至八月十四日提供以下中文輔導時段。
10 August (Mon): 10:30 – 12:30
11 August (Tue): 10:30 – 12:30
12 August (Wed): 14:30 – 16:30
13 August (Thu): 10:30 – 12:30 and 14:30 – 16:30
網上預約：
https://ilccuhk.as.me/schedule.php
更多中文輔導時段。
====================================
C. “The Power of Words” 「書寫力量」
This is a reading and writing event organized by the ILC, Hong Kong Literature Research Centre, the Office of Arts Administrator (OAA) and Tolopoem. Activities we have this semester include Blackboard / Glass Wall Poems, Talks of Dialogue in the Arts and Workshops.
自學中心、香港文學研究中心、藝術行政主任辦公室及吐露詩社合辦的大型閱讀及寫作活動。這個學期的活動，除黑板詩及玻璃詩外，還有藝文縱談及各式工作坊。各項活動的資料可以參看：https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/CH/Event/thepowerofwords.aspx
====================================
【Independent Online Learning Resources】自學中心網上自學資源
A. Independent Online Learning Resources in English
- Academic Writing
Visit this link on academic writing skills and convention for different citation styles:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/Writing_Writing.aspx
- Vocabulary
Visit this link for both General Vocabulary and Specific Vocabulary (e.g. For Business and Medical Professionals) lists and practices:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/Writing_Vocab.aspx
- Job Search and Interviews
Visit this link to identify your capabilities and personality types, learn how to prepare job search documents and personal statements, and how to get ready for job interviews:
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/ENResources/JobSearching.aspx
B. Independent Online Learning Resources in Chinese中文網上自學材料
- Academic Writing論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on academic writing, with highlights on structure, expressions, common grammatical mistakes, etc.
針對大學生撰寫學術論文時所遇到的困難，提供實用的知識和練習。內容包括：學期論文的結構與寫作步驟、常見語法錯誤、表達與語言邏輯等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/AWOnline/general1.html
- ‘Pulewang’ Online Putonghua Platform「普樂網」網上普通話平台
An online Putonghua learning platform designed for CU students. Essential knowledge of Putonghua is introduced with interactive exercises and games. Extended conversational exchanges on selected topics of social affairs and student life are available for oral practice with texts and pinyin.
針對本校同學學習需要的網上普通話平台，內容圍繞大學生的學習與日常生活，設計深入淺出，每單元均有練習與遊戲，互動有趣，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Chinese/plw/index.html
- Argumentative Writing議論文寫作
Visit this link for advice on the structure, the content and the language of argumentative writing.
介紹議論文的結構及寫作要求，以解說、例子及練習，呈現寫作議論時要注意的內容及語言特點：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/arguWriting/001.html
- Cantonese Pronunciation粵語拼音速遞
This guide is designed for mainland students as an effective way to learn Cantonese pronunciation. Basic knowledge of Cantonese syllables is introduced with exercises. Comparison of Cantonese and Putonghua pronunciation is also highlighted
協助內地同學迅速掌握粵語發音。內容包括：語音基礎、粵普對比、難點練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/cantontones/_home/index.html
- Cantonese Express港式粵語速遞
An interactive introduction to Hong Kong style Cantonese. Daily expressions and situational conversations are introduced with interactive exercises.
以有趣互動的方式介紹港式粵語，包括日常生活用語、情景會話、互動練習等，歡迎使用：http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/canton_express/others/frontpage.html
- Online Cantonese for Foreigners
A free online platform for international students to learn basic Cantonese. The texts are clear and simple, and interactive exercises easy to use: http://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/chinese/can_eng/layout.html
- Online Putonghua for Foreigners
Do you know how to make orders in a Chinese restaurant and learn how to bargain when you travel in China? Here are some situational conversations and basic knowledge of Putonghua to learn online: https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/EN/CHResources/Lang_PTH_EnglishSpk.aspx
- Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) 中國語言及文化自學資源網
Online Platform for Successful Chinese Learning (OPSCL) is a biliterate (English and Chinese) online platform that contains reviews of learning materials suitable for autodidactic study in the 5 big areas of Mandarin, Cantonese, Chinese Characters, Chinese Culture, and Hong Kong Culture. Electronic learning materials that is good for self-learning would be review. Each review consists of a description and other useful information. Users can search for resources by various criteria, rate the resources, and write their own comments. A self-assessment system is also provided so as to recommend an entry point to the users according to their current level.
中國語言及文化自學資源網(OPSCL)為一推薦自學資源之網上平台。平台為有意學習普通話、粵語、漢字、中國文化或香港文化等五大範疇的人士提供中文及英文雙語之學習資源，以推動自主學習與終身學習。平台內推薦的資源均附有簡介及評語，使用者可按自身需要搜尋學習資源，並在使用後給予評分或評論，以備其他使用者參考。此外，平台設有「自評系統」，使用者可通過完成自評，確定自身的學習起步點，從而尋找適合自己程度的學習資源。
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Workshop/ChineseLanguageAndCulture/EN/index.aspx
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Workshop/ChineseLanguageAndCulture/TC/index.aspx
https://www.ilc.cuhk.edu.hk/Workshop/ChineseLanguageAndCulture/SC/index.aspx
====================================
Contact us 聯絡我們
The Independent Learning Centre  自學中心
Address: Wu Chung Library, United College
Tel. No.：3943-8733 / 3943-8764
E-mail：ilc-counsel@cuhk.edu.hk
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.

From: Jephthah Cheung
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
lokcheung@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
近年醫學界發現，我們的腸道健康與大腦息息相關！原來「便秘」和「睡眠質素」的改變，可能是腦部退化的早期信號。為了深入了解這條神奇的「腸腦連線」，香港中文大學精神科學系睡眠研究組現正招募研究參加者。
研究對象:
年齡介乎 50 至 80 歲
關注腸道健康或者受便秘問題困擾（如排便困難、次數較少等）
沒有腦退化、精神疾病史
參加者需完成以下簡單程序：
填寫問卷 及 進行簡單面談
進行一次非入侵性睡眠檢測
記錄連續兩星期「大便日記」
進行一次結腸運輸試驗
收集一次大便樣本
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者最多可獲 HKD 500 超市禮券的津貼
如對本研究有興趣，請透過以下連結報名參加：
[網址連結:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eeTcY6hrKILNwhg
]
如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電 3919 7792 / 9568 9006 或 WhatsApp 9568 9006與負責研究人員聯絡、查詢詳情。謝謝
-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Recent research suggests that gut health is closely linked to brain function. Changes in bowel habits (e.g. constipation) and sleep quality may even be early signs of neurodegeneration.
To better understand this “gut–brain axis, we sincerely invite you to take part in our research study.
Who can join:
Aged 50–80
Concerned about gut health or bothered by constipation
No history of dementia or psychiatric disorders
What you will do:
Complete questionnaires and a brief interview
Undergo a sleep assessment
Record a 2-week bowel diary
Complete a colonic transit time test
Collect one stool sample
Incentive:
All assessments are free of charge.
Eligible participants may receive up to HKD 500 in supermarket vouchers upon completion.
Interested? Please sign up here:
[
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_eeTcY6hrKILNwhg
]

From: Yumi Sato
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
yumisato@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
Positive Support for Children with SEN and Trauma-Informed Seminar
This seminar aims to equip individuals who are interested in working in the social welfare or education sectors, or who wish to learn more about children and adolescents with Special Educational Needs (SEN). The focus will be on the learning needs of students with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and specific learning difficulties (SpLD).
Through a 2.5-hour practical training session, participants will gain an understanding of students’ strengths and weaknesses, and learn effective individualised support strategies through case studies. The seminar also integrates the six core principles of Trauma-Informed Care and applies positive education approaches, including the use of character strengths to build children’s sense of identity. It aims to create safe, caring, and inspiring learning environments while fostering psychological resilience in children.
The seminar will be delivered by experienced specialists in child clinical and developmental fields, combining theory and practice to help participants translate knowledge into actionable support strategies.
Participants who attend the full seminar will receive an electronic certificate, which will be sent to the email address registered in this form. Please check your inbox.
All
electronic attendance certificates
will be distributed by the
end of October
.
Target participants:Undergraduate and postgraduate students, teachers, social workers, and counsellors who are interested in supporting children and adolescents with Special Educational Needs (SEN)

Dr Chan Fung Ying
, Honorary Clinical Associate Professor, Department of Paediatrics, The Chinese University of Hong Kong
Mr Remus Kwok
, Honorary Advisor, Positive Education Research Laboratory, Department of Social and Behavioural Sciences, The City University of Hong Kong
Ms Helen Kwok
, Senior Lecturer, Department of Counselling and Psychology, The Hong Kong Shue Yan University; Registered Counselling Psychologist, Counselling and Research Centre

Understanding Children and Adolescents with SEN
- Dr Chan Fung Ying
Types of learners and specific educational needs
The mission, passion, and skills of mentorship
Positive Education
- Mr Kwok Kai Chun
Using character strengths to build children's self-identity
Trauma-Informed Care
- Ms Kwok Sin Hang
Trauma-informed care: understanding and supporting neurodiverse children
Terms and Conditions:
Once registered, no changes can be made to the submitted information after the deadline. The electronic certificate cannot be amended.
Seminar details are subject to the latest announcement. The organising team reserves the right to make changes, which will be communicated via email or social media as soon as possible.
Places are limited and will generally be allocated on a first-come, first-served basis. Early registration is recommended.
In case of severe weather, if Tropical Cyclone Warning Signal No. 8 or above, or a Black Rainstorm Warning Signal is still in force within 3 hours before the seminar, the session will be cancelled. Arrangements for a replacement session will be announced separately. Participants should also consider their own safety, transportation, and local conditions when deciding whether to attend.
Should you have any questions, please feel free to contact Yumi via WhatsApp (6646 9614) or email (yumisato@cuhk.edu.hk).

【誠邀參與正向支援SEN兒童及創傷知情講座】
是次講座旨在裝備有志投身社福或教育界，或有興趣了解特殊教育需要（SEN）兒童及青少年的人士。內容聚焦自閉症（ASD）、專注力不足／過度活躍症（ADHD）及讀寫障礙（SpLD）學生的學習特性與支援需要。透過2.5小時的實用培訓，參加者將掌握學生的強弱項，並透過案例學習有效的個別化支援策略。講座同時結合創傷知情照顧（Trauma-Informed Care）創傷知情六大原則 及正向教育（positive education）運用性格強項建立孩子的自我形象，創造安全、關懷及具啟發性的學習環境，建立兒童的心理韌性。講座由資深兒童臨床及發展專家主講，結合理論與實務，協助學員將知識轉化為具體可行的支援策略。
完整參加講座，將獲電子證書一張，並以此表格所登記之電郵發送，請留意電郵信箱。

- 導師制的使命、熱情與技巧

香港中文大學兒科學系名譽臨床副教授兒童體智及行為發展科專科醫生陳鳳英醫生

Positive Support for Children with SEN and Trauma-Informed Seminar
This seminar aims to equip individuals who are interested in working in the social welfare or education sectors, or who wish to learn more about children and adolescents with Special Educational Needs (SEN). The focus will be on the learning needs of students with autism spectrum disorder (ASD), attention deficit hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), and specific learning difficulties (SpLD).
Through a 2.5-hour practical training session, participants will gain an understanding of students’ strengths and weaknesses, and learn effective individualised support strategies through case studies. The seminar also integrates the six core principles of Trauma-Informed Care and applies positive education approaches, including the use of character strengths to build children’s sense of identity. It aims to create safe, caring, and inspiring learning environments while fostering psychological resilience in children.
The seminar will be delivered by experienced specialists in child clinical and developmental fields, combining theory and practice to help participants translate knowledge into actionable support strategies.
Participants who attend the full seminar will receive an electronic certificate, which will be sent to the email address registered in this form. Please check your inbox.

「重塑榕樹凹：共創山海村落」—
地方營造大使招募
中文大學建築學院現正推動一項以「鄉郊地方營造（Rural Placemaking）」為核心的鄉村學堂及暑期工作坊，誠邀熱愛香港鄉郊文化、樂於親身參與實作的你，一同走進榕樹凹，參與村落景觀的復育與共創行動。
計劃期間，我們將邀請香港建造學院團隊擔任導師，帶領參加者學習傳統建造工藝及鄉郊實踐技術。參加者可自選出席一天或多天工作坊。若完成九天的工作坊後，參加者將獲頒由中文大學建築學院及香港建造學院簽發之服務證書，以作嘉許。
榕樹凹介紹：
榕樹凹位於新界東北端，於三百多年前開基立村，是一條歷史悠久的客家溫姓村落，村落鼎盛時期曾有逾三百名居民。由於地理位置接近邊境，榕樹凹在1980年代曾設有英軍軍營，留下了一段獨特而鮮為人知的歷史印記。雖然村落現已無人居住，但村民近年積極推動復村工作，透過修復祖屋、整理村史、舉辦村宴及傳統儀式，如籌辦麒麟隊；重建社群連結與文化記憶，展現出對深厚的鄉土感情與文化傳承精神。
****************************************
願景
共創鄉郊地方營造：以低碳修復與地方記憶，重塑山海景觀。
空間實作：以小型建設改善路徑與休憩空間。
感官敘事：將歷史轉化為具體的景觀導覽。
​共創行動：透過行動連結設計思考與鄉村振興。
****************************************
活動地點： 新界沙頭角榕樹凹村
****************************************
工作坊形式及階段:
鄉村導賞：認識榕樹凹村落歷史，了解鄉郊地方營造與文化地景。
物資收集：在山海與村落之間收集可用材料。
景觀實踐*：進行場地清理及空間建設實作，由香港建造學院導師帶領鄉村學堂，教授鄉郊景觀實踐技藝與傳統建造方法。
（ *
代表當日將由建造學院導師帶領鄉村學堂及景觀實踐活動。）
8
月
11日（二）、17日（一）*、18日（二） *、25日（二）
9月
1日（二）、8日（二）、15日（二）、22日（二）
實際工作坊日期將視乎報名人數、天氣及工作人員情況作適當調整，包括增加或減少工作坊次數，屈時會通知相關參加者及在宣傳平台上公布。
- 參加者可因應自身時間安排，選擇參與單日或多日工作坊。
- 請參加者選擇所有可出席日期，以便主辦單位安排及分組。
- 導賞活動日期將稍後公布，會安排在平日和假日或工作坊期間舉行。

*************************************

名額：每節12人。
*************************************
對象：

****************************************
計劃名稱：

備註：
1. 榕樹凹屬禁區範圍，參加者需預先申請禁區許可證方可前往。
2. 在項目進行期間，所有與工作坊相關的船程費用將由計劃負責安排及資助。參加者需要自行安排陸路交通，並準備足夠食物（午餐）和飲用水。

“Reimagining Yung Shue Au: Co-creating a Mountain-Sea Village”
— Recruitment for Rural-placemaking Ambassadors
Re-telling the Yung Shue Au Story: Co-creating Rural Place
The School of Architecture at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently organising a rural school and summer workshop centred on the concept of
rural placemaking
. We invite individuals who are passionate about Hong Kong’s rural culture and interested in hands-on practice to join us in Yung Shue Au and participate in the revitalisation and co-creation of the village landscape.
During the programme, instructors from the Hong Kong Institute of Construction will lead participants in learning traditional construction crafts and rural practical skills. Participants may choose to attend one or multiple workshop sessions according to their availability. Those who complete nine workshop days will receive a service certificate jointly issued by the School of Architecture, CUHK and the Hong Kong Institute of Construction in recognition of their participation and contribution.
Introduction to Yung Shue Au
Located in the northeastern New Territories, Yung Shue Au is a historic Hakka village established over 300 years ago by the Wan clan. At its peak, the village was home to more than 300 residents. Owing to its proximity to the border, a British military camp was stationed in the village during the 1980s, leaving behind a unique yet little-known historical legacy.
Although the village is currently uninhabited, villagers have actively promoted village revitalisation in recent years through repairing ancestral houses, documenting village history, organising village banquets and traditional rituals, as well as reviving the Qilin dance team. These efforts reflect a deep attachment to the village and a strong commitment to cultural inheritance and community reconnection.
Vision
Co-creating Rural Placemaking
Reimagining the mountain-sea landscape through low-carbon restoration and local memories.
Spatial Practice
Improving pathways and communal resting spaces through small-scale construction.
Sensory Narratives
Transforming local history into tangible landscape interpretation experiences.
Collective Action
Connecting design thinking with rural revitalisation through practical engagement.
Venue:
Yung Shue Au, Sha Tau Kok, New Territories
Programme Format and Phases
Village Guided Tour
Understanding the history of Yung Shue Au and learning about rural placemaking and cultural landscapes.
Material Collection
Collecting usable materials from the surrounding mountain, coastal, and village environment.
Landscape Practice
Participating in site clearing and spatial construction workshops led by instructors from the Hong Kong Institute of Construction, focusing on rural landscape practices and traditional building techniques.
(* Stars indicate days when Hong Kong Institute of Construction instructors will lead the Landscape workshop.)
August to September
11 August (Tue), 17 August (Mon)*, 18 August (Tue)*, 25 August (Tue)
September
1 September (Tue), 8 August (Tue), 15 August (Tue), 22 August (Tue)
Please note that actual workshop dates are subject to adjustment based on enrollment numbers, weather conditions, and staff availability. This includes the potential to increase or decrease the number of sessions. “Reimagining Yung Shue Au: Co-creating a Mountain-Sea Village”
— Recruitment for Rural-placemaking Ambassadors
Re-telling the Yung Shue Au Story: Co-creating Rural Place
The School of Architecture at The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently organising a rural school and summer workshop centred on the concept of
rural placemaking
. We invite individuals who are passionate about Hong Kong’s rural culture and interested in hands-on practice to join us in Yung Shue Au and participate in the revitalisation and co-creation of the village landscape.
During the programme, instructors from the Hong Kong Institute of Construction will lead participants in learning traditional construction crafts and rural practical skills. Participants may choose to attend one or multiple workshop sessions according to their availability. Those who complete nine workshop days will receive a service certificate jointly issued by the School of Architecture, CUHK and the Hong Kong Institute of Construction in recognition of their participation and contribution.
Introduction to Yung Shue Au
Located in the northeastern New Territories, Yung Shue Au is a historic Hakka village established over 300 years ago by the Wan clan. At its peak, the village was home to more than 300 residents. Owing to its proximity to the border, a British military camp was stationed in the village during the 1980s, leaving behind a unique yet little-known historical legacy.
Although the village is currently uninhabited, villagers have actively promoted village revitalisation in recent years through repairing ancestral houses, documenting village history, organising village banquets and traditional rituals, as well as reviving the Qilin dance team. These efforts reflect a deep attachment to the village and a strong commitment to cultural inheritance and community reconnection.
Vision
Co-creating Rural Placemaking
Reimagining the mountain-sea landscape through low-carbon restoration and local memories.
Spatial Practice
Improving pathways and communal resting spaces through small-scale construction.
Sensory Narratives

Collective Action
Connecting design thinking with rural revitalisation through practical engagement.

Participating in site clearing and spatial construction workshops led by instructors from the Hong Kong Institute of Construction, focusing on rural landscape practices and traditional building techniques.

CLCP4793 – Special Topics in Putonghua (Medicine & Healthcare): Master Putonghua for Medical Settings!  CLCP4793 普通話專題科（醫學）：掌握醫療場景下的普通話溝通技巧！ - Yale-China Chinese Language Academy
From: Yale-China Chinese Language Academy

- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
“探热”普通話點講啊？“吊鹽水“呢？普通話“體檢”原來係指“驗身”！想知多啲同醫療健康相關嘅普通話詞彙？又想改善下同內地醫護人員或者病人溝通果陣時嘅表達？咁就快啲來報名修讀CLCP4793喇！
CLCP4793 是一門高級普通話課程，課程通過模擬真實醫療語境，豐富學生的醫療及健康相關詞彙，提升學生在該領域的普通話溝通能力。對醫療場景下的普通話使用或相關話題感興趣的所有同學都可以報名修讀！

課程特色：
聚焦醫療與健康主題，提升醫療場景下的普通話表達能力
角色扮演模擬多個專科診症場景：呼吸科、消化科、心臟科、內分泌科、骨科等
邀請醫療從業者及中大醫學院教授參與分享及指導
藉助Micro-Modules 輔助學習，介紹內地醫療制度、醫學生培訓等

適合對象： 醫學院學生及對相關話題感興趣的所有中大學生
註冊方式： CUSIS
查詢： cla_upd@cuhk.edu.hk / 3943-822
Ever wondered how to say “fever check” or “IV drip” in Putonghua?
If you're curious about medical-related Putonghua vocabulary or want to improve your communication with healthcare professionals or patients from Mainland China, this course is for you!
CLCP4793
is an advanced Putonghua course designed to enrich students’ vocabulary and communication skills in medical and healthcare contexts. All CUHK students interested in the use of Putonghua in medical settings or related topics are welcome to enroll—no medical background required!

Course Highlights:
Focus on healthcare and medical topics to enhance Putonghua communication in medical settings
Role-play simulations of specialist consultations: pulmonology, gastroenterology, cardiology, endocrinology, orthopedics, etc.
Guest sharing and guidance from medical professionals and Faculty of Medicine of CUHK
Supplementary Micro-Modules introducing Mainland China’s healthcare system, medical education, and more

Who Should Join:
CUHK medical students and any students interested in medical Putonghua or healthcare-related topics

CUSIS

Interested in healthcare and want to communicate better in Cantonese?
CLCC1903 is a beginner-level course open to all CUHK students who wish to explore medical Cantonese in real-life clinical contexts. Whether you're studying medicine, social work, or just curious about healthcare communication, this course will equip you with the essential language skills to engage with patients and professionals in Cantonese.

What You’ll Learn:
Basic medical vocabulary and sentence structures
Cantonese for appointments, check-ups, emergencies, surgery, psychiatry, and more
Interactive tasks and contextual exercises based on daily clinical settings

Learning Outcomes:
Ask and respond to simple questions in Cantonese
Use selected vocabulary and grammar in everyday medical conversations
Communicate effectively in basic healthcare interactions

Format & Assessment:
3-hour face-to-face lectures
Presentation (30%) | Participation (20%) | Test/Quiz (50%)

Open to:
All CUHK students with little or no Cantonese background who are interested in healthcare communication

Registration:
CUSIS

Enquiries:
cla_upd@cuhk.edu.hk / 3943-8224
對醫療健康有興趣？想提升你在粵語環境下的溝通能力？
CLCC1903 是一門初階醫學粵語課程，歡迎所有中大學生選修。無論你是否修讀醫科、社工，或只是對醫療溝通有興趣，這門課都能幫助你掌握基本醫療粵語，與病人及醫護人員有效互動。

你將學到：
醫療常用詞彙與句型
預約、檢查、急症、手術、精神科等場景的粵語表達
結合臨床情境的互動練習與語言任務

學習成果：
能以粵語進行簡單問答
運用所學詞彙與語法進行日常醫療溝通
在基礎醫療互動中表達清晰、得體

授課模式與評核：
面授課堂（3小時）
簡報（30%）| 課堂參與（20%）| 測驗／小測（50%）

適合對象：
所有中大學生，尤其是對醫療溝通有興趣、但缺乏粵語基礎的同學

CLCP3702 is a 2-credit course offered starting from Term 1, 2022-23. This course is designed for native speakers of Cantonese who are interested in films. The course introduces students to popular films in Putonghua and film critique. Students will discuss the selected movies with their peers and introduce other movies with similar or contrasting themes and motifs.
Course topics include:
1. Characteristics of Putonghua used in movies
2. Features of Putonghua used in dubbed films
3. Putonghua used in HK-produced movies

CLCC1152 is a 2-credit course offered in Term 1, 2026-27. This course is designed for international students and Putonghua-speaking students.
Course description:
This course introduces the phonetic system of Cantonese. Supported by audiovisual aids, students will understand the sound of the vowels and consonants, the pronunciation rules, and the intonations in casual conversations and in reading literature. The articulation of some Cantonese sounds that needs attention for second language learners will also be examined. Through interactive classroom learning activities, students' accuracy of Cantonese pronunciation will be enhanced.
Medium of instruction:
Cantonese and English
Registration:
Students are required to submit the “Course Add/Drop Form for Undergraduate Course” to CLA
More details:
Available on the CUSIS timetable

CLCC1152是2026-27年第一學期開設的兩學分科目，為國際生及母語為普通話的學生而設。
科目描述：
本科目介紹粵語的語音系統，在視聽教材的幫助下，學生將了解元音和輔音的發音、發音規則以及在對話和閱讀文學作品中的語調。科目亦會探討第二語言學習者需要注意的粵語語音，並通過互動課堂學習活動，提高學生粵語發音的準確性。

Announcements
Free HPV Screening for Men in Specific Groups [Free!!] !!!注意: 男性特定群組 HPV 病毒篩查   [費用全免] [$400交通津貼] - Department of Surgery
From: Tim Lau
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學泌尿外科研究招募
:
香港中文大學泌尿外科現正進行一項男性特定群體的尿液及生物樣本HPV和病例對照研究。人類乳頭瘤病毒（HPV） 是全球最常見的性傳染病毒之一，能影響男性並導致多種疾病，包括生殖器疣（椰菜花）、陰莖癌、肛門癌 及 口咽癌。然而，男性 HPV 的感染情況一直缺乏研究，而你的參與將有助填補這個重要的知識空白。
本研究旨在了解HPV感染率、患者人口統計特徵、臨床特徵以及被診斷患有HPV相關惡性腫瘤的男性患者的疾病負擔。以評估男性尿液 HPV 測試的準確性，並更深入了解男性感染 HPV的風險因素，以及幫助未來預防及治療策略。
-如初步檢測確診為HPV陽性的患者，或將安排進一步行檢查 (例如:軟式膀胱鏡檢查等等)及跟進複檢。
參加者條件（男性，18歲或以上）：
1) 陰莖癌，肛⾨癌，或咽喉癌患者
2) 曾患性傳染病
3) 曾有同性性⾏為
4) 慢性前列腺炎患者
地點：沙⽥威爾斯親王醫院
樣本收集： 尿液及尿道拭子、口咽拭子、肛門拭子、冠狀溝拭子
-填寫簡單問卷
-根據情況也可能採集 20 毫升血液
[費用全免]
-完成整個研究計劃後可獲得港幣
$400
津貼
參加者的資料將會以專業方式絕對保密!!
所收集的資料僅用於學術研究用途
名額有限，先到先得!
閣下如對本研究有興趣請透過以下連結報名：
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf__iQ0Ike8hpG6qIm1mjtF0nCTdcPFKT2v9jFARsuZbqjMJw/viewform?usp=header
-如果評估合適參與研究，將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如有查詢，歡迎電郵: timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk，與研究人員劉先生聯絡。
________________________________________________________________________
Free HPV Screening for Men in Specific Groups [Free!!]
The Chinese University of Hong Kong Division of Urology Research Recruitment
The Department of Surgery (Urology), The Chinese University of Hong Kong is currently recruiting participants for a hybrid cohort and case-control study on male urinary HPV.
Human Papillomavirus (HPV) is one of the most common sexually transmitted viruses worldwide. It can affect men and lead to serious conditions including genital warts, penile cancer, anal cancer, and oropharyngeal cancer. However, HPV infection in men remains under-studied. Your cooperation is highly solicited.
This research aims to determine HPV prevalence, patient demographics, clinical characteristics, and disease burden in men. It will also evaluate the accuracy of a new urine-based HPV DNA test and explore risk factors to support future prevention and treatment strategies.
Participants who test positive for HPV in the initial urine test may be invited for further investigations (e.g. flexible cystoscopy) and regular follow-up re-testing.
Eligibility (Males aged 18 or above)
Patients diagnosed with penile cancer, anal cancer, or oropharyngeal cancer
Men with a history of sexually transmitted diseases (STD)
Men who have sex with men (MSM)
Patients with chronic prostatitis / chronic pelvic pain syndrome (CPPS)
Study Location: Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin
Narrative description
Urine sample + swabs (urethral, oropharyngeal, anal, coronal sulcus)
Complete a simple questionnaire
Optional: 20 ml blood sample (if required)
Free of Charge in HPV test !!
Upon successful completion of the study, participants will receive a
HKD 400
travel subsidy
Your Privacy is Fully Protected.
Data will only be used for academic research purposes.
If you are interested, please register via the link below:
https://docs.google.com/forms/d/e/1FAIpQLSf__iQ0Ike8hpG6qIm1mjtF0nCTdcPFKT2v9jFARsuZbqjMJw/viewform?usp=header
Suitable applicants will be contacted shortly.
For inquiries, please email:  timlau@surgery.cuhk.edu.hk
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

bodyText:

2026/08/07

Announcements
【 $250 Coupon 】Recruiting Children (aged 11 or under) for the Gut Microbiome and Children's Emotional Health Development Study 誠意邀請11歲或以下兒童參加腸道微生物及兒童心智發展的研究-Department of Psychiatry.  - Department of Psychiatry
From: Dr. WONG Wing Ho, Oscar
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
oscarwhwong@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
家長您好，我們是香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系的研究團隊。本研究由香港中文大學醫學院精神科學系、內科及藥物治療學系統籌。
本研究團隊誠邀5歲以下兒童參與一項有關腸道微生態與兒童大腦發展及風險研究。此研究希望透過收集小朋友之大便及口腔樣本，幫助了解腸道微生態與大腦發展的關係。
研究對象:
1) 確診/懷疑小朋友有自閉症傾向或其他發展問題
2) 4歲或以下的小朋友 (交齊問卷和樣本的日子未滿5歲即可)
3) 父母皆為華裔或亞裔人士
4) 小朋友18歲以下的兄弟姊妹
以下為是次研究需要完成的事項：
1) 簽署參加同意書
2) 網上問卷調查：網上問卷主要詢問小朋友的行為及腸道情況，填寫時間約45分鐘
3) 收集大便和口腔樣本：我們會給家長一個樣本收集包，請家長使用收集包內的物在家中資協助收集樣本
4) 飲食習慣的問卷：記錄小朋友的飲食習慣
完成研究後，參加者可以獲得$200的超市現金券、 G-NiiB益生菌試用裝和腸道健康報告作為答謝 另外，家長有機會被邀請進行面談並隨訪2年,如有需要我們會提供轉介信。是次研究是自願參與性質參與，這個研究期間所取得的資料都會被嚴格保密。
如家長有意願參與此項研究，請填寫以下網上篩選問卷(https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_81kdBVoLu4f6l3o)。收到問卷回覆後，我們會再與合適參加是次研究的小朋友之家長連絡。
如果家長對研究細節有任何疑問，歡迎透過WhatsApp 6099-3064或致電 2607-6057與我們聯絡。
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
Dear Parents,
We are a team of researchers from the Department of Psychiatry at the Chinese University of Hong Kong. We are conducting a research project jointly organised by the Department of Psychiatry, the Department of Medicine and Therapeutics of the Chinese University of Hong Kong.
Our team sincerely invites your children to participate in research on gut microbiome and children's brain development. Through collecting stool and buccal samples, we aim to investigate the relationship between gut microbiome and brain development.
A gut health report will be provided, A G-Niib probiotics trial pack and a $200 supermarket voucher will be awarded to participants.
Target participants:
1) The child is diagnosed/suspected to have autism or other developmental problems
2) The child is 4 years old or under (all questionnaires and samples are submitted before 5 years old)
3) Both parents are Chinese or Asian
4) Children’s brothers and sisters under 18 years old are also welcome to join
Procedures and details of this Study:
1) Research Consent
2) Online Questionnaire : A 45-minute questionnaire on children’s behaviors and their physical health condition

Announcements
(Earn $700!!!) Recruiting adults aged 18–65 who have recovered from depression to participate in a study on depression recurrence (participants on medication are welcome if condition is medically stable) (獲得 $700!!!) 誠邀年齡介乎18歲至65歲的抑鬱症康復者參與預測抑鬱症復發相關的研究(歡迎仍在服藥但病情穩定者參加) - Department of Psychiatry
From: Phoebe Chan
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學精神科學系正進行一項研究，探討運用語音分析能否預測抑鬱症復發。現招募年齡介乎18歲至65歲的抑鬱症康復者參與研究。詳情如下：
我們誠邀符合以下條件的人士參與本次研究：
18歲至65歲的抑鬱症康復者
廣東話為母語
使用智慧型手機並可持續連接互聯網
接受本研究所使用的即時通訊應用程式的服務條款和隱私權政策
您需要做什麼？
接受臨床評估作為篩查
填寫問卷
連續
7
天
於指定的手機應用程式以語音方式記錄情緒狀態
一年後接受跟進臨床評估
完成整個實驗及跟進評估，可以獲得最多HK$700作為研究津貼
如有興趣參與研究，請按以下連結填寫篩選問卷。
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_e9b0QXbpcuCUxrE
若您適合參與研究，研究人員會聯絡您解釋研究詳情。
閣下留下的資料僅供研究用途，絕對保密。如閣下對是項研究有任何查詢，請電郵
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
或 WhatsApp:(+852- 53202853)。
If you are interested, please complete the following screening questionnaire.
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_e9b0QXbpcuCUxrE
If you are suitable for participating in the study, the researchers will contact you to explain the study details.
Information collected will be only used for research purposes and will be kept strictly confidential. If you have any enquiries, please contact us via email
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
or WhatsApp: (+852-53202853).

Announcements
AI and Music!! Recruiting Young Music Lovers | AI and Popular Song Emotion Categorization Research AI and Music!!招募音樂愛好青年｜人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究 - Department of Psychiatry
From: Xiuyang Meng
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
mastersleep@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
招募音樂愛好青年｜人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究
我們正在尋找熱愛音樂的你，參與人工智能與流行歌曲情緒分類研究，用你的聽感為 AI 模型注入真實的青年情緒視角。
研究目的
本研究旨在運用人工智能技術，從青年視角對粵語流行歌曲進行情緒分類標註，評估青年群體對音樂情緒的主觀感知特徵，並為個性化音樂推薦系統及情緒調節相關研究提供數據支持。
招募條件
18 至 24 歲，熱愛音樂且經常聆聽流行音樂，能流暢使用粵語及英語進行溝通與表達的青年。
參與內容
聆聽 50 首粵語流行歌曲，並完整聽畢每首參與標註的曲目，依據自身主觀體驗與即時情緒感受，將歌曲進行情緒分類。
如何加入？
請點擊以下連結進行註冊，並回答幾條簡單問題。研究員將聯絡適合的參加者，詳細解釋研究內容：
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5pU67FrIxYilalw
聯絡我們
如有任何疑問，請於辦公時間內致電 6115-0322 與研究助理陳小姐 或 蒙先生聯絡。
Recruiting Young Music Lovers | AI and Popular Song Emotion Categorization Research
We are looking for music lovers like you to participate in our research on AI and popular song emotion categorization, contributing your listening experience to inject authentic youth emotional perspectives into our AI model.
Purpose of the Study
This study aims to use artificial intelligence technology to annotate the emotion categories of Cantopop songs from a youth perspective, evaluate the subjective emotional perception characteristics of young people towards music, and provide data support for personalized music recommendation systems and emotion regulation-related research.
Eligibility Criteria
Young people aged 18 to 24 who love music, listen to popular music regularly, and are able to communicate fluently in Cantonese and English.
Participation Content
Listen to 50 Cantopop songs in full, and categorize each song according to your subjective experience and immediate emotional feelings.
How to Join?
Please click the link below to register and answer a few simple questions. Our researchers will contact eligible participants to explain the study details in full:
https://cuhk.qualtrics.com/jfe/form/SV_5pU67FrIxYilalw
Contact Us
If you have any questions, please call 6115-0322 during office hours to speak with our research assistants Ms. Chan or Mr. Meng.
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
Copyright © 2013. All Rights Reserved. The Chinese University of Hong Kong.
/weekly/

  [Online experiment] Looking for native English speakers
Prof. Haerim Hwang (Department of English, CUHK) is looking for participants for a study on language production.
Which participants are we looking for?
- English is your first/native and dominant language
- Your graduate degree is not in the field of linguistics
- Can use your laptop/computer and have access to stable internet (no smartphones, laptops, or hotspot)
- Can participate in an experiment on Zoom in a quiet environment
- Have Chrome on your laptop/computer
How do I participate?
1. Fill out this questionnaire
-- English speakers: https://forms.gle/ttuhGGCwRx2n95kBA
2. Our research team will reach out to you, confirming your availability.
3. It will take approximately 2 hours to complete these tasks.
What do I get out of the study?
You will get HK$250 in cash upon the completion of the task.
Your participation will enhance our understanding of how people process English sentences.
Questions?
Contact Prof. Haerim Hwang at haerimhwang@cuhk.edu.hk
Ethics Approval
The Chinese University of Hong Kong Survey and Behavioural Research Ethics Committee SBREC (fssc02@cuhk.edu.hk) has vetted the study (Approval ID: SBRE-22-0026D). If you have any concerns regarding ethics, please contact them.

Announcements
~Recruiting vocally healthy participants aged 18 and above to participate in an acoustic analysis study to explore the quality and characteristics of the voice (HK$150 coupon) 誠意邀請18歲或以上沒有聲線障礙的人士參與探索聲線質量和特徵的聲學分析研究 (HK$150 coupon) - Department of Otorhinolarynogology, Head and Neck Surgery
From: Rina To
For comments and enquiries related to this message, please send to
rinato@cuhk.edu.hk
- - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -
香港中文大學耳鼻咽喉 頭頸外科學系現正招募十八歲或以上沒有聲線障礙的人士參與一項聲學分析的研究，旨在探究平滑化倒頻譜突出峰值 (CPPS) 的臨界值和其診斷準確性。
CPPS是一種可應用於日常對話的聲線聲學分析參數。CPPS相對於其他常用的聲學參數具有更高的診斷準確性。但是，根據文獻的報告顯示，使用不同的語言，聲線樣本類型，和軟件，都會影響到CPPS的結果。我們希望這項研究的結果能夠為臨床醫生和研究人員對聲線障礙患者進行客觀測量並為聲線評估的量化結果提供明確的參考。
招募對象：
年滿十八歲或以上
沒有聲線問題的人士
以廣東話為母語
費用：全免
評估與檢查地點：威爾斯親王醫院
研究程序及内容：
1）參加者將填寫聲線問卷， 並親臨威爾斯親王醫院接受喉纖維內視鏡檢查和聲線錄製。
2）喉纖維內視鏡檢查時能清楚看見咽喉，每次檢查需時約三十分鐘，是屬於低風險的檢查，一般只會感到輕微不適。
報名連結﹕
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=4267989
參與研究，獲得獎勵：
完成聲線評估後，您可獲得港幣150元的超市現金券。
名額有限，先到先得。收到報名後，我們會再與合資格的參加者聯絡。
歡迎將此招募信息推薦給身邊有需要的家人以及朋友。
如有查詢，請與研究人員王先生（Mr. Wang）聯絡。
電郵：
zikaiwang@link.cuhk.edu.hk
The Department of Otorhinolaryngology, Head and Neck Surgery, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, is currently recruiting vocally healthy participants aged 18 and above for a study investigating the cut-off score and diagnostic accuracy of the smoothed cepstral peak prominence (CPPS) for Cantonese speakers with dysphonia.
CPPS is a parameter for acoustic analysis of voice that can be used in everyday conversation to provide a more comprehensive and realistic picture of an individual's vocal characteristics in natural communication situations. CPPS has a higher diagnostic accuracy than other commonly used acoustic parameters. However, reports in the literature indicate that the use of different languages, different types of voice samples, and different software can affect the results of the CPPS. We hope that the results of this study will provide clinicians and researchers with a clear reference for the quantitative results of objective measurement and voice assessment in patients with voice disorders.
Recruitment target:
Age 18 or above
People who do not have voice problems
Fluent in Cantonese as a native language or proficient in Cantonese
Cost: Free of charge
Location: Prince of Wales Hospital
Procedures and details of this Study:
Participants will undergo a laryngeal videostroboscopy examination and a comprehensive voice assessment at Prince of Wales Hospital.
A videostroboscopy examination can clearly observe the throat to detect whether it has structural or functional problem for speaking. Each examination takes approximately thirty minutes. It is a low-risk procedure, and participants typically only experience mild discomfort.
Registration link:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=4267989
Participate in the study and receive a reward:
After completing the voice assessment, you will receive a HK$ 150 supermarket gift card.
Limited seats available on a first-come first-served basis. We will contact you afterwards if you are suitable to join this study.
Welcome to recommend this recruitment information to your family and friends in need.
If you have any inquiries, please contact Mr. Wang.
Email:
zikaiwang@link.cuhk.edu.hk
View Count
For request submissions, please submit them at
https://cumassmail.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk
For enquiries, please write to:
http://servicedesk.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk

2

β
細胞功能和胰島素抵抗的影響】
香港中文大學內科及藥物治療學系與香港中文大學香港中西醫結合醫學研究所現正聯合進行一項為期36週，以內服中藥(沖劑)治療 2 型糖尿病人
 研究對象：18至70歲華人
沒有重大疾病，沒有服用中藥， 身體質量指數 (BMI) ≥18 kg/m²  (公斤 ÷ 米 ÷ 米)
不吸煙或已戒煙至少 12 個月，如女性目前未懷孕
患糖尿病未滿 6 年，且在過去 3 個月內未使用任何降血糖藥物（包括胰島素）治療
至少具備以下其中一項風險因素:
糖尿病家族史 (尤其父母或兄弟姐妹在40歲前診斷 )
代謝綜合症 (3高：高血糖，高血壓，高膽固醇)
超重或肥胖
脂肪肝
多囊卵巢綜合症
妊娠糖尿病病史
如不確定自己是否患有糖尿病，會安排你服用葡萄糖飲料（75 克口服葡萄糖耐量試驗）
研究內容：中西醫評估、心電圖、肝纖維化掃描、抽血檢查、填寫問卷、服用研究中藥或安慰劑等
地點：新界沙田威爾斯醫院，舊座，3 樓，3M 病房 - 糖尿及內分泌研究中心
參與研究費用全免，成功參與者可獲得高達港幣 $1,000 的津貼，名額有限，先到先得！

如果初步合適參與研究，負責同事將稍後聯絡你，謝謝
如對研究內容有任何疑問，歡迎致電  3505 3897 / 6937 3365 或 WhatsApp 6937 3365與負責研究人員聯絡、查詢詳情。
[Clinical safety, efficacy and multiomic evaluation of a novel Chinese Medicine formula in Type 2 diabetes: Effects on beta-cell function and insulin resistance
.]
Department of Medicine and Therapeutics and Hong Kong Institute of Integrative Medicine, CUHK are jointly conducting a 36-week clinical study on the use of oral traditional Chinese medicine (granule form) for treating type 2 diabetes.
Eligibility Criteria: Ethnic Chinese individuals aged 18 to 70 years
No major illnesses, not currently taking any traditional Chinese medicine, and with a Body Mass Index (BMI) ≥ 18 kg/m² (kg ÷ metre ÷ metre)
Non-smokers or those who have quit smoking for at least 12 months; females must not be currently pregnant
Diagnosed with type 2 diabetes for less than 6 years and have not used any glucose-lowering medications (including insulin) in the past 3 months
Must have at least one of the following risk factors:
Family history of diabetes (especially if parents or siblings were diagnosed before age of 40)
Metabolic syndrome (three highs: high blood sugar, high blood pressure, high blood cholesterol)
Overweight or obesity
Fatty liver
Polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)
History of gestational diabetes
If you are unsure whether you have diabetes, a 75g oral glucose tolerance test (OGTT) will be arranged for you.

Study Procedures Include:
Chinese and Western medical assessments, Electrocardiogram (ECG), Liver fibrosis scan, Blood tests, Questionnaire completion, Taking either the study Chinese medicine or a placebo
Location: Ward 3M, 3/F, Old Block, Diabetes and Endocrinology Research Centre, Prince of Wales Hospital, Sha Tin, New Territories
Free of charge to participate.
Successful participants may receive an allowance of up to HKD $1,000.
Limited quota – first come, first served!
Register via the following link:
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/mycuform/view.php?id=3542692
If you are eligible based on initial assessment, our research team will contact you shortly. Thank you!
For inquiries, please contact:
3505 3897 / 6937 3365
WhatsApp: 6937 3365

To encourage CUHK teams to apply and to deepen their understanding of the Scheme, we will be holding a briefing session on 4 August 2026, during which awardees from previous cohorts will share their experiences and tips in a panel discussion.
We believe you will gain more insight and have a deeper understanding of the RAISe+ application after attending the briefing session, which will help you to better prepare your application for both CUHK registration and ITC application.
Details are listed as follows:
RAISe+ 4th Cohort Briefing Session
Date: 4 Aug 2026 (Tue)
Time: 09:30 AM - 11:30 AM
Venue: Room UGA, UG/F, InnoPort, CUHK
Registration Link: https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13737242
Registration Deadline: 2 Aug 2026 (Sun)
Submission of Application Form
If you are interested in applying for the CUHK RAISe+ Scheme 4th Solicitation Exercise, please fill in the following webform. For more details, please refer to our Website.
https://cloud.itsc.cuhk.edu.hk/webform/view.php?id=13735596
Late submissions will not be entertained under typical circumstances. We will review the applications received and select 15 teams for the official submission to ITC.
About RAISe+ Scheme
The Research, Academic and Industry Sectors One-plus (RAISe+) Scheme aims to help the prospective research teams with good potential to transform, realise and commercialise the research and development (“R&D”) outcomes and become successful start ups within around five years. For more details, please refer to ITC website, where you could find the funding guideline and application form template.
